skills.name: create-task-from-request
skills.description: Turn an incoming request or message into a well-formed Asana task in the right project with assignee and due date. Use for intake and ticket creation.
skills.content:
# Create Task from Request

Convert an incoming request into a structured Asana task.

## Steps
1. Extract the work to be done, the relevant project, an assignee if named, and any due date.
2. If the project is referenced by name, list projects to resolve its ID.
3. Create the task with a clear name, a description capturing the request details, the project, assignee, and due date.
4. Add a comment with any links or source context if helpful.

## Output
Report the created task name, its URL or ID, project, assignee, and due date.

skills.name: summarize-project-tasks
skills.description: Search tasks in an Asana project and summarize status, overdue items, and who owns what. Use for standups and project status checks.
skills.content:
# Summarize Project Tasks

Produce a status snapshot of an Asana project.

## Steps
1. Resolve the project, then search its tasks.
2. For each task capture name, assignee, due date, and completion state.
3. Group into completed, in progress, and overdue or due soon.
4. Note any unassigned tasks or tasks with no due date.

## Output
A concise status summary: counts per group, overdue tasks called out by name and owner, and any gaps to address.

skills.name: update-task-status
skills.description: Find an Asana task and update its fields — assignee, due date, completion, or add a progress comment. Use to keep tasks current from other systems.
skills.content:
# Update Task Status

Keep an Asana task in sync with the latest state.

## Steps
1. Identify the target task by ID, or search to find it by name.
2. Read the current task to confirm it is the right one.
3. Update the relevant fields — completion, assignee, or due date.
4. Add a comment summarizing what changed and why.

## Output
Report which fields changed and confirm the task ID. If no matching task was found, say so.

templates.title: Ashby pipeline digest
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled daily workflow that lists open Ashby jobs, summarizes candidate counts per stage, flags applications stalled for more than five days, logs metrics to a tracking table, and Slacks hiring managers a personalized pipeline digest.

templates.title: Resume to Ashby candidate
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches a folder of inbound resumes, extracts contact info and work history, deduplicates against existing Ashby candidates, creates new candidate records when needed, and tags them with the source job they applied through.

templates.title: Interview note logger
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs after every interview is logged in your meeting tool, summarizes the transcript, scores the candidate against the job requirements, creates a structured note on the matching Ashby candidate, and notifies the hiring manager in Slack.

templates.title: Stage-change responder
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that detects when an Ashby application moves into a new stage, sends the candidate a stage-appropriate email, prepares the interviewer brief in a file, and updates a recruiting tracking table so coordinators always know who is next.

templates.title: Ashby DEI snapshot
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled monthly workflow that pulls Ashby candidates, applications, and openings, computes funnel diversity metrics by stage, role, and source, and writes a confidential report file shared with people leadership and compliance.

templates.title: Candidate research enricher
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that takes new Ashby candidates, researches each across LinkedIn and the web for relevant background, writes a structured profile summary onto the candidate as an Ashby note, and updates a recruiting table with research links.

templates.title: Offer ready brief
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs when an Ashby application reaches the offer stage, gathers compensation benchmarks, interview feedback, and candidate priorities, drafts an offer brief file for the hiring manager, and Slacks the people team to start the offer process.

skills.name: add-candidate
skills.description: Create a candidate in Ashby from an inbound application or referral and attach them to a job. Use for sourcing and referral intake.
skills.content:
# Add Candidate

Capture a new candidate into Ashby and link them to the right role.

## Steps
1. Gather the candidate name, email, source, and the target job.
2. If the job is named, list jobs to resolve its ID.
3. Create the candidate, then create an application linking them to the job with the correct source.
4. Add a note with referral context or screening details, and apply any relevant tags.

## Output
Report the created candidate and application IDs, the linked job, and the source applied.

skills.name: advance-candidate-stage
skills.description: Move a candidate application to a new interview stage in Ashby and log the decision. Use to keep the pipeline moving after interviews.
skills.content:
# Advance Candidate Stage

Progress a candidate through the hiring pipeline.

## Steps
1. Find the application — by ID, or list applications for the candidate or job.
2. Confirm the current stage by getting the application.
3. Change the application stage to the target stage.
4. Add a note capturing the rationale and any interview feedback.

## Output
Confirm the candidate, the stage moved from and to, and the note added.

skills.name: pipeline-status-report
skills.description: List candidates and applications by status or job in Ashby and summarize pipeline health. Use for recruiting standups and weekly reports.
skills.content:
# Pipeline Status Report

Summarize the state of an Ashby hiring pipeline.

## Steps
1. List the relevant jobs, or focus on one role.
2. List applications, grouping candidates by current stage and status (active, hired, archived).
3. Flag candidates stalled in a stage or awaiting feedback.
4. Note new candidates added since the last report.

## Output
A pipeline summary: candidate counts per stage and status, stalled candidates called out by name and role, and recent additions.

templates.title: Athena scheduled report runner
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that runs a saved AWS Athena query daily, writes the result rows to a Sim table, and posts a Slack summary of the top movers.

templates.title: Athena S3 access audit
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs Athena queries against S3 access logs weekly, identifies unusual access patterns or new principals, and writes findings to a security audit table.

templates.title: Athena cost-explorer query
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that runs Athena queries against AWS cost-and-usage reports daily, writes top cost movers per service to a table, and posts an anomaly digest to Slack.

templates.title: Athena + Tinybird real-time bridge
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that combines historical Athena queries with realtime Tinybird endpoints into a unified reporting view, writes results to a dashboard table.

templates.title: Athena + PostHog data-warehouse join
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that joins PostHog event exports with Athena historical data, computes funnel conversion across the join, and writes a daily report.

templates.title: Athena ad-hoc query agent
templates.prompt: Build a Slack agent that translates natural-language analytics questions into safe AWS Athena queries, executes them, and returns the table answer with the query for review.

templates.title: Athena weekly executive metrics
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled weekly workflow that runs a set of AWS Athena queries against the data lake for revenue, retention, and usage metrics, writes the results to a metrics table, and emails a formatted scorecard to leadership.

templates.title: DynamoDB + Athena unified analytics
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that exports DynamoDB tables nightly into Athena-queryable Parquet, registers the schema, and writes a sample query for analyst use.

skills.name: run-query
skills.description: Run a SQL query against data in S3 via Athena, wait for completion, and return the results. Use for ad-hoc analysis and reporting over your data lake.
skills.content:
# Run Query

Execute a SQL query in Athena and return the results.

## Steps
1. Compose the SQL, naming the database and confirming the output location.
2. Start the query to obtain a query execution ID.
3. Poll get query execution until the state is SUCCEEDED, FAILED, or CANCELLED.
4. On success, fetch the query results and shape the rows into a clean table.

## Output
Return the result rows plus the execution ID, data scanned, and runtime. On failure, surface the Athena error message and the SQL that caused it.

skills.name: scheduled-metrics-report
skills.description: Run a saved or composed Athena query on a schedule to compute metrics and produce a report. Use for recurring KPI and usage reporting.
skills.content:
# Scheduled Metrics Report

Compute recurring metrics from data in S3.

## Steps
1. Use a named query, or compose the metrics SQL for the reporting period.
2. Start the query and poll execution until it completes.
3. Fetch the results and format the metrics for reporting.
4. Compare against the prior period to highlight movement where relevant.

## Output
A metrics summary with current values, period-over-period change, and the execution ID for traceability.

skills.name: manage-named-queries
skills.description: Create, look up, and list saved (named) queries in Athena to standardize reusable SQL. Use to maintain a library of vetted analytics queries.
skills.content:
# Manage Named Queries

Maintain a library of reusable Athena queries.

## Steps
1. To save a query, create a named query with a clear name, description, database, and the SQL body.
2. To reuse one, list named queries or get a named query by ID to retrieve its SQL.
3. Run the retrieved SQL via start query when execution is needed.
4. Keep names and descriptions accurate so the right query is easy to find.

## Output
Report the named query ID and name for creates, or the resolved SQL for lookups.

templates.title: Attio enrichment pipeline
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that watches new Attio records, enriches each contact with company size, funding, and tech stack via Apollo, and writes the enriched fields back to Attio.

templates.title: Attio deal pipeline tracker
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that mirrors Attio deals into a Sim table, calculates pipeline velocity per stage, and posts a daily Slack summary of deals at risk.

templates.title: Attio email-to-record logger
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that watches Gmail for emails to or from Attio contacts, logs each as an interaction on the matching record, and creates a follow-up task if mentioned.

templates.title: Attio call-summary updater
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that runs after a Fireflies sales call, summarizes the transcript into a deal-ready summary, and updates the matching Attio deal record.

templates.title: Attio win/loss analyzer
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled monthly workflow that pulls closed Attio deals, analyzes patterns in wins vs losses, and writes an insights report file for the sales team.

templates.title: Attio outreach orchestrator
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches Attio for contacts entering the outreach stage, drafts a personalized first-touch email, and queues it for the rep to review and send.

templates.title: Attio Slack channel-per-deal
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that for Attio deals above a threshold creates a Slack channel, invites the account team, and pins the deal record link.

skills.name: upsert-record
skills.description: Create or update a person, company, or deal record in Attio, matching on a key field to avoid duplicates. Use to sync external data into the CRM.
skills.content:
# Upsert Record

Keep an Attio record in sync without creating duplicates.

## Steps
1. Identify the target object (people, companies, or a custom object) and the matching attribute, such as email or domain.
2. Assemble the record values to set.
3. Use assert record to upsert on the matching attribute so an existing record is updated and a new one is created only when needed.
4. Verify the resulting record by getting it back.

## Output
Report whether the record was created or updated and its record ID.

skills.name: log-note-on-record
skills.description: Attach a note to an Attio record capturing a call, meeting, or update. Use to keep CRM context current after interactions.
skills.content:
# Log Note on Record

Record context against the right Attio record.

## Steps
1. Find the target record — by ID, or search records to locate it by name or domain.
2. Compose the note title and body summarizing the interaction or update.
3. Create the note on that record.
4. Optionally create a follow-up task if next steps were agreed.

## Output
Confirm the record the note was attached to and the note ID, plus any follow-up task created.

skills.name: create-followup-task
skills.description: Create a task in Attio linked to a record with an owner and due date. Use to capture follow-ups and next steps from deals or conversations.
skills.content:
# Create Follow-up Task

Turn a next step into a tracked Attio task.

## Steps
1. Identify the related record and the work to be done.
2. Determine the assignee and a due date.
3. Create the task with a clear description, linked record, owner, and deadline.
4. Confirm the task was created against the right record.

## Output
Report the created task ID, the linked record, assignee, and due date.

skills.name: manage-list-pipeline
skills.description: Query and update entries in an Attio list to move records through a pipeline or segment. Use for managing deal stages and curated segments.
skills.content:
# Manage List Pipeline

Move records through an Attio list-based pipeline.

## Steps
1. Resolve the target list, then query list entries to see current state.
2. Identify which entries need to change stage or attributes.
3. Create, update, or remove list entries as needed to reflect the new state.
4. Summarize the pipeline distribution after the changes.

## Output
Report which entries moved and their new stage, plus the resulting count of records per stage.

templates.title: AppConfig runtime config loader
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that retrieves the latest deployed AWS AppConfig configuration for a given application, environment, and profile, parses the JSON, and uses the feature flags to branch downstream agent behavior.

templates.title: AppConfig feature-flag publisher
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that takes a JSON feature-flag document, creates a new hosted configuration version in an AWS AppConfig configuration profile, and starts a deployment to the target environment using a chosen deployment strategy.

templates.title: AppConfig deployment monitor
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists in-progress AWS AppConfig deployments for an environment, gets each deployment status, and posts a Slack alert when a deployment is rolling back or has stalled.

templates.title: AppConfig config inventory
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that lists every AWS AppConfig application, its environments, and its configuration profiles, and writes a unified inventory into a tracking table so the platform team has a single source of truth.

templates.title: AppConfig change auditor
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists recent AWS AppConfig deployments across environments, summarizes which configuration versions were deployed when, and writes an audit report file for compliance review.

templates.title: AppConfig drift checker
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that retrieves the live AWS AppConfig configuration and compares it against an expected baseline stored in a table, alerting Slack when the deployed configuration drifts from the approved version.

templates.title: AppConfig bootstrap from GitHub
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered when a config file changes in a GitHub pull request that creates a new hosted AWS AppConfig configuration version from the file contents and deploys it to a staging environment for validation.

templates.title: AppConfig gated rollout
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that gates an AWS AppConfig deployment behind a Slack approval: it creates the configuration version, waits for sign-off, starts the deployment with a linear strategy, and monitors completion before reporting back.

skills.name: read-feature-flags
skills.description: Retrieve the latest deployed AWS AppConfig configuration for an application, environment, and profile and use the values to drive feature flags or dynamic settings.
skills.content:
# Read AppConfig Feature Flags

Load live configuration to branch workflow behavior.

## Steps
1. Identify the target application, environment, and configuration profile (IDs or names).
2. Get the latest deployed configuration for that combination.
3. Parse the returned content (usually JSON) into a structured object.
4. Use the flag or setting values to decide which downstream path to take.

## Output
The resolved configuration values and the decision they drive. Do not hardcode flag values — always read them fresh from AppConfig.

skills.name: publish-and-deploy-config
skills.description: Create a new hosted AWS AppConfig configuration version from a document and deploy it to an environment with a chosen deployment strategy.
skills.content:
# Publish and Deploy Config

Ship a new configuration version safely.

## Steps
1. Assemble the configuration content (JSON, YAML, or text) and confirm the target application and configuration profile.
2. Create a new hosted configuration version with the correct content type.
3. Start a deployment of that version to the target environment using an appropriate deployment strategy.
4. Record the returned deployment number for follow-up monitoring.

## Output
The new version number and the started deployment number, plus the deployment state.

skills.name: monitor-deployment-rollback
skills.description: Watch in-progress AWS AppConfig deployments for an environment and surface rollbacks or stalled rollouts so they can be acted on.
skills.content:
# Monitor Deployment Rollback

Keep an eye on configuration rollouts.

## Steps
1. List deployments for the target environment and find in-progress ones.
2. Get the status of each active deployment, capturing state and percentage complete.
3. Flag deployments that are rolling back or have stopped making progress.
4. Optionally stop a deployment that needs to be halted.

## Output
A per-deployment status summary with any rollbacks or stalls called out for action.

skills.name: inventory-appconfig
skills.description: List AWS AppConfig applications, environments, and configuration profiles to build a single inventory of what configuration exists across the account.
skills.content:
# Inventory AppConfig

Build a unified view of all AppConfig resources.

## Steps
1. List every application and capture its ID, name, and description.
2. For each application, list its environments and configuration profiles.
3. Note the profile type (freeform vs feature flags) and where each profile is stored.
4. Assemble the results into a single structured inventory.

## Output
An inventory of applications with their environments and configuration profiles, suitable for writing to a tracking table.

templates.title: IAM permission drift detector
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that diffs AWS IAM policies against the Terraform source of truth, alerts on drift, and writes the drift report to a security Slack channel.

templates.title: IAM wildcard policy auditor
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that scans AWS IAM policies for wildcard permissions, scores each by blast radius, and writes a remediation queue to a security table.

templates.title: IAM access-review automator
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled quarterly workflow that posts AWS IAM access-review requests to role owners in Slack, captures attestations, and writes the audit log to a compliance table.

templates.title: IAM stale-key sweeper
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that reviews IAM users for aged access keys, notifies the owner via Slack, and rotates the key with a fresh one or removes it after a grace period.

templates.title: IAM unused-role cleaner
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled monthly workflow that finds IAM roles with no recent activity, requires owner approval in Slack, and removes the role to reduce attack surface.

templates.title: IAM least-privilege recommender
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that simulates IAM principal policies against expected actions, generates least-privilege policy suggestions for over-permissioned roles, and opens Linear tickets for engineers to apply.

templates.title: IAM policy guardrail watcher
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that snapshots AWS IAM managed policies and role attachments, classifies risk on each change, and pings the security team in Slack when a change broadens permissions.

skills.name: audit-iam-permissions
skills.description: List IAM users, roles, and their attached policies to produce an access audit. Use for security reviews and least-privilege checks.
skills.content:
# Audit IAM Permissions

Report who and what has access in IAM.

## Steps
1. List users and roles to establish the inventory.
2. For each principal of interest, list attached user or role policies.
3. Optionally simulate principal policy to confirm whether a principal can perform sensitive actions.
4. Flag overly broad policies, unused principals, or access keys that should be rotated.

## Output
An audit summary: principals and their attached policies, with risky or excessive grants called out. Do not expose secret values.

skills.name: check-effective-permissions
skills.description: Use IAM policy simulation to verify whether a user or role can perform specific actions on resources. Use for troubleshooting access and validating changes.
skills.content:
# Check Effective Permissions

Determine whether a principal is actually allowed to do something.

## Steps
1. Identify the principal (user or role) and the actions and resource ARNs to test.
2. Run simulate principal policy for those actions against the resources.
3. Read the allowed or denied decision for each action, noting which statement governs it.
4. If denied unexpectedly, inspect the attached policies to explain why.

## Output
A per-action allow/deny verdict with the governing policy, and a plain-language explanation of any denial.

skills.name: provision-iam-principal
skills.description: Create an IAM user or role, attach managed policies, and place users into groups to grant scoped access. Use for onboarding and standing up service roles.
skills.content:
# Provision IAM Principal

Stand up a new IAM user or role with the right permissions.

## Steps
1. Decide whether to create a user (for a person or app) or a role (for a service or cross-account access).
2. For a user, create the user, then add them to the relevant groups or attach the needed managed policy ARNs. For a role, create the role with a trust policy that names the allowed principal, then attach the policy ARNs.
3. Prefer attaching existing managed policies over broad wildcards; grant only the actions required.
4. Confirm the result by listing the attached user or role policies.

## Output
Report the created principal name and ARN and the policies now attached. Do not print any generated secret values.

skills.name: rotate-access-keys
skills.description: Create a fresh IAM access key for a user and delete the old one to complete a safe rotation. Use for scheduled key rotation and remediating aged keys.
skills.content:
# Rotate Access Keys

Replace a user’s access key following the two-step rotation pattern.

## Steps
1. Create a new access key for the target user so two keys exist briefly.
2. Hand the new key to its consumer securely and let dependents switch over and verify they still work.
3. Once the new key is confirmed in use, delete the old access key by its ID.
4. Confirm only the intended key remains for the user.

## Output
Report the user, that a new key was issued, and the old key ID that was deleted. Never print the secret access key value — reference keys only by their access key ID.

templates.title: Identity Center access-review
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled quarterly workflow that surfaces AWS Identity Center permission sets and group memberships, requests owner attestation in Slack, and writes the audit log to a compliance table.

templates.title: Identity Center new-hire onboarder
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that on a Workday new-hire event provisions AWS Identity Center permission sets based on role, and writes the assignment to a tracking table.

templates.title: Identity Center offboarder
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that on a Workday termination revokes the user’s AWS Identity Center assignments and writes the action log to the security audit table.

templates.title: Identity Center assignment monitor
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that snapshots AWS Identity Center account assignments and permission sets, flags new or broadened access, and pings the security Slack channel on changes.

templates.title: Identity Center permission-set drift
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that diffs AWS Identity Center permission sets against the Terraform source of truth, alerts on drift, and writes the report.

templates.title: Identity Center orphaned-access finder
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that lists AWS Identity Center account assignments, flags principals with stale or unexpected access, emails owners for confirmation, and writes the findings to a security dashboard table.

templates.title: Identity Center compliance reporter
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that produces an AWS Identity Center compliance report — permission sets, group memberships, and account assignments — and writes the file for auditors.

templates.title: STS Identity-Center role broker
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes an Identity Center user request, assumes the matching AWS STS role to mint scoped short-lived credentials, writes the issuance to a session log, and alerts Slack when a request targets a privileged role.

skills.name: grant-temporary-access
skills.description: Assign a permission set to a user or group on an AWS account through Identity Center and confirm the assignment completes. Use for just-in-time elevated access.
skills.content:
# Grant Temporary Access

Provision elevated access via an Identity Center account assignment.

## Steps
1. Resolve the Identity Center instance, target account, and permission set.
2. Resolve the principal — get the user or group to confirm the correct ID and type.
3. Create the account assignment for that principal, permission set, and account.
4. Poll check assignment status until it reports SUCCEEDED.

## Output
Confirm the principal, account, permission set, and final assignment status. If it failed, surface the failure reason.

skills.name: revoke-access
skills.description: Remove a permission set assignment from a user or group in Identity Center and confirm deletion. Use to wind down temporary or expired access.
skills.content:
# Revoke Access

Remove an account assignment to revoke access.

## Steps
1. List account assignments to confirm the principal currently holds the permission set on the account.
2. Delete the account assignment for that principal, permission set, and account.
3. Poll check assignment deletion status until it reports SUCCEEDED.
4. Re-list assignments to verify the grant is gone.

## Output
Confirm what was revoked and the final deletion status. Note if the assignment did not exist.

skills.name: access-audit-report
skills.description: Enumerate permission sets, group memberships, and account assignments in Identity Center to produce an access report. Use for compliance and periodic reviews.
skills.content:
# Access Audit Report

Report who has access to what across accounts.

## Steps
1. List instances and accounts to scope the report.
2. List permission sets and, per account, list account assignments.
3. Resolve users and groups behind each assignment with get user and get group.
4. Compile assignments grouped by account and permission set.

## Output
An access report: per account, which principals hold which permission sets, with anything unexpected flagged for review.

templates.title: Secrets Manager scheduled rotation
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists AWS Secrets Manager secrets, generates a new value for each secret past its rotation window, updates it with the new value, and writes the rotation status to a compliance table.

templates.title: Secrets Manager inventory auditor
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that lists all AWS Secrets Manager secrets, flags ones missing descriptions or older than a chosen age, writes a security review, and posts the findings to Slack.

templates.title: Secrets Manager stale-secret cleaner
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists AWS Secrets Manager secrets, identifies ones created before a chosen cutoff, requests owner approval in Slack, deletes the approved secrets, and writes the cleanup audit.

templates.title: Secrets Manager + Infisical mirror
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that mirrors secrets between AWS Secrets Manager and Infisical for cross-cloud applications, normalizes naming, and writes a sync log.

templates.title: Secrets Manager break-glass retrieval
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that gates retrieval of a sensitive AWS Secrets Manager secret behind a Slack approval, captures the requester and justification, fetches the secret only after sign-off, and writes the audit record.

templates.title: Secrets Manager + 1Password bridge
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that bridges select AWS Secrets Manager secrets into 1Password for human-shared credentials while keeping access logs aligned for audit.

templates.title: Secrets Manager change watcher
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls AWS Secrets Manager secret version IDs, compares them against a baseline stored in a table, and pings the security Slack channel when a secret changes unexpectedly.

skills.name: rotate-secret-value
skills.description: Update a stored secret in AWS Secrets Manager with a new value as part of a rotation flow. Use to push refreshed credentials without manual console edits.
skills.content:
# Rotate Secret Value

Update a secret with a new value.

## Steps
1. Confirm the target secret exists by getting it (do not log the returned value).
2. Obtain the new secret value to store, as a string or JSON key/value payload.
3. Update the secret with the new value, creating a new version.
4. Verify by getting the secret and checking the updated version metadata, not the raw value.

## Output
Confirm the secret name and that a new version was created. Never print the secret value itself.

skills.name: audit-secret-inventory
skills.description: List secrets in AWS Secrets Manager and report metadata like last-changed and rotation status. Use for hygiene checks and finding stale secrets.
skills.content:
# Audit Secret Inventory

Report on the secrets that exist without exposing their values.

## Steps
1. List secrets to enumerate names, descriptions, and tags.
2. For each secret of interest, read metadata such as last changed and last rotated dates.
3. Flag secrets that are stale, undescribed, or appear unused.
4. Summarize without ever fetching or printing secret values.

## Output
An inventory summary: secret names with last-changed and rotation status, and stale or unrotated secrets called out. No secret values.

skills.name: store-new-secret
skills.description: Create a new secret in AWS Secrets Manager from a provided credential or generated value. Use to register app credentials, API keys, or DB passwords centrally.
skills.content:
# Store New Secret

Register a new credential in Secrets Manager.

## Steps
1. Choose a clear hierarchical name for the secret, such as my-app/prod/db-password.
2. Assemble the value to store — a plain string, or a JSON object of key/value pairs for structured credentials.
3. Create the secret with that name, value, and a description of what it is and where it is used.
4. Confirm creation by reading back the version metadata, not the value.

## Output
Confirm the secret name, ARN, and new version ID. Never echo the stored secret value back.

skills.name: decommission-secret
skills.description: Schedule deletion of a secret in AWS Secrets Manager with a recovery window so it can be restored if needed. Use to retire unused or rotated-out credentials safely.
skills.content:
# Decommission Secret

Retire a secret without permanently losing it immediately.

## Steps
1. Confirm the target secret and that nothing still depends on it.
2. Schedule deletion with a recovery window (e.g. 30 days) so it can be restored during that period; reserve force delete for confirmed-orphaned secrets only.
3. Record the scheduled deletion date.
4. Re-list secrets to confirm it is marked for deletion.

## Output
Confirm the secret name and the scheduled deletion date, or that immediate deletion was requested. Do not print the secret value.

templates.title: SendGrid + SES enterprise sender
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that splits transactional traffic between SendGrid and AWS SES based on message category and recipient region, balances volume to stay under per-provider limits, and writes provider, status, and latency to a delivery table.

templates.title: SES bulk announcement
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that takes a recipient list from a table and an SES email template, sends the announcement using SES bulk send with per-recipient template data, and writes the per-recipient send status back to the table.

templates.title: SES verified-identity audit
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists AWS SES verified identities, checks the account sending quota and reputation, and posts a Slack report when any identity is unverified or the account approaches the daily quota.

templates.title: SES templated nurture
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that walks each contact in a tables-based nurture sequence through staged SES templated sends with delays between steps, branches on open or click, and stops the sequence when the contact replies.

templates.title: SES + Mailgun multi-region sender
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that routes transactional emails through SES in primary regions and through Mailgun for regions where SES is not provisioned, normalizing template variables and writing one unified send log to a table.

templates.title: SES + AgentMail customer concierge
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that sends outbound customer messages through AWS SES but provisions a per-customer AgentMail inbox to receive replies, threads conversations across both, and tags AgentMail threads with the customer ID.

templates.title: SES domain reputation monitor
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled daily workflow that pulls SES account sending statistics and per-identity reputation indicators, logs them to a tracking table for trend lines, and flags any identity whose complaint or bounce rate is trending up.

templates.title: SES template library sync
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads my approved email templates from a table, creates or updates each one in AWS SES with create template, lists existing SES templates to detect drift, and deletes templates that have been removed from the table so the SES library stays in sync.

skills.name: send-notification-email
skills.description: Send a transactional email through AWS SES to one or more recipients. Use for alerts, confirmations, and one-off notifications from a workflow.
skills.content:
# Send Notification Email

Send a transactional email via SES.

## Steps
1. Determine the verified sender identity, the recipients, subject, and body.
2. Choose a plain-text or HTML body to match the message.
3. Send the email, including reply-to or CC recipients if needed.
4. Confirm the send succeeded and capture the message ID.

## Output
Report the SES message ID and the recipients. If the send was rejected, surface the SES error (for example, an unverified sender or sandbox restriction).

skills.name: send-templated-campaign
skills.description: Send a templated SES email to many recipients with per-recipient personalization. Use for newsletters, onboarding sequences, and bulk notifications.
skills.content:
# Send Templated Campaign

Send personalized emails using an SES template.

## Steps
1. Confirm the template exists with get template, or create it first.
2. Assemble the recipient list with each recipient's template data for personalization.
3. Use send bulk email for many recipients, or send templated email for a single message.
4. Collect per-recipient send status.

## Output
Report how many messages were accepted versus failed, with message IDs and the reason for any failures.

skills.name: manage-email-templates
skills.description: Create, fetch, list, and delete reusable email templates in AWS SES. Use to maintain a consistent, version-controlled template library.
skills.content:
# Manage Email Templates

Maintain the SES template library.

## Steps
1. To add a template, create it with a name, subject, and HTML and text parts using placeholder variables.
2. To review, get a template by name or list templates.
3. To retire one, delete the template by name.
4. Keep template names descriptive so they are easy to reference when sending.

## Output
Report the template name affected and the action taken, or the template contents for a fetch.

skills.name: check-sending-health
skills.description: Inspect AWS SES account sending limits, quota usage, and verified identities. Use to confirm capacity and deliverability readiness before a send.
skills.content:
# Check Sending Health

Verify SES is ready to send.

## Steps
1. Get the account to read the sending quota, send rate, and whether the account is out of the sandbox.
2. List identities to confirm the intended sender domain or address is verified.
3. Compare planned volume against the remaining 24-hour quota.
4. Flag any blockers — sandbox mode, unverified senders, or quota nearly exhausted.

## Output
Report sending enabled status, quota used versus max, and any unverified identities that would block the send.

templates.title: AWS STS access key identifier

templates.title: STS Identity-Center role broker

skills.name: assume-cross-account-role
skills.description: Call AWS STS to assume a role and obtain temporary credentials for a target account. Use for cross-account access in a workflow.
skills.content:
# Assume Cross-Account Role

Obtain temporary credentials by assuming an IAM role.

## Steps
1. Identify the role ARN to assume and a descriptive session name.
2. Set the session duration and any external ID required by the trust policy.
3. Call assume role to receive temporary access key, secret key, and session token.
4. Pass the temporary credentials to the downstream step that needs cross-account access.

## Output
Confirm the assumed role ARN and credential expiration. Never print the secret access key or session token in plain logs.

skills.name: verify-caller-identity
skills.description: Use AWS STS get caller identity to confirm which account, user, or role the current credentials resolve to. Use to validate setup and debug auth issues.
skills.content:
# Verify Caller Identity

Confirm which AWS identity the workflow is operating as.

## Steps
1. Call get caller identity with the active credentials.
2. Read the returned account ID, user ID, and principal ARN.
3. Compare against the expected account and role for the task.
4. If it does not match, flag a likely credential or assume-role misconfiguration.

## Output
Report the account ID and ARN of the active identity, and whether it matches the expected principal.

skills.name: mint-mfa-session-token
skills.description: Use AWS STS to mint short-lived session credentials, optionally backed by an MFA token, for IAM-user workflows that require MFA. Use for time-boxed elevated sessions.
skills.content:
# Mint MFA Session Token

Issue temporary credentials, optionally enforcing MFA.

## Steps
1. Decide the session duration the downstream task needs.
2. If MFA is required, supply the MFA device serial number and the current token code.
3. Call get session token to receive a temporary access key, secret key, and session token.
4. Hand the temporary credentials to the step that needs them and let them expire naturally.

## Output
Confirm that a session token was issued and its expiration time. Never print the secret access key or session token value.

skills.name: identify-access-key-owner
skills.description: Use AWS STS get access key info to resolve which account an access key ID belongs to. Use for incident triage of leaked or unexpected keys.
skills.content:
# Identify Access Key Owner

Find out which account owns an access key ID.

## Steps
1. Take the access key ID under investigation (for example, one found in a leak or an unexpected log).
2. Call get access key info to resolve the owning AWS account ID.
3. Compare the account against your known and expected accounts.
4. If it belongs to an unexpected account, escalate for investigation.

## Output
Report the access key ID (never the secret) and its owning account ID, plus whether that account is expected.

skills.name: extract-invoice-fields
skills.description: Run an invoice or receipt through AWS Textract and return clean structured fields (vendor, date, totals, line items). Use when you need to digitize finance documents.
skills.content:
# Extract Invoice Fields

Use AWS Textract to pull structured data from an invoice or receipt image/PDF.

## Steps
1. Choose the processing mode: Single Page for JPEG, PNG, or one-page PDF; Multi-Page for multi-page PDF/TIFF staged in S3.
2. Provide the document (upload, file reference, or S3 URI) and enable Extract Forms and Extract Tables so key-value pairs and line items are captured.
3. Run the extraction and read the returned blocks (KEY_VALUE_SET, TABLE, CELL, LINE).
4. Map key-value pairs to fields: vendor, invoice number, invoice date, due date, subtotal, tax, and total.
5. Reconstruct line items from the TABLE/CELL blocks into rows with description, quantity, unit price, and amount.

## Output
Return a clean JSON record with the header fields and a line-items array. Flag any field where Textract confidence is low or the totals do not reconcile so a human can review.

skills.name: extract-form-key-values
skills.description: Turn a scanned form into structured key-value pairs and tables using AWS Textract. Use for intake forms, applications, and contracts.
skills.content:
# Extract Form Key-Values

Digitize a scanned form into structured data.

## Steps
1. Select Single Page mode for an image or one-page PDF, or Multi-Page mode with an S3 URI for longer documents.
2. Enable Extract Forms (key-value pairs) and, if the form has tables, Extract Tables. Enable Analyze Document Layout for complex multi-column forms.
3. Run the extraction and parse the KEY_VALUE_SET blocks into field-name to field-value pairs.
4. Normalize field names (trim labels, lowercase keys) and coerce values like dates and numbers.

## Output
Return a flat object of normalized field names to values, plus any extracted tables as arrays of rows. Note pages or fields with low confidence for review.

skills.name: ocr-document-to-text
skills.description: Convert a scanned document or image into plain readable text with AWS Textract OCR. Use to digitize handwritten notes, faxes, or image-only PDFs for indexing or search.
skills.content:
# OCR Document To Text

Extract readable text from a scanned or image-only document.

## Steps
1. Pick the processing mode that matches the file: Single Page for an image or one-page PDF, Multi-Page (S3) for multi-page documents.
2. Provide the document and run the extraction. Plain OCR does not require the Forms or Tables features.
3. Read the LINE and WORD blocks and join LINE blocks in reading order to reconstruct the text.
4. Preserve paragraph and page breaks using the PAGE blocks.

## Output
Return the full extracted text as clean Markdown, grouped by page. Include the page count from document metadata and surface any low-confidence lines so they can be reviewed before indexing.

skills.name: provision-new-user
skills.description: Create a new Azure AD (Entra ID) user account and add it to the right groups. Use when onboarding an employee or contractor.
skills.content:
# Provision New User

Create an Azure AD user and grant initial group access.

## Steps
1. Use Create User with the required fields: display name, mail nickname, user principal name (e.g. name@yourdomain.com), and an initial password. Set Account Enabled to Yes.
2. Fill optional profile fields when available: first name, last name, job title, department, office location, and mobile phone.
3. For each group the person should belong to, resolve the group with Get Group or List Groups, then call Add Group Member with the new user id.
4. Confirm membership with List Group Members.

## Output
Return the created user id, user principal name, and the list of groups they were added to. If a username collision or password-policy error occurs, report it clearly instead of retrying blindly.

skills.name: offboard-user
skills.description: Disable an Azure AD account and strip its group memberships when someone leaves. Use for secure offboarding.
skills.content:
# Offboard User

Revoke access for a departing user.

## Steps
1. Resolve the account with Get User by user principal name or id.
2. Use Update User to set Account Enabled to No so the user can no longer sign in.
3. Use List Group Members or the user record to enumerate the groups the user belongs to.
4. For each group, call Remove Group Member with the user id.

## Output
Return the disabled user id and the list of groups the user was removed from. Note any group where removal failed so it can be handled manually, and recommend writing the action to an audit record.

skills.name: audit-group-membership
skills.description: List the members of an Azure AD group for an access review. Use for periodic attestation of privileged or sensitive groups.
skills.content:
# Audit Group Membership

Produce a current membership snapshot for a group.

## Steps
1. Resolve the target group with Get Group or List Groups (filter or search by name).
2. Call List Group Members for the group id, raising Max Results if the group is large.
3. For each member, optionally call Get User to enrich with job title, department, and account-enabled status.

## Output
Return a table of members with id, display name, email, department, and whether the account is enabled. Highlight disabled or stale accounts that still hold membership and should be reviewed for removal.

templates.title: Azure DevOps sprint burndown digest

skills.name: triage-build-failure
skills.description: Investigate a failed Azure DevOps build, pinpoint the failing stage, and summarize the root cause. Use when a pipeline run breaks.
skills.content:
# Triage Build Failure

Diagnose why an Azure DevOps build failed.

## Steps
1. Use Get Build Timeline for the build id to find which stage, job, or task failed.
2. Use List Build Logs to locate the log id for the failing step, then Get Build Log to read its contents.
3. Scan the log for the first error, the failing command, and the exit code; ignore noise after the initial failure.
4. Optionally use Get Work Items Between Builds against the last successful build to see what changed.

## Output
Return a concise root-cause summary: the failing stage/task, the key error line, the likely cause, and a suggested next action. Include a deep link to the run when available.

skills.name: create-work-item
skills.description: Create a new Azure DevOps work item (Issue, Task, or Epic) with the right fields. Use to file bugs, tasks, or features from another system.
skills.content:
# Create Work Item

File a structured Azure DevOps work item.

## Steps
1. Choose the work item type: Issue, Task, or Epic, matching the request.
2. Use Create Work Item with a clear title and an HTML or plain-text description.
3. Set context fields where known: assignee, priority (1-4), area path, iteration path, and semicolon-separated tags.
4. For a Task, set Activity, Remaining Work, and Completed Work; for an Epic, set Start Date and Target Date.

## Output
Return the new work item id, type, title, state, and a link. Confirm the assignee and iteration. If a required field is missing, ask for it rather than guessing.

skills.name: generate-release-notes
skills.description: Compile release notes from the work items completed between two Azure DevOps builds. Use at release time to summarize what shipped.
skills.content:
# Generate Release Notes

Produce release notes for a build range.

## Steps
1. Identify the From Build ID (previous release) and To Build ID (current release).
2. Use Get Work Items Between Builds to list the associated work items.
3. For each work item, use Get Work Items Batch or Get Work Item to pull title, type, and state.
4. Group items by type (Features/Epics, Tasks, Bugs/Issues) and write a one-line summary per item.

## Output
Return formatted Markdown release notes grouped by category, each line linking the work item id and title. Add a short headline summary of the most user-facing changes at the top.

skills.name: report-pipeline-health
skills.description: Summarize recent Azure DevOps pipeline run results to surface pass rate and regressions. Use for daily or weekly engineering health reports.
skills.content:
# Report Pipeline Health

Summarize recent pipeline reliability.

## Steps
1. Use List Pipelines to enumerate the pipelines you care about.
2. For each, use List Pipeline Runs to pull recent runs within your window.
3. Compute pass rate (succeeded vs total), average duration, and the count of recent failures per pipeline.
4. Flag pipelines whose pass rate dropped or whose duration increased noticeably versus prior runs.

## Output
Return a per-pipeline summary table (name, pass rate, avg duration, recent failures) and a short narrative calling out regressions and any pipeline that is consistently red.

skills.name: send-document-for-signature
skills.description: Send a Box document for e-signature and confirm the request. Use for contracts, NDAs, and approval forms that need a signer.
skills.content:
# Send Document For Signature

Kick off a Box Sign request for one or more documents.

## Steps
1. Identify the Box file id(s) to sign (use Search or List Folder Items if you only have a name).
2. Use Create Sign Request with the source file ids and the primary signer email; set the signer role (signer, approver, or final copy reader).
3. Add a clear email subject and message, and add any additional signers as a JSON array of email/role objects.
4. Optionally set a destination folder for the signed copy, days valid, and reminders.

## Output
Return the sign request id, status, signer list, and the prepare/sign URL. Tell the user the request was sent and how to track it. If a file id cannot be resolved, ask for clarification.

skills.name: track-signature-status
skills.description: Check the status of Box Sign requests and follow up on pending signers. Use to monitor outstanding e-signature requests.
skills.content:
# Track Signature Status

Report on outstanding and completed Box Sign requests.

## Steps
1. Use List Sign Requests to retrieve recent requests, paging with the marker when needed.
2. For a specific request, use Get Sign Request with the sign request id to read per-signer status.
3. Identify requests that are still pending versus signed, declined, or expired.
4. For stalled requests, use Resend Sign Request to nudge signers, or Cancel Sign Request if it is no longer needed.

## Output
Return a status summary per request: name, overall status, which signers have signed, and which are outstanding. Recommend resend or cancel actions for stale requests.

skills.name: organize-files-into-folder
skills.description: Upload files into a structured Box folder, creating folders as needed. Use to file documents into a standard organized layout.
skills.content:
# Organize Files Into Folder

Place documents into the correct Box folder structure.

## Steps
1. Determine the destination. Use List Folder Items or Search to find an existing folder, or Create Folder under the right parent (use "0" for root) if it does not exist.
2. Upload each file with Upload File, setting the parent folder id and an explicit file name when needed.
3. To reorganize existing files, use Update File to rename, move (set Move to Folder ID), tag, or describe them.
4. Use Copy File when a document must live in more than one folder.

## Output
Return the created folder id (if any) and a list of the files placed, each with its id, name, and final folder. Confirm the resulting structure.

skills.name: search-box-content
skills.description: Find files and folders in Box matching a query and return their details. Use to locate documents before acting on them.
skills.content:
# Search Box Content

Locate documents in Box.

## Steps
1. Use Search with the query string. Narrow with optional filters: ancestor folder id, file extensions (e.g. pdf,docx), and content type (file, folder, or web link).
2. Page through results with limit and offset if there are many matches.
3. For promising hits, use Get File Info to confirm name, size, owner, and modified date.

## Output
Return the matching items with id, name, type, owner, and last-modified date. If the query is ambiguous or returns too many results, suggest a tighter query or folder scope.

skills.name: enrich-company-by-domain
skills.description: Look up a company by domain and return its brand assets and firmographics. Use to enrich a CRM record, lead, or account with logo, colors, and company data.
skills.content:
# Enrich Company By Domain

Fetch brand and company data for a known domain.

## Steps
1. Use Get Brand with the company domain as the identifier (e.g. nike.com). A stock ticker, ISIN, or crypto symbol also works.
2. Read the returned logos, colors, fonts, links, description, and company firmographics.
3. Pick the best logo for the use case (prefer a transparent or themed variant) and the primary brand color.

## Output
Return a tidy record: company name, domain, description, primary logo URL, primary brand color hex, social links, and key firmographics. If the quality score is low or the brand is unclaimed, note that the data may be incomplete.

skills.name: resolve-brand-by-name
skills.description: Search for a brand by name to find its domain and logo when you only have the company name. Use to disambiguate or resolve a domain before deeper enrichment.
skills.content:
# Resolve Brand By Name

Find a brand when you only know its name.

## Steps
1. Use Search Brands with the company name (e.g. "Nike").
2. Review the results array; each entry has a brand name, domain, and icon.
3. Choose the best match by exact name and most likely official domain.
4. Optionally follow up with Get Brand on the chosen domain for full assets and firmographics.

## Output
Return the resolved brand name, domain, and icon URL. If several plausible matches exist, list the top candidates with their domains so the user can confirm.

skills.name: collect-brand-assets-for-personalization
skills.description: Gather a prospect or customer brand kit (logo, colors, fonts) for personalizing decks, emails, or portals. Use ahead of personalized outreach or design work.
skills.content:
# Collect Brand Assets For Personalization

Build a usable brand kit for a target company.

## Steps
1. Resolve the company domain (use Search Brands first if you only have a name).
2. Use Get Brand to retrieve logos, colors, and fonts.
3. Select assets fit for purpose: a high-contrast logo for a deck cover, the primary and secondary colors, and the brand font names.

## Output
Return a brand kit object: logo URLs by theme (light/dark), an ordered color palette with hex values, and font names. Note any missing asset so the design step can fall back to a neutral default.

templates.title: Brex cash balance monitor

templates.title: Brex budget utilization report

templates.title: Brex team directory assistant

templates.title: Brex vendor payment tracker

skills.name: spend-report
skills.description: Summarize Brex spend over a period, broken down by category, merchant, and user.
skills.content:
# Spend Report

Build a clear summary of company spend from Brex expenses.

## Steps
1. List expenses filtered to the requested period using the purchased-at date filters.
2. Group expenses by merchant category, merchant, and user, totaling billing amounts (amounts are in cents).
3. Highlight the largest expenses and any with OUT_OF_POLICY status.

## Output
Return total spend, a breakdown by category and merchant, the top spenders, and any flagged out-of-policy expenses with dashboard links.

skills.name: attach-receipt
skills.description: Upload a receipt file and attach it to the right Brex expense.
skills.content:
# Attach a Receipt

Get a receipt onto the correct Brex expense.

## Steps
1. If the target expense is known, use Upload Receipt with the expense ID.
2. If not, use Match Receipt so Brex pairs the receipt with the right expense automatically.
3. Confirm the upload succeeded and capture the receipt ID.

## Output
Return the receipt ID, the receipt name, and the expense it was attached to (or note that Brex is matching it automatically).

skills.name: memo-cleanup
skills.description: Find Brex expenses missing memos and fill them in from merchant details.
skills.content:
# Memo Cleanup

Keep expense memos complete for accounting.

## Steps
1. List recent expenses and find ones with an empty memo.
2. For each, draft a short memo from the merchant descriptor, category, and amount.
3. Update each expense with the drafted memo using Update Expense Memo.

## Output
Return the list of expenses updated, each with its new memo, and any expenses that could not be updated.

skills.name: budget-utilization
skills.description: Report utilization for Brex budgets and spend limits.
skills.content:
# Budget Utilization

Show how much of each budget and spend limit has been used.

## Steps
1. List budgets and capture each amount and status.
2. List spend limits and capture each current period balance.
3. Compute utilization where both an amount and a balance are available (amounts are in cents).

## Output
Return each budget and spend limit with its owner, period, amount, and utilization, flagging any that are near or over their limit.

skills.name: cash-balance-check
skills.description: Check Brex cash account balances and recent account activity.
skills.content:
# Cash Balance Check

Give a quick read on company cash in Brex.

## Steps
1. List cash accounts and capture current and available balances (amounts are in cents).
2. For the primary account, list recent cash transactions.
3. Note any unusually large recent movements.

## Output
Return each account with its balances, the most recent transactions for the primary account, and any large movements worth a look.

skills.name: statement-reconciliation
skills.description: Reconcile a Brex card statement period against its settled transactions.
skills.content:
# Statement Reconciliation

Tie a card statement back to its underlying transactions.

## Steps
1. List card statements and pick the period to reconcile.
2. List card transactions posted within that period using the posted-at filter.
3. Compare transaction totals to the statement start and end balances and flag gaps.

## Output
Return the statement period, its balances, the transaction total for the period, and any discrepancy that needs review.

skills.name: scrape-page-content
skills.description: Fetch the content of a single web page through Bright Data Web Unlocker, bypassing bot blocks and geo-restrictions. Use to read a page an agent cannot otherwise access.
skills.content:
# Scrape Page Content

Retrieve a page that is normally blocked or geo-restricted.

## Steps
1. Use Scrape URL with the target URL and your unlocker zone (e.g. web_unlocker1).
2. Choose the format: Raw HTML for full markup, or JSON for a parsed response.
3. Set the Country code when the page differs by region.
4. Run it and read the returned content and HTTP status code.

## Output
Return the cleaned page content (text or relevant HTML) and the status code. If the status indicates a block or error, report it and suggest a different zone or country rather than returning empty content.

skills.name: search-the-web
skills.description: Run a search-engine query through Bright Data SERP API and return ranked results. Use for keyword research, competitive monitoring, or grounding an answer in fresh results.
skills.content:
# Search The Web

Get structured search results for a query.

## Steps
1. Use SERP Search with the query and your SERP zone.
2. Pick the search engine (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, or Yandex) and set country/language for localized results.
3. Set the number of results to the amount you need.
4. Read the results array (title, URL, snippet, rank).

## Output
Return the ranked results as a list with title, URL, and snippet. Summarize the top findings for the user, and note the engine, country, and query used so the result is reproducible.

skills.name: discover-pages-by-intent
skills.description: Find web pages that match a described intent using Bright Data Discover, optionally pulling page content. Use to gather sources on a topic without crafting exact queries.
skills.content:
# Discover Pages By Intent

Find relevant pages from a natural-language description.

## Steps
1. Use Discover with a search query and an Intent describing what you actually want (e.g. "official pricing pages and recent change notes").
2. Set the number of results, country, and language as needed.
3. Enable Include Page Content and choose Markdown or JSON when you want the page bodies, not just links.

## Output
Return the discovered pages ranked by relevance with URL, title, and (if requested) extracted content. Summarize what was found and flag any low-relevance results so they can be filtered out.

skills.name: run-dataset-scraper
skills.description: Trigger a Bright Data pre-built dataset scraper for structured extraction across many URLs and retrieve the results. Use for bulk structured data from sites like e-commerce or social.
skills.content:
# Run Dataset Scraper

Extract structured records across many URLs with a pre-built scraper.

## Steps
1. Identify the dataset scraper id for the target site (e.g. gd_...).
2. For small batches (up to 20 URLs), use Sync Scrape to get results back inline; choose JSON, NDJSON, or CSV.
3. For larger jobs, use Scrape Dataset, which returns a snapshot id.
4. Poll Snapshot Status until it is ready, then use Download Snapshot to fetch the data. Use Cancel Snapshot to abort a job that is no longer needed.

## Output
Return the structured records (or the snapshot id and status for async jobs). For async runs, report progress and only return data once the snapshot is complete.

skills.name: automate-web-task
skills.description: Drive a browser agent to complete a multi-step task on a website, like navigating, clicking, and submitting. Use when a site has no API and a human would normally do the clicks.
skills.content:
# Automate Web Task

Have the browser agent perform a goal-oriented task on the web.

## Steps
1. Write a clear, step-by-step Task describing the goal and any success condition (e.g. "log in, open Billing, download the latest invoice").
2. Set the Start URL so the agent begins on the right page.
3. Put any credentials or sensitive inputs in Variables (Secrets) and reference them in the task by name rather than pasting them inline.
4. Restrict Allowed Domains to keep the agent on the intended site, and raise Max Steps for longer flows.

## Output
Return whether the task succeeded, the final output, and the share URL for the recorded session so the run can be audited. If the agent gets stuck, report the last step and what blocked it.

skills.name: extract-structured-data-from-site
skills.description: Use a browser agent to navigate a site and return data in a defined JSON schema. Use to pull structured records (prices, listings, table rows) from pages without an API.
skills.content:
# Extract Structured Data From Site

Navigate a website and return structured data.

## Steps
1. Write a Task that tells the agent what to find and where (e.g. "go to the pricing page and collect every plan name and monthly price").
2. Set the Start URL and limit Allowed Domains to the target site.
3. Provide a Structured Output Schema (stringified JSON schema) describing the exact fields you want back.
4. Run it; the agent fills the schema from what it observes on the page.

## Output
Return the data as objects matching the provided schema. Confirm each field was actually found on the page; if a field could not be located, leave it null and note it rather than fabricating a value.

skills.name: fill-and-submit-form
skills.description: Have a browser agent fill out and submit a web form using supplied field values. Use for vendor portals, questionnaires, or applications that have no API.
skills.content:
# Fill And Submit Form

Complete a web form end to end.

## Steps
1. Describe the form and the mapping of values to fields in the Task (e.g. "fill the contact form: name, company, message, then submit").
2. Set the Start URL to the form page and constrain Allowed Domains.
3. Pass any private values through Variables (Secrets) so they are injected securely.
4. Ask the agent to confirm the submission succeeded (look for a success message or confirmation page) before finishing.

## Output
Return whether the form submitted successfully, any confirmation text or reference number shown, and the session share URL as an audit trail. If a required field was missing or validation failed, report which field and why.

skills.name: book-a-meeting
skills.description: Create a Cal.com booking for an attendee on a chosen event type and time. Use to schedule a call once you know the slot and attendee details.
skills.content:
# Book A Meeting

Create a confirmed Cal.com booking.

## Steps
1. Identify the event type to book (select it or pass its numeric event type id).
2. Set the Start Time as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.
3. Provide the attendee name, email, and IANA time zone (e.g. America/New_York). Add guests or a duration override if needed.
4. Create the booking.

## Output
Return the booking UID, start and end time, attendee, and the meeting URL. Confirm the booking to the user. If the slot is unavailable, suggest checking available slots first and propose alternatives.

skills.name: find-available-slots
skills.description: Look up open time slots for a Cal.com event type within a date range. Use before booking to offer the attendee valid times.
skills.content:
# Find Available Slots

Retrieve bookable time slots for an event type.

## Steps
1. Select the event type (or pass its id, or an event type slug plus username).
2. Set the Start Time and End Time of the window to search (ISO 8601 UTC).
3. Set the attendee time zone so slots are returned in their local time, and a duration if the event supports multiple lengths.
4. Read the returned slots.

## Output
Return the available slots as a clean list of start times in the requested time zone. Summarize the next few openings for the user; if none exist in the window, widen the range and retry.

skills.name: reschedule-or-cancel-booking
skills.description: Move a Cal.com booking to a new time or cancel it, with a reason. Use to handle change or cancellation requests for an existing booking.
skills.content:
# Reschedule Or Cancel Booking

Change or cancel an existing Cal.com booking.

## Steps
1. Identify the booking by its UID (use List Bookings to find it if you only have attendee or date details).
2. To move it, use Reschedule Booking with the new Start Time (ISO 8601) and an optional rescheduling reason.
3. To cancel, use Cancel Booking with an optional cancellation reason.
4. For request-based event types, use Confirm Booking or Decline Booking instead.

## Output
Return the booking UID and its new status (rescheduled, cancelled, confirmed, or declined) plus the updated time when applicable. Confirm the change to the user.

skills.name: summarize-upcoming-bookings
skills.description: List and summarize upcoming Cal.com bookings for a period. Use for a daily agenda or to brief a host on their schedule.
skills.content:
# Summarize Upcoming Bookings

Produce an agenda from Cal.com bookings.

## Steps
1. Use List Bookings with status Upcoming.
2. For each booking, read the title, start/end time, attendees, and meeting URL.
3. Sort chronologically and group by day if the range spans multiple days.

## Output
Return an ordered agenda: each entry with time, title, attendee name, and join link. Add a short headline like the number of meetings and the first start time so the host gets a quick read on the day.

skills.name: list-upcoming-meetings
skills.description: Pull upcoming Calendly scheduled events for a date range and summarize them. Use to brief a host on their schedule or build a daily agenda.
skills.content:
# List Upcoming Meetings

Summarize upcoming Calendly events.

## Steps
1. Use List Scheduled Events. Filter to status active and set Min Start Time and Max Start Time (ISO 8601 UTC) for the window.
2. Filter by user or organization URI when scoping to a specific host (Get Current User returns your URI if needed).
3. For each event, read name, start_time, end_time, location, and scheduling_url; page with the page token if there are many.

## Output
Return an ordered agenda: each meeting with time, name, location/join link, and the invitee. Add a one-line headline (count and first start time) for a quick read.

skills.name: get-event-attendees
skills.description: Retrieve the invitees for a Calendly scheduled event, including answers and contact info. Use to prep for a meeting or sync attendees to a CRM.
skills.content:
# Get Event Attendees

List who is attending a Calendly event.

## Steps
1. Identify the scheduled event by its UUID or URI (use List Scheduled Events to locate it).
2. Use List Event Invitees for that event; optionally filter by email or status.
3. Read each invitee record: name, email, status, and any questions and answers captured at booking.

## Output
Return the invitees with name, email, status, and their intake answers. Flag canceled or no-show invitees so they can be handled differently from confirmed attendees.

skills.name: cancel-scheduled-event
skills.description: Cancel a Calendly scheduled event with an optional reason. Use to call off a meeting and notify the invitee through Calendly.
skills.content:
# Cancel Scheduled Event

Call off a Calendly meeting.

## Steps
1. Find the scheduled event UUID or URI (use List Scheduled Events filtered by invitee email or time if you only have those details).
2. Use Cancel Event with the event UUID and a clear cancellation reason.
3. Calendly notifies the invitee automatically.

## Output
Return the event UUID and confirmation that it was canceled. Echo the reason. If the event is already canceled or cannot be found, report that instead of retrying.

skills.name: push-record-to-clay
skills.description: Send a single contact or account record to a Clay table via its populate webhook so Clay can enrich it. Use to hand a lead off to a Clay enrichment waterfall.
skills.content:
# Push Record To Clay

Send one record into a Clay table for enrichment.

## Steps
1. Get the Clay table populate webhook URL (Clay shows it on the table when you add a "Webhook" source).
2. Build the record as a JSON object whose keys match the Clay table column names you want to populate (e.g. name, email, company, domain, linkedin_url).
3. If the table has webhook authentication enabled, supply the auth token; it is sent in the x-clay-webhook-auth header.
4. Populate the table with the record.

## Output
Return the webhook response and metadata (status, timestamp). Confirm the record was accepted. Note that enrichment runs asynchronously inside Clay, so the enriched columns appear there, not in the immediate response.

skills.name: bulk-load-list-into-clay
skills.description: Push many prospect or account rows from a table into a Clay workbook for enrichment. Use to seed a lead list or sync a CRM segment into Clay.
skills.content:
# Bulk Load List Into Clay

Load a list of records into a Clay table.

## Steps
1. Gather the source rows (e.g. from a Sim table or a CRM query).
2. Get the Clay table populate webhook URL and any auth token.
3. For each row, map your fields to the Clay column names and populate the table once per record. Keep the JSON keys consistent across all records so columns line up.
4. Send the records, pacing them if the list is large.

## Output
Return a count of records pushed and any that failed (with the error). Remind the user that Clay enriches the rows on its side, and suggest they verify the row count in the Clay table once ingestion completes.

skills.name: find-user
skills.description: Look up a Clerk user by email, username, or name and return their profile. Use to resolve a user before acting on their account or syncing them elsewhere.
skills.content:
# Find User

Locate a Clerk user account.

## Steps
1. Use List Users with a Search Query (matches email, phone, username, or name), or the email/username filters for an exact match.
2. If you already have the Clerk user id (user_...), use Get User instead for the full record.
3. Review the returned profile: id, primary email, name, externalId, and flags like banned, locked, and twoFactorEnabled.

## Output
Return the matched user id, primary email, name, and key status flags. If multiple users match, list the candidates with their emails so the right one can be confirmed; if none match, say so.

skills.name: provision-user
skills.description: Create or update a Clerk user with email, name, and metadata. Use to onboard a user or sync profile changes from another system into Clerk.
skills.content:
# Provision User

Create or update a Clerk user.

## Steps
1. To create, use Create User with at least an email address (and optionally phone, username, password, first/last name).
2. To set application roles or app data, pass Public Metadata (visible to the frontend) and Private Metadata (server-only) as JSON.
3. Set External ID to link the Clerk user to your own system id.
4. To modify an existing user, use Update User with the user id and only the fields that change.

## Output
Return the user id, primary email, and the metadata that was set. Confirm whether the user was created or updated. If a required field is missing or the email already exists, report it clearly.

skills.name: audit-user-sessions
skills.description: List and inspect a Clerk user active sessions and revoke suspicious ones. Use for security review or forced sign-out.
skills.content:
# Audit User Sessions

Review and control Clerk sessions.

## Steps
1. Use List Sessions filtered by user id and status (e.g. active) to see current sessions.
2. For a specific session, use Get Session to read its details: client, status, lastActiveAt.
3. Identify sessions that look risky (stale, unexpected client, or flagged by your own logic).
4. Use Revoke Session with the session id to force sign-out of any session that should not continue.

## Output
Return the list of sessions reviewed with status and last-active time, and the ids of any sessions revoked. Summarize the action taken so the security trail is clear.

skills.name: manage-organization
skills.description: Create a Clerk organization or look up its details and membership. Use when provisioning a new team or tenant in a multi-tenant app.
skills.content:
# Manage Organization

Create or inspect a Clerk organization.

## Steps
1. To create, use Create Organization with the organization name and the Creator User ID (that user becomes the admin); optionally set a slug and max members.
2. To inspect, use Get Organization by org id or slug, or List Organizations with a search query and include members count.
3. Read back the org id, slug, members count, and limits.

## Output
Return the organization id, name, slug, and member count. When creating, confirm the admin user and echo the org id so it can be linked back to your billing or CRM record.

templates.title: Natural-language ClickHouse query
templates.prompt: Build a workflow where I ask a question in plain English, an agent writes the matching ClickHouse SQL against my events table, runs the query, and returns the results formatted as a readable answer.

templates.title: Daily ClickHouse metrics digest
