templates.title: Event ingestion to ClickHouse
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes incoming event payloads, maps them to the right columns with an agent, and bulk-inserts the rows into a ClickHouse table for analytics.

skills.name: answer-question-with-sql
skills.description: Translate a plain-English analytics question into ClickHouse SQL, run it, and return the answer. Use for ad-hoc data questions over a ClickHouse table.
skills.content:
# Answer Question With SQL

Turn a natural-language question into a ClickHouse query and report the result.

## Steps
1. If you do not know the schema, use Introspect Schema or Describe Table to learn the columns and types.
2. Write a ClickHouse SELECT using ClickHouse functions (toDate, uniqExact, quantile, etc.). Filter on primary/sorting keys and add a LIMIT for exploratory queries.
3. Run it with the Query (SELECT) operation against the connection (host, port, database, credentials).
4. Inspect the returned rows and row count.

## Output
Return the result as a small table plus a one-sentence answer to the original question. Include the SQL you ran so it is reproducible. If the query errors, report the message and adjust the SQL rather than guessing blindly.

skills.name: summarize-metrics
skills.description: Run aggregation queries against ClickHouse and summarize key metrics and trends. Use for a recurring metrics digest or dashboard refresh.
skills.content:
# Summarize Metrics

Compute and summarize metrics from ClickHouse.

## Steps
1. Confirm the relevant table and time column with Describe Table if needed.
2. Write aggregation queries (e.g. daily uniqExact users, counts, quantiles over a time window) using Query (SELECT).
3. Run each query against the connection and collect the results.
4. Compare against the prior period to spot increases, drops, or anomalies.

## Output
Return a concise digest: the headline numbers, period-over-period change, and any notable anomalies. Keep it readable, lead with the most important metric, and note the time window covered.

skills.name: bulk-insert-events
skills.description: Insert a batch of rows into a ClickHouse table after mapping them to the right columns. Use to ingest event or record payloads into ClickHouse.
skills.content:
# Bulk Insert Events

Load a batch of records into a ClickHouse table.

## Steps
1. Use Describe Table to confirm the target column names and types.
2. Map each incoming payload to those columns, coercing types (e.g. timestamps to DateTime format, numbers to the right width).
3. Build a JSON array of row objects with consistent keys, then use Insert Rows (Bulk) against the table.
4. Verify with Count Rows or a small SELECT.

## Output
Return the number of rows inserted and any rows that were skipped or failed validation, with the reason. Confirm the new total row count so the caller knows ingestion succeeded.

templates.title: Cloudflare DNS change tracker
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that pulls every Cloudflare DNS record for my zones each hour, diffs the snapshot against the previous run, logs added, removed, and modified records to a table, and posts a Slack alert when sensitive records like MX or NS change.

templates.title: Cache purge on deploy
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that fires when a Vercel deployment succeeds on production, purges the Cloudflare cache for the affected hostnames, verifies the new content is being served, and posts a confirmation message to Slack with the purged paths.

templates.title: SSL and zone health check
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled weekly workflow that inspects every Cloudflare zone for SSL certificate status, security level, and zone settings drift, logs findings to a table, and opens Linear tickets for any zones that need attention.

templates.title: DNS analytics digest
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that pulls Cloudflare DNS analytics for the top zones every Monday, identifies query spikes, anomalies, and surges in particular record types, and emails a written analysis to the platform team with traffic graphs and recommendations.

templates.title: Zone provisioning workflow
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that accepts a domain name from a form, creates a new Cloudflare zone, sets opinionated default DNS records and zone settings, generates the nameserver instructions, and posts the setup summary to Slack so the team can finalize delegation.

templates.title: DNS record bulk importer
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads a table of DNS records — name, type, content, TTL — validates each row, creates or updates the matching record in Cloudflare, and writes results back to the table so DNS changes are versioned and reviewable.

templates.title: Zone settings policy enforcer
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that reads a baseline of required Cloudflare zone settings from a knowledge base, compares it against every zone weekly, automatically reverts unauthorized changes, and emails a compliance report to security leadership.

skills.name: audit-dns-records
skills.description: Pull all DNS records for a Cloudflare zone and report on misconfigurations, dangling records, and sensitive record changes.
skills.content:
# Audit Cloudflare DNS Records

Export and review the DNS configuration for a zone to catch misconfigurations and risky records.

## Steps
1. Resolve the zone ID for the target domain.
2. List every DNS record (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS) for the zone.
3. Flag records that point to deprovisioned hosts, wildcard CNAMEs, missing SPF/DMARC TXT records, and proxied vs. unproxied mismatches.
4. Group findings by record type and severity.

## Output
A prioritized list of DNS issues with the record name, type, current value, and recommended fix.

skills.name: purge-cache
skills.description: Purge Cloudflare cache for specific URLs or an entire zone after a deploy, then confirm what was cleared.
skills.content:
# Purge Cloudflare Cache

Clear cached content so visitors see the latest deploy.

## Steps
1. Identify the affected zone and the paths or hostnames that changed.
2. Purge by specific files when possible; only purge everything for the zone if the change is global.
3. Confirm the purge succeeded and note the timestamp.

## Output
A short confirmation listing the zone, the purged URLs (or "full zone"), and the purge time.

skills.name: check-ssl-and-zone-settings
skills.description: Inspect SSL certificate status and security settings for Cloudflare zones and report drift from a desired baseline.
skills.content:
# Check SSL and Zone Settings

Verify SSL/TLS posture and key security settings across zones.

## Steps
1. List the target zones.
2. For each zone read SSL mode, certificate status/expiry, minimum TLS version, and security level.
3. Compare against the desired baseline (e.g. Full Strict, TLS 1.2+).
4. Flag expiring certs and any setting weaker than the baseline.

## Output
A per-zone table of SSL status, settings, and any drift that needs remediation.

templates.title: CloudFormation drift detector
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled daily workflow that runs drift detection on every CloudFormation stack in my AWS account, waits for detection to complete, summarizes drifted resources, logs them to a table, and posts a Slack alert when any production stack drifts.

templates.title: Stack inventory builder

templates.title: Template validator gate

Pull the template, validate it via the CloudFormation API, summarize any syntax or structural errors, and post the validation result as a PR comment to block merges on broken templates.

templates.title: Stack failure investigator

templates.title: Template archive and search

templates.title: Resource change report

templates.title: Pre-deploy drift gate
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that runs before a deploy, initiates drift detection on the target CloudFormation stack, polls until drift detection completes, and either approves the deploy or blocks it with a Slack alert explaining the drifted resources.

skills.name: detect-stack-drift
skills.description: Run drift detection on CloudFormation stacks and summarize resources whose live config no longer matches the template.
skills.content:
# Detect CloudFormation Stack Drift

Find resources that have been changed outside of CloudFormation.

## Steps
1. List the target stacks (or accept a specific stack name).
2. Initiate drift detection for each stack and poll until detection completes.
3. Pull the drift results and isolate resources with status DRIFTED or DELETED.
4. For each drifted resource, summarize the property differences.

## Output
A per-stack drift report listing each drifted resource, its type, and the specific properties that differ from the template.

skills.name: inventory-stacks
skills.description: List CloudFormation stacks with their status, region, and resources to build a single inventory of deployed infrastructure.
skills.content:
# Inventory CloudFormation Stacks

Build a unified view of all deployed stacks.

## Steps
1. List every stack and capture name, status, creation/update time, and region.
2. For each stack, describe its resources and count them by type.
3. Highlight stacks in failed or rollback states.

## Output
A table of stacks with status, region, resource count, and any stacks needing attention.

skills.name: investigate-stack-failure
skills.description: Pull recent CloudFormation stack events to diagnose a failed create, update, or rollback and explain the root cause.
skills.content:
# Investigate CloudFormation Stack Failure

Diagnose why a stack operation failed.

## Steps
1. Describe the target stack and confirm its current status.
2. Pull recent stack events, ordered newest first.
3. Find the first FAILED event and read its resource status reason.
4. Trace any dependent resource failures that cascaded from it.

## Output
A plain-English root-cause summary naming the failing resource, the error reason, and a suggested fix.

templates.title: CloudWatch alarm digest
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled daily workflow that summarizes the past 24 hours of CloudWatch alarms by service and severity, identifies repeat offenders, and posts a digest to Slack.

templates.title: CloudWatch log triage
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that runs CloudWatch Logs Insights queries hourly for error patterns, clusters matches, writes top groups to a triage table, and pings the on-call engineer.

templates.title: CloudWatch cost-control alerts
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that pulls CloudWatch billing alarms daily, projects month-end spend by service, and posts an alert when projection exceeds budget thresholds.

templates.title: CloudWatch incident scribe

templates.title: CloudWatch SLO burn-rate watcher

templates.title: CloudWatch metric archiver
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that exports CloudWatch metric snapshots into S3 long-term storage, preserving granularity for compliance, and writing a manifest table.

templates.title: CloudWatch log error triager
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that runs a CloudWatch Logs Insights query against application log groups every few minutes, groups recurring error signatures with an agent, opens a Linear issue for any new error pattern, and posts a Slack alert.

templates.title: CodePipeline rollback brake
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches CloudWatch alarms after a deployment, and when an error-rate alarm fires while a CodePipeline execution is in progress, stops the execution with a reason and notifies the release channel.

templates.title: DynamoDB hot-partition watcher
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that pulls DynamoDB CloudWatch metrics, identifies hot partitions and throttled requests, and writes the report to a Slack channel with mitigation suggestions.

skills.name: investigate-error-spike
skills.description: Run a CloudWatch Logs Insights query to find and summarize error spikes in a log group over a time window.
skills.content:
# Investigate CloudWatch Error Spike

Find the cause of an error spike using Logs Insights.

## Steps
1. Identify the relevant log group and the time window to investigate.
2. Run a Logs Insights query that filters for error or exception lines and aggregates by error type.
3. Pull representative sample log events for the top error groups.
4. Correlate timing with any recent deploys or traffic changes.

## Output
A summary of the top error types, their counts, sample messages, and the likely cause.

skills.name: check-metric-health
skills.description: Pull CloudWatch metric statistics for a resource and report whether key metrics are within healthy ranges.
skills.content:
# Check CloudWatch Metric Health

Review key metrics for a resource against expected thresholds.

## Steps
1. Identify the namespace, metric names, and dimensions for the resource (e.g. CPUUtilization, latency, error rate).
2. Get metric statistics over the chosen window with an appropriate period and statistic (Average, p99, Sum).
3. Compare values against healthy thresholds.

## Output
A per-metric summary with the current value, trend, and whether it is within a healthy range.

skills.name: review-alarm-state
skills.description: List CloudWatch alarms, report which are in ALARM or INSUFFICIENT_DATA, and optionally mute noisy alarms.
skills.content:
# Review CloudWatch Alarm State

Get a snapshot of alarm health across the account.

## Steps
1. Describe alarms and group them by state (OK, ALARM, INSUFFICIENT_DATA).
2. For alarms in ALARM, capture the metric, threshold, and reason.
3. If asked, mute alarms that are known-noisy during a maintenance window and note them.

## Output
A list of alarms currently firing or missing data, with the metric and threshold for each.

skills.name: approve-pending-deployment
skills.description: Find a pending CodePipeline manual approval, summarize the change, and approve or reject it.
skills.content:
# Approve Pending CodePipeline Deployment

Handle a manual approval gate in a pipeline.

## Steps
1. Get the pipeline state and locate the action awaiting approval (status InProgress on a manual approval action) and its approval token.
2. Pull the execution details for the stage to summarize what is being deployed (source revisions, trigger).
3. Submit the approval result with the token, the Approved or Rejected decision, and a summary explaining the decision.

## Output
The decision that was submitted, the approval summary, and the pipeline/stage/action it applied to.

skills.name: investigate-failed-pipeline
skills.description: Find the failing stage and action of a CodePipeline execution and report the error details.
skills.content:
# Investigate Failed CodePipeline Execution

Diagnose why a pipeline run failed.

## Steps
1. List recent executions for the pipeline and identify the failed one (or use the provided execution ID).
2. Get the pipeline state and find the stage and action with a Failed status.
3. Capture the action error code, error message, and external execution URL, plus the source revisions that were being deployed.

## Output
The failing stage and action, the error details, the commit/revision involved, and a link to the external execution.

skills.name: trigger-pipeline-release
skills.description: Start a CodePipeline execution, optionally with variable overrides, and report the execution ID.
skills.content:
# Trigger CodePipeline Release

Kick off a pipeline run.

## Steps
1. Confirm the pipeline name (list pipelines if unsure).
2. Start the execution, passing any pipeline variable overrides (e.g. version or environment) and an idempotency token if retries are possible.
3. Optionally poll the pipeline state to confirm the execution entered the first stage.

## Output
The pipeline execution ID that was started and the variables it ran with.

skills.name: retry-failed-stage
skills.description: Retry the failed actions of a CodePipeline stage and confirm the stage re-entered execution.
skills.content:
# Retry Failed CodePipeline Stage

Re-run a failed stage without restarting the whole pipeline.

## Steps
1. Get the pipeline state and identify the failed stage and the execution ID stuck in it.
2. Retry the stage with FAILED_ACTIONS mode (or ALL_ACTIONS if the whole stage should re-run).
3. Check the pipeline state again to confirm the stage is InProgress.

## Output
The stage that was retried, the retry mode used, and the current stage status.

templates.title: Incident response coordinator
templates.prompt: Create a knowledge base connected to my Confluence or Notion with runbooks and incident procedures. skills.name: publish-meeting-notes
skills.description: Create a Confluence page with structured meeting notes including attendees, decisions, and action items in the right space.
skills.content:
# Publish Meeting Notes to Confluence

Turn raw meeting notes into a clean, structured Confluence page.

## Steps
1. Confirm the target space and any parent page.
2. Structure the notes into sections: attendees, agenda, decisions, and action items with owners.
3. Create the page with a clear, dated title.
4. Return the page URL.

## Output
A confirmation with the new page title and link, plus the list of action items captured.

skills.name: update-doc-page
skills.description: Read an existing Confluence page, apply updates, and save it back, respecting version control to avoid conflicts.
skills.content:
# Update a Confluence Page

Safely edit an existing documentation page.

## Steps
1. Read the target page to get its current content and version number.
2. Apply the requested changes to the body, preserving existing structure and formatting.
3. Update the page, incrementing the version number by one to avoid optimistic-locking conflicts.
4. If the update fails on a version conflict, re-read and retry.

## Output
A confirmation of the updated page with its new version number and link.

skills.name: search-knowledge
skills.description: Search Confluence content for a topic and summarize the most relevant pages with links for quick reference.
skills.content:
# Search Confluence Knowledge

Find and summarize documentation on a topic.

## Steps
1. Search content using the topic keywords, optionally scoped to a space.
2. Read the top matching pages.
3. Summarize what each page covers and how it relates to the question.

## Output
A short briefing answering the question, with links to the source pages cited.

skills.name: collect-page-feedback
skills.description: List and summarize comments on a Confluence page so you can triage feedback and open questions.
skills.content:
# Collect Confluence Page Feedback

Gather and organize comments left on a page.

## Steps
1. Read the target page to confirm its identity.
2. List all comments on the page.
3. Group comments into themes: questions, corrections, and approvals.

## Output
A digest of comment themes with any unresolved questions flagged for follow-up.

templates.title: Convex support ticket triage

templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that runs each night, pages through every Convex table with List Documents, writes the exported JSON to S3 with date partitions, and records the run in an audit table.

skills.name: run-convex-function
skills.description: Run a Convex query, mutation, or action with named arguments and use its result.
skills.content:
# Run a Convex Function

Call a function deployed to Convex and work with its return value.

## Steps
1. Pick the operation that matches the function type: Run Query for reads, Run Mutation for writes, Run Action for side effects like calling external APIs.
2. Provide the Deployment URL (https://your-deployment.convex.cloud) and a deploy key from the dashboard Settings page.
3. Set Function Path in module:function form, for example messages:list or tasks/admin:reset.
4. Pass Function Arguments as a JSON object whose keys match the argument names the function declares, for example {"limit": 10}.

## Output
The function result is available as value, with any console output in logLines. Surface the fields downstream steps need.

skills.name: export-convex-table
skills.description: Page through a full Convex table snapshot with List Documents until hasMore is false.
skills.content:
# Export a Convex Table

Read every document in a table using snapshot pagination so the export is consistent.

## Steps
1. Use the List Documents operation with the deployment URL, deploy key, and the table name (leave empty to export all tables).
2. On the first call leave Snapshot and Cursor empty; the response pins a snapshot timestamp.
3. While hasMore is true, call List Documents again passing back the returned snapshot and pageCursor values.
4. Collect the documents arrays from each page into your destination.

## Output
A complete, point-in-time set of documents for the table, each including _id and _creationTime.

skills.name: sync-convex-changes
skills.description: Fetch only changed Convex documents since a snapshot using Document Deltas.
skills.content:
# Sync Convex Changes Incrementally

After an initial export, keep a downstream copy fresh by reading only what changed.

## Steps
1. Run an initial export with List Documents and keep the final snapshot value.
2. On each sync run, call Document Deltas with that value as the Cursor (and optionally a table name).
3. While hasMore is true, keep calling Document Deltas with the returned cursor; persist the last cursor for the next run.
4. Apply each document by _id; documents with _deleted set to true should be removed downstream.

## Output
The changed documents since the stored cursor plus a new cursor to persist, giving reliable incremental sync when documents are applied idempotently by _id.

skills.name: audit-identity-sensors

skills.content:
# Audit CrowdStrike Identity Sensors

Review Identity Protection sensor coverage across the fleet.

## Steps
1. Query sensors, optionally filtered by status or hostname.
2. For sensors of interest, pull detailed attributes (version, last seen, assigned policy).

A coverage report listing healthy sensors, plus any that are offline, stale, or misconfigured for SOC review.

skills.name: summarize-sensor-aggregates
skills.description: Pull documented CrowdStrike sensor aggregates and summarize the fleet distribution by version, status, or platform.
skills.content:
# Summarize CrowdStrike Sensor Aggregates

Build a high-level picture of the sensor fleet.

## Steps
1. Request the documented sensor aggregates (e.g. counts by version, status, or platform).
2. Compute the distribution and identify outliers, such as a large share of outdated versions.

skills.name: run-code-in-sandbox
skills.description: Run Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript in an isolated Daytona sandbox and return the output. Use as a safe code interpreter for computation, parsing, or data wrangling.
skills.content:
# Run Code In Sandbox

Execute code safely in an isolated Daytona sandbox.

## Steps
1. Create a sandbox with the Create Sandbox operation (or reuse an existing sandbox ID), setting an auto-stop interval so it cleans up after itself.
2. Use Run Code with the language set to python, javascript, or typescript. Print the values you need to stdout — the printed output is what comes back.
3. Check the exit code: 0 means success; on failure, read the result output for the error, fix the code, and rerun.
4. Delete the sandbox with Delete Sandbox when the work is finished if it was created just for this task.

## Output
Return the printed result and the exit code. If the run produced chart artifacts, mention them. On repeated failures, return the last error output instead of fabricating a result.

skills.name: analyze-data-file
skills.description: Upload a data file into a Daytona sandbox, analyze it with Python, and download any generated results. Use for CSV/JSON analysis that needs real computation.
skills.content:
# Analyze Data File

Process a workflow file with real code in a sandbox.

## Steps
1. Create a sandbox (or reuse one) and note its ID.
2. Use Upload File to place the data file at a known path, e.g. /home/daytona/data.csv. A trailing slash on the destination uploads into that directory under the original file name.
3. Use Run Code with Python to read the file from that path, compute the analysis, print a summary, and write any derived files (reports, charts) to known paths.
4. Use Download File to pull each derived file back into the workflow, and List Files to discover outputs if paths are dynamic.
5. Delete the sandbox when finished.

## Output
Return the printed analysis summary and the downloaded result files. Name the exact sandbox paths used so the run can be reproduced.

skills.name: clone-repo-and-run-checks
skills.description: Clone a Git repository into a Daytona sandbox and run install, build, or test commands. Use for CI-style checks, repo health monitoring, or validating changes.
skills.content:
# Clone Repo And Run Checks

Run repository checks in an isolated environment.

## Steps
1. Create a sandbox sized for the job (set CPU and memory in advanced options for heavy builds).
2. Use Git Clone with the repository URL and a clone path like /home/daytona/repo. Pass a branch for non-default branches, and a username plus token for private repositories.
3. Use Execute Command from the clone path (set the working directory) to run installs, builds, or tests. Raise the timeout for long commands — the default is 10 seconds.
4. Inspect each exit code and capture the output of failing commands.
5. Delete the sandbox when the checks complete.

## Output
Return pass/fail per command with exit codes, and include the failing output verbatim when something breaks.

skills.name: manage-sandbox-fleet

# Manage Sandbox Fleet

Audit and clean up sandboxes in the organization.

## Steps
1. Use List Sandboxes to enumerate sandboxes; filter by name prefix or labels, and page with the cursor when there are many.
2. Inspect each sandbox state and timestamps to find ones idle or running longer than expected.
3. Stop Sandbox for environments worth keeping but not actively used; Delete Sandbox for disposable ones (e.g. labeled temporary).
4. When creating sandboxes elsewhere, set auto-stop and auto-delete intervals so cleanup happens automatically.

## Output
Return a summary of sandboxes found, which were stopped or deleted and why, and any that were left running with their states.

skills.name: send-contract-for-signature
skills.description: Send a document to one or more signers for e-signature, using a DocuSign template or an uploaded file.
skills.content:
# Send Contract for Signature

Send a document out for e-signature through DocuSign and confirm it was delivered.

## Steps
1. Determine whether to send from a template (preferred for standard agreements) or from an uploaded document. If a template is named, use List Templates to resolve its ID.
2. For a template, call Send from Template with the template ID and a template-roles JSON array mapping each role name to a signer name and email. For an ad-hoc document, call Send Envelope with the email subject, signer name, signer email, and the document file.
3. Add any CC recipients and set the email subject to something the signer will recognize.
4. Send immediately unless asked to save as a draft.

## Output
Report the envelope ID and status. List each signer and CC recipient with their email so the requester can confirm the right people were addressed.

skills.name: track-pending-envelopes
skills.description: List envelopes awaiting signature, identify ones stalled past a threshold, and surface who still needs to sign.
skills.content:
# Track Pending Envelopes

Find DocuSign envelopes that are sent but not yet completed so stalled signatures can be chased.

## Steps
1. Call List Envelopes filtered to sent and delivered status over a recent date window.
2. For each envelope, use List Recipients to see which signers have signed and which are still outstanding.
3. Compute how long each envelope has been waiting and flag any past the requested threshold (default 48 hours).

## Output
Return a table of stalled envelopes: envelope ID, subject, days waiting, and the outstanding signer name and email. Sort by longest waiting first.

skills.name: archive-completed-documents
skills.description: Find completed envelopes, download the signed PDFs, and extract key metadata for archiving.
skills.content:
# Archive Completed Documents

Collect signed documents once an envelope is complete and capture their metadata.

## Steps
1. Call List Envelopes filtered to completed status over the requested date window.
2. For each completed envelope, call Download Document with "combined" to get the full signed PDF.
3. Record the envelope ID, subject, completed date, and signer list for each document.

## Output
Return each completed envelope with its downloaded file, signers, and completed date. Note any envelope where the download failed so it can be retried.

skills.name: void-stale-envelope
skills.description: Void an envelope that should no longer be signed and record the reason.
skills.content:
# Void Stale Envelope

Cancel a DocuSign envelope that is no longer valid — wrong recipient, superseded terms, or expired offer.

## Steps
1. Confirm the envelope ID. If only a subject or signer is known, use List Envelopes to resolve it, and verify it is not already completed.
2. Call Get Envelope to confirm the current status is still voidable (created, sent, or delivered).
3. Call Void Envelope with a clear void reason describing why it is being cancelled.

## Output
Confirm the envelope ID, its new voided status, and the recorded reason. If the envelope was already completed or voided, report that instead of attempting to void it.

skills.name: upload-file-to-dropbox
skills.description: Upload a file to a specific Dropbox path and optionally generate a shareable link.
skills.content:
# Upload File to Dropbox

Save a file into Dropbox at a chosen location and optionally share it.

## Steps
1. Determine the destination path, including the filename and extension (e.g., /reports/q3-summary.pdf).
2. Call Upload File with the file and destination path. Use overwrite mode only if replacing an existing file; otherwise use add and enable auto-rename to avoid clobbering.
3. If a shareable link is requested, call Create Shared Link on the uploaded path with the requested visibility (public, team-only, or password-protected).

## Output
Report the final stored path (after any auto-rename) and, if created, the shared link URL.

skills.name: find-files-in-dropbox
skills.description: Search Dropbox for files by query, extension, or folder, and return matching paths.
skills.content:
# Find Files in Dropbox

Locate files in Dropbox matching a search term or filter.

## Steps
1. Use Search Files with the query term. Scope to a folder path when the location is known, and pass file extensions (e.g., pdf,xlsx) to narrow results.
2. If browsing a known folder instead of searching, use List Folder with the folder path; enable recursive listing to include subfolders.
3. For any candidate match, use Get Metadata to confirm size, type, and last-modified time before acting on it.

## Output
Return the matching files as a list of path, name, size, and last-modified. If nothing matches, say so and suggest a broader query.

skills.name: organize-dropbox-folder
skills.description: List a folder and move, copy, or delete files to reorganize Dropbox contents.
skills.content:
# Organize Dropbox Folder

Reorganize files in Dropbox by moving them into the right folders.

## Steps
1. Call List Folder on the source path to enumerate the files to process.
2. Decide each file destination based on the requested rules (by type, date, campaign, or naming pattern). Create target folders with Create Folder if they do not exist.
3. Use Move File/Folder to relocate each file, or Copy File/Folder when the original must stay in place. Enable auto-rename to avoid conflicts.

## Output
Return a summary of every file moved or copied with its old and new path, and flag any operation that failed.

skills.name: share-dropbox-link
skills.description: Create a shared link for a Dropbox file or folder with controlled visibility and expiration.
skills.content:
# Share Dropbox Link

Generate a shareable link for an existing Dropbox item with the right access controls.

## Steps
1. Confirm the exact path of the file or folder. Use Get Metadata to verify it exists.
2. Call Create Shared Link with the path and the requested visibility — public for anyone, team-only for internal sharing, or password-protected with a supplied password.
3. Set an expiration date if the link should not be permanent.

## Output
Return the shared link URL, its visibility setting, and the expiration date if one was applied.

skills.name: run-dspy-prediction
skills.description: Call a self-hosted DSPy Predict program to get a structured output from an input.
skills.content:
# Run DSPy Prediction

Send input to a self-hosted DSPy Predict program and return its structured answer.

## Steps
1. Confirm the DSPy server base URL and, if required, the API key.
2. Choose the Predict operation and supply the input text. Set the input field name only if the program signature expects something other than the default.
3. Pass any extra signature fields as an additional-inputs JSON object.

## Output
Return the program answer and any structured fields it produced. If the server returns a non-success status, surface the status and the raw output for debugging.

skills.name: reason-with-chain-of-thought
skills.description: Use a DSPy Chain of Thought program to answer a question with explicit reasoning.
skills.content:
# Reason with Chain of Thought

Answer a question through a self-hosted DSPy Chain of Thought program that exposes its reasoning.

## Steps
1. Confirm the DSPy server base URL and API key if needed.
2. Choose the Chain of Thought operation and supply the question. Add any background as context.
3. Run the program and capture both the answer and the reasoning trace.

## Output
Return the final answer plus the reasoning rationale so the requester can audit how the conclusion was reached.

skills.name: run-dspy-react-agent
skills.description: Run a DSPy ReAct agent on a task that requires multi-step tool use, and capture its trajectory.
skills.content:
# Run DSPy ReAct Agent

Execute a task with a self-hosted DSPy ReAct agent that interleaves reasoning and actions.

## Steps
1. Confirm the DSPy server base URL and API key if needed.
2. Choose the ReAct operation and describe the task clearly. Set a max-iterations cap to bound how many reasoning-action cycles run.
3. Provide any needed context, then execute the agent.

## Output
Return the final answer and the step-by-step trajectory (thoughts, actions, observations). If the agent hit the iteration cap without finishing, note that and summarize the last state.

skills.name: create-tracked-short-link
skills.description: Create a Dub short link for a destination URL with UTM parameters and an optional custom slug.
skills.content:
# Create Tracked Short Link

Turn a long destination URL into a branded, trackable Dub short link.

## Steps
1. Take the destination URL and any campaign metadata (source, medium, campaign name).
2. Call Create Link with the URL. Set the UTM source, medium, and campaign fields so clicks attribute correctly, and set a custom slug when a memorable link is wanted.
3. Add a custom domain, title, or tag IDs if the request specifies them.

## Output
Return the full short link URL, its slug, the destination, and the QR code URL. Confirm which UTM parameters were applied.

skills.name: report-link-analytics
skills.description: Pull Dub click, lead, and sales analytics for a link or campaign over a time window.
skills.content:
# Report Link Analytics

Summarize how a Dub short link or campaign is performing.

## Steps
1. Choose the Get Analytics operation. Set the event type (clicks, leads, sales, or composite) the request cares about.
2. Scope to a specific link via link ID or external ID, or to a domain for a whole campaign. Set the interval (e.g., 7d, 30d) or explicit start and end dates.
3. Set group-by to break results down by country, device, referrer, or top links when a breakdown is asked for; otherwise use count for totals.

## Output
Report the headline metrics (clicks, leads, sales, revenue) and, when grouped, the top segments. Call out notable winners and decliners versus the prior period when comparison data is available.

skills.name: batch-create-campaign-links
skills.description: Upsert a Dub short link for each row in a list of destinations with consistent UTM tagging.
skills.content:
# Batch Create Campaign Links

Generate consistent tracked links for many destinations at once.

## Steps
1. For each destination URL in the list, build the UTM parameters and slug from the row data so tagging is uniform across the batch.
2. Use Upsert Link (keyed on external ID or slug) so re-runs refresh rather than duplicate existing links.
3. Collect the resulting short link for each row.

## Output
Return a table mapping each destination to its short link and external ID. Report how many links were created versus refreshed, and flag any rows that failed.

skills.name: audit-existing-links
skills.description: List Dub links and check each destination for broken or stale URLs to flag for cleanup.
skills.content:
# Audit Existing Links

Review existing Dub links to catch broken or outdated destinations.

## Steps
1. Call List Links, optionally filtered by domain or tag IDs, paginating until all links are retrieved.
2. For each link, inspect the destination URL and check it for 4xx or 5xx responses or obviously stale targets.
3. Note links with low or zero clicks over a long period as candidates for archiving.

## Output
Return a remediation list: short link, destination, detected issue (broken, redirecting, stale), and a suggested action. Sort broken links first.

skills.name: answer-with-duckduckgo
skills.description: Search DuckDuckGo for a quick instant answer or abstract on a topic and return it with its source.
skills.content:
# Answer with DuckDuckGo

Get a fast, privacy-preserving answer to a factual question using DuckDuckGo Instant Answers.

## Steps
1. Form a concise query from the question. Enable Remove HTML so returned text is clean.
2. Run the search and read the instant answer, abstract, and abstract source.
3. If the result is a disambiguation page rather than a direct answer, refine the query to be more specific and search again.

## Output
Return the answer or abstract text along with the source name and URL so the claim is attributable. If no instant answer exists, say so and surface the related topics instead.

skills.name: gather-related-topics
skills.description: Use DuckDuckGo to collect related topics and external links around a subject for research.
skills.content:
# Gather Related Topics

Build a quick research starting point on a subject using DuckDuckGo.

## Steps
1. Search the subject with Remove HTML enabled.
2. Collect the heading, abstract, related topics, and any external link results.
3. Group the related topics into themes and pick the most authoritative links to explore further.

## Output
Return the abstract summary plus a list of related topics and external links, each with its URL, organized by theme.

skills.name: validate-claim-online
skills.description: Check a stated claim against DuckDuckGo results to confirm or flag it as unsupported.
skills.content:
# Validate Claim Online

Verify whether a claim is supported by public web sources via DuckDuckGo.

## Steps
1. Turn the claim into a focused search query and run it with Remove HTML enabled.
2. Compare the instant answer, abstract, and source against the claim.
3. Decide whether the result supports, contradicts, or is silent on the claim.

## Output
Return a verdict — supported, contradicted, or unverified — with the source name and URL. If unverified, recommend a more targeted query or a dedicated source.

skills.name: search-elasticsearch-index
skills.description: Run a query against an Elasticsearch index and return the matching documents.
skills.content:
# Search Elasticsearch Index

Query an index and return the relevant documents.

## Steps
1. Confirm the connection details (host or cloud ID and auth) and the target index name.
2. Choose the Search operation and build the query DSL — match for full-text, term for exact values, range for numeric or date bounds, and bool to combine clauses.
3. Set size and offset for paging, add a sort spec when ordering matters, and use source includes/excludes to trim returned fields.

## Output
Return the matching hits with their _id, _score, and relevant _source fields, plus the total count and query time. If nothing matched, report zero hits and suggest loosening the query.

skills.name: index-document
skills.description: Add or update a document in an Elasticsearch index.
skills.content:
# Index Document

Write a document into an Elasticsearch index so it becomes searchable.

## Steps
1. Confirm the connection details and target index.
2. Build the document as a JSON object with appropriate field types. Choose the Index Document operation; supply a document ID to upsert a known record, or omit it to let Elasticsearch auto-generate one.
3. To change only specific fields of an existing document, use Update Document with a partial document and the document ID instead.
4. Set the refresh policy to immediate or wait-for when the write must be searchable right away.

## Output
Return the resulting _id, _version, and the operation result (created or updated).

skills.name: bulk-load-documents
skills.description: Index, update, or delete many Elasticsearch documents in a single bulk request.
skills.content:
# Bulk Load Documents

Apply many document operations to Elasticsearch efficiently in one call.

## Steps
1. Confirm the connection details and target index.
2. Assemble the operations as NDJSON: an action line (index, create, update, or delete) followed by the document line where required.
3. Run the Bulk Operations call and set a refresh policy if the data must be immediately searchable.

## Output
Report whether any errors occurred and summarize the per-item results — how many succeeded versus failed and the reason for any failures.

skills.name: check-cluster-health
skills.description: Report Elasticsearch cluster health and key index statistics.
skills.content:
# Check Cluster Health

Assess the health of an Elasticsearch deployment.

## Steps
1. Confirm the connection details.
2. Call Cluster Health to get the overall status (green, yellow, red) and node count. Optionally wait for a target status.
3. Use List Indices and Get Index Info to spot oversized, unassigned, or unhealthy indices, and Cluster Stats for storage and shard totals.

## Output
Report the cluster status, number of nodes, and any indices that look problematic. If status is yellow or red, explain the likely cause (e.g., unassigned replicas) and what to check next.

skills.name: narrate-text-to-speech
skills.description: Convert a block of text into natural-sounding speech audio with a chosen ElevenLabs voice.
skills.content:
# Narrate Text to Speech

Generate spoken audio from text using ElevenLabs.

## Steps
1. Take the text to narrate and confirm the target voice ID (ask for one if not provided).
2. Pick a model — use a multilingual model for non-English or mixed-language text, or a turbo/flash model when low latency matters.
3. For consistent delivery, set stability higher; for more expressive variation, set it lower. Raise similarity boost to stay closer to the reference voice.

## Output
Return the generated audio file and its URL. Confirm the voice and model used so the requester can adjust if the delivery is not right.

skills.name: narrate-article-as-audio
skills.description: Turn a long article or blog post into a podcast-style audio narration.
skills.content:
# Narrate Article as Audio

Produce a listenable audio version of written content.

## Steps
1. Clean the source text — strip markdown, navigation, and boilerplate so only the readable prose remains. Expand abbreviations the voice should speak in full.
2. Choose a voice ID suited to the content and a high-quality multilingual model for natural delivery.
3. Convert the cleaned text to speech, keeping stability moderate so the narration sounds engaging but consistent.

## Output
Return the audio file and a player-ready URL, along with the voice used. If the text is very long, note any truncation and suggest splitting it into parts.

skills.name: generate-voice-prompt
skills.description: Generate a short branded voice clip such as an IVR prompt, greeting, or notification.
skills.content:
# Generate Voice Prompt

Create a short, polished voice clip for things like phone menus, greetings, or alerts.

## Steps
1. Take the exact script for the prompt. Keep it concise and confirm pronunciation of any names or numbers.
2. Select a consistent brand voice ID so every prompt sounds the same.
3. Set stability high for a steady, professional delivery and convert the script to speech.

## Output
Return the audio file and its URL. When generating a set of prompts, list each clip with its script so they can be wired into the phone tree or app.

skills.name: add-leads-to-campaign
skills.description: Create leads in Email Bison and attach them to an outbound campaign with personalization variables.
skills.content:
# Add Leads to Campaign

Load prospects into Email Bison and enroll them in a campaign.

## Steps
1. Confirm the instance URL and target campaign. If only a campaign name is known, use List Campaigns to resolve its ID.
2. For each prospect, call Create Lead with first name, last name, email, and any title or company. Pass personalization fields as a custom-variables JSON array (e.g., linkedin_url, first_line).
3. Collect the new lead IDs and call Attach Leads to Campaign with the campaign ID and those IDs.

## Output
Report how many leads were created and attached, list any duplicates or invalid emails that were skipped, and confirm the campaign they were added to.

skills.name: triage-campaign-replies
skills.description: Pull recent Email Bison replies, classify each by intent, and tag the lead accordingly.
skills.content:
# Triage Campaign Replies

Process inbound replies to outbound campaigns and route them.

## Steps
1. Call List Replies, optionally scoped to a campaign, sender email, or the inbox folder, and filter to unread when only new replies matter.
2. Classify each reply as interested, not interested, objection, out-of-office, or auto-reply based on its content.
3. Resolve or create the matching tag with List Tags / Create Tag, then call Attach Tags to Leads to label the lead by intent.

## Output
Return each reply with its lead, classification, and the tag applied. Highlight interested replies so a rep can follow up first.

skills.name: manage-campaign-status
skills.description: Pause, resume, or archive an Email Bison campaign and adjust its sending settings.
skills.content:
# Manage Campaign Status

Control whether an Email Bison campaign is actively sending and tune its limits.

## Steps
1. Confirm the campaign ID (resolve via List Campaigns if only a name is given).
2. Call Update Campaign Status with pause, resume, or archive as requested.
3. To adjust throughput or behavior, call Update Campaign to change max emails per day, max new leads per day, sequence prioritization, or tracking settings.

## Output
Confirm the campaign new status and any sending settings that changed. Note the prior values so the change can be reverted if needed.

skills.name: report-campaign-performance
skills.description: Summarize Email Bison campaign performance — sends, opens, replies, and positive reply rate.
skills.content:
# Report Campaign Performance

Produce a performance snapshot across Email Bison campaigns.

## Steps
1. Call List Campaigns to get the active campaigns and their stats.
2. For reply-level detail, call List Replies per campaign and tally interested versus total to compute positive reply rate.
3. Rank campaigns by reply rate and identify top and bottom performers.

## Output
Return a digest: per-campaign sends, opens, replies, and positive reply rate, with the best and worst performers called out and a one-line takeaway for each.

skills.name: embed-text
skills.description: Generate an OpenAI embedding vector for a piece of text to use in semantic search or similarity.
skills.content:
# Embed Text

Convert text into an OpenAI embedding vector.

## Steps
1. Take the input text. If it is long, ensure it fits the model context; otherwise chunk it first.
2. Choose the model — text-embedding-3-small for cost-efficient general use or text-embedding-3-large for higher accuracy. Keep the model consistent with any existing vectors it will be compared against.
3. Generate the embedding.

## Output
Return the embedding vector, the model used, and token usage. Note the vector dimensionality so it can be matched to the destination vector index.

skills.name: embed-documents-for-retrieval
skills.description: Chunk and embed a set of documents so they can be upserted into a vector store for retrieval.
skills.content:
# Embed Documents for Retrieval

Prepare documents for semantic retrieval by chunking and embedding them.

## Steps
1. Split each document into reasonably sized chunks with light overlap so context is preserved.
2. Embed each chunk with a single consistent OpenAI model (e.g., text-embedding-3-small).
3. Pair each vector with its source metadata (document ID, chunk index, title) ready for upsert into the vector store.

## Output
Return the embeddings with their associated metadata and the model used. Report how many chunks were produced and flag any chunk that failed to embed.

skills.name: find-semantic-duplicates
skills.description: Embed items and compare vectors by cosine similarity to flag near-duplicate content.
skills.content:
# Find Semantic Duplicates

Detect items that mean the same thing even when worded differently.

## Steps
1. Embed each candidate item with the same OpenAI model used for the existing set.
2. Compare each new vector against existing vectors using cosine similarity.
3. Flag pairs above a similarity threshold (e.g., 0.9) as likely duplicates; treat lower scores as distinct.

## Output
Return the flagged duplicate pairs with their similarity scores, sorted highest first, so they can be merged or deduplicated.

skills.description: Enrich a person from their email address — name, role, company, social profiles, and more.
skills.content:
# Enrich Contact from Email

Turn an email address into a full contact profile using Enrich.so.

## Steps
1. Take the email address. Choose Email to Profile for a full enrichment, or Email to Person (Lite) for a fast, cheaper lookup.
2. Enable fresh-data fetch when up-to-date info matters more than speed.
3. Read back name, current title, company, location, and any LinkedIn or social URLs.

## Output
Return the enriched fields in a clean object. Note which fields could not be resolved so downstream steps know what is missing, and report remaining credits if relevant.

skills.name: find-and-verify-work-email
skills.description: Find a prospect work email from a name and company or LinkedIn URL, then verify deliverability.
skills.content:
# Find and Verify Work Email

Locate a reliable work email for a prospect and confirm it is safe to send to.

## Steps
1. If you have a name and company domain, use Find Email. If you have a LinkedIn profile URL, use LinkedIn to Work Email instead.
2. Run Verify Email on the returned address to check deliverability, and Disposable Email Check to rule out throwaway domains.
3. If the work email cannot be found, optionally fall back to LinkedIn to Personal Email when appropriate.

## Output
Return the discovered email, its verification status (valid, risky, invalid), and whether it is disposable. Recommend whether the address is safe to add to outreach.

skills.name: enrich-company-firmographics
skills.description: Look up firmographic data for a company — size, industry, funding, revenue, and traffic.
skills.content:
# Enrich Company Firmographics

Build a firmographic profile for a target account using Enrich.so.

## Steps
1. Identify the company by name or domain. Use Company Lookup for core firmographics.
2. Add Company Funding & Traffic and Company Revenue for deeper financial signals when account scoring needs them.
3. If you only have a visitor IP, use IP to Company first to resolve the organization.

## Output
Return a consolidated account brief: company name, domain, industry, employee count, funding, revenue, and traffic. Flag any data points that could not be resolved.

skills.name: search-prospects
skills.description: Search Enrich.so for people or companies matching an ideal-customer-profile filter.
skills.content:
# Search Prospects

Find people or companies that match a target profile.

## Steps
1. For people, use Search People with filters like job title, industry, location, and skills. For companies, use Search Company with industry, location, and employee-size bounds.
2. To pull contacts at known accounts, use Search Company Employees with the company IDs and target job titles.
3. Page through results using the page and page-size parameters until you have enough matches.

## Output
Return the matching people or companies with their key identifying fields and any profile URLs, plus a count of total matches. Suggest tighter filters if too many or too few results come back.

skills.name: create-evernote-note
skills.description: Create a new Evernote note with a title, content, tags, and target notebook.
skills.content:
# Create Evernote Note

Save new content as a note in Evernote.

## Steps
1. Confirm the note title and content. Plain text is fine; the content is stored as ENML.
2. Choose the Create Note operation. To file it in a specific notebook, resolve the notebook GUID with List Notebooks and pass it.
3. Add comma-separated tag names so the note is findable later.

## Output
Return the new note GUID, its title, and the notebook and tags it was saved under.

skills.name: search-evernote-notes
skills.description: Search Evernote for notes matching a query and return their titles and metadata.
skills.content:
# Search Evernote Notes

Find notes across Evernote using its search grammar.

## Steps
1. Build a query using Evernote search syntax — e.g., tag:work, intitle:meeting, notebook scoping, or plain keywords.
2. Run Search Notes. Scope to a notebook GUID when the location is known, and set max results and offset to page through matches.
3. For any note you need the body of, call Get Note with its GUID and include content.

## Output
Return the matching notes with title, GUID, and notebook, plus the total match count. If a note body is needed, include its retrieved content.

skills.name: extract-note-action-items
skills.description: Read recent Evernote notes and extract action items, owners, and due dates.
skills.content:
# Extract Note Action Items

Pull tasks out of meeting notes or research notes in Evernote.

## Steps
1. Use Search Notes to find the relevant recent notes (e.g., by tag or notebook).
2. For each match, call Get Note with content to read the full body.
3. Identify action items, the responsible owner, and any due dates mentioned in the text.

## Output
Return a structured list of action items, each with its owner, due date if stated, and a link back to the source note GUID. Flag items with no clear owner.

skills.name: organize-notes-with-tags
skills.description: Create tags and apply them to Evernote notes to keep them organized.
skills.content:
# Organize Notes with Tags

Keep Evernote notes structured by tagging them consistently.

## Steps
1. Call List Tags to see existing tags and avoid duplicates. Create any missing tag with Create Tag (optionally nested under a parent tag).
2. For each note to organize, read it with Get Note if needed, decide the right tags from its content, and apply them via Update Note with the tag names.
3. Keep tag names consistent in casing and wording across notes.

## Output
Return each note GUID with the tags applied and note any new tags that were created.

skills.name: search-the-web-with-exa
skills.description: Run an Exa neural or keyword search to find high-quality web sources on a topic.
skills.content:
# Search the Web with Exa

Find authoritative web pages on a topic using Exa AI search.

## Steps
1. Use the Search operation with a clear query. Pick the search type — neural for meaning-based discovery, keyword for exact terms, or auto to let Exa decide.
2. Narrow results with include/exclude domains, a category filter (research paper, news article, company, GitHub), and published-date bounds for recency.
3. Enable include-text or include-summary so each result comes back with usable content rather than just a link.

## Output
Return the top results with title, URL, published date, and the text or summary. Note which filters were applied so the search can be tightened or broadened.

skills.name: answer-question-with-citations
skills.description: Use Exa Answer to get a direct, sourced answer to a factual question.
skills.content:
# Answer Question with Citations

Get a grounded answer to a question with supporting sources via Exa.

## Steps
1. Use the Answer operation and pass the question in natural language.
2. Enable include-text when you want the supporting passages, not just the citation URLs.
3. Review the citations to confirm the answer is well-supported before relying on it.

## Output
Return the answer text plus its citations (titles and URLs). If the citations are weak or conflicting, say so and recommend a follow-up search.

skills.name: extract-page-contents
skills.description: Use Exa Get Contents to pull clean text and summaries from a set of URLs.
skills.content:
# Extract Page Contents

Retrieve readable content from specific web pages using Exa.

## Steps
1. Use the Get Contents operation with the target URLs (comma-separated).
2. Enable include-text for full content, and supply a summary query to get a focused summary tailored to what you need.
3. To pull deeper context from a site, set a subpage count and target keywords (e.g., docs, pricing, about).

## Output
Return each URL with its extracted text or summary and any highlights. Flag any URL that could not be crawled.

skills.name: find-similar-pages
skills.description: Use Exa Find Similar Links to discover pages related to a known URL.
skills.content:
# Find Similar Pages

Discover sources similar to a reference page using Exa.

## Steps
1. Use the Find Similar Links operation with the source URL.
2. Set the number of results and enable exclude-source-domain so you get genuinely new sources, not more pages from the same site.
3. Apply a category filter or include/exclude domains to keep the discovery on-target, and enable include-text or include-summary for context.

## Output
Return the similar pages with title, URL, and a snippet or summary, ordered by relevance. Note the filters used.

skills.name: extract-invoice-fields
skills.description: Parse an uploaded invoice with Extend and return structured vendor, line item, and total fields.
skills.content:
# Extract Invoice Fields

Use Extend to turn an invoice PDF or image into structured, validated data.

## Steps
1. Take the uploaded invoice document (file upload or URL).
2. Run the Extend parser to produce structured chunks and blocks.
3. Pull the key fields: vendor name, invoice number, invoice date, due date, line items (description, quantity, unit price), subtotal, tax, and total.
4. Validate that totals add up and that required fields are present; flag any that are missing or inconsistent.

## Output
Return a clean JSON object with the extracted fields plus a list of any validation warnings. Note the page count and credits used so cost can be tracked.

skills.name: parse-document-to-markdown
skills.description: Convert a scanned or complex document into clean, LLM-ready markdown using Extend.
skills.content:
# Parse Document to Markdown

Use Extend to convert any supported document (PDF, image, or Office file) into clean markdown an agent can reason over.

## Steps
1. Take the source document and choose a chunking strategy (page, section, or document) based on how the content will be consumed.
2. Run the Extend parser with markdown output.
3. Stitch the returned chunks into a single ordered markdown document, preserving headings, tables, and lists.

## Output
Return the full markdown text plus the page count. If the document was chunked, also return the per-chunk markdown so downstream steps can process sections independently.

skills.name: classify-and-route-document
skills.description: Parse an uploaded document with Extend, identify its type, and route it to the right downstream handler.
skills.content:
# Classify and Route Document

Use Extend to read an incoming document and decide where it should go.

## Steps
1. Run the Extend parser on the uploaded document to get its text content.
2. Inspect the parsed content to classify the document type (e.g. invoice, contract, claim form, purchase order, KYC document).
3. Pull the few identifying fields needed for routing (such as document type, reference number, and amount).
4. Decide the destination queue, table, or channel based on the classification and any thresholds.

## Output
Return the detected document type, the routing decision, and the extracted routing fields. Note any document that could not be confidently classified for manual review.

skills.name: summarize-recent-meetings
skills.description: List recent Fathom meetings and produce a concise digest of decisions, owners, and action items.
skills.content:
# Summarize Recent Meetings

Use Fathom to pull recent meetings and turn them into a readable digest.

## Steps
1. List Fathom meetings, filtering by a date range (createdAfter / createdBefore) and optionally by team or recorder.
2. Request summaries and action items in the response so each meeting comes back with its recap.
3. Across the meetings, group the key decisions, commitments, and open action items by topic or owner.

## Output
Return a digest with one short section per meeting (title, date, attendees, key points) followed by a consolidated action-item list with owners. Use the pagination cursor to cover the full range if there are many meetings.

skills.name: extract-meeting-action-items
skills.description: Pull a specific Fathom meeting summary and extract a clean list of action items with owners.
skills.content:
# Extract Meeting Action Items

Use Fathom to turn a single meeting into a tracked task list.

## Steps
1. Get the meeting summary for the given recording ID.
2. Identify every commitment or next step mentioned, with the responsible owner and any stated due date.
3. If owners are unclear, fall back to the transcript to find who made each commitment.

## Output
Return a structured list of action items, each with the task description, owner, and due date (or null). Include a one-line meeting recap at the top for context.

skills.name: log-sales-call-to-crm
skills.description: Pull a Fathom call summary and CRM matches, then format a CRM-ready note with next steps.
skills.content:
# Log Sales Call to CRM

Use Fathom to capture a sales call and prepare it for the CRM.

## Steps
1. Get the summary for the meeting recording ID, including CRM matches so the linked contact or deal is known.
2. Extract the customer pain points, objections, commitments, and agreed next steps.
3. Format a concise call note suitable for logging against the matched CRM record.

## Output
Return the matched CRM contact or deal identifier, a formatted call note, and a list of follow-up next steps with owners and dates so they can be written into the CRM.

skills.name: find-verified-email
skills.description: Find a prospect verified work email from their name and company, or from a LinkedIn URL.
skills.content:
# Find Verified Email

Use Findymail to discover a deliverable work email for a prospect.

## Steps
1. If you have a name plus company domain, use Find Email From Name. If you have a LinkedIn profile URL, use Find Email From LinkedIn.
2. Findymail verifies the email at discovery time, so the returned address is already checked for deliverability.
3. Capture the contact name, email, and domain from the response.

## Output
Return the verified email, the matched contact name, and the source company domain. If no email was found, say so clearly rather than guessing an address.

skills.name: verify-email-list
skills.description: Run a list of email addresses through Findymail verification and split into deliverable and undeliverable.
skills.content:
# Verify Email List

Use Findymail to clean an email list before an outbound send.

## Steps
1. For each email address, run Verify Email.
2. Read the verified flag and the detected provider for each result.
3. Partition the list into deliverable addresses and undeliverable ones.

## Output
Return two lists: deliverable emails (with provider) and undeliverable emails. Include a short summary count so the caller knows how many were removed.

skills.name: map-company-team
skills.description: Given a company domain, find employees by job title and enrich the company profile into a team map.
skills.content:
# Map Company Team

Use Findymail to build an org map for a target account.

## Steps
1. Use Get Company Info on the domain to pull industry, size, and description.
2. Use Find Employees with the company website and a list of target job titles to pull matching people.
3. Optionally find each contact verified email or phone for the highest-priority roles.

## Output
Return the company profile plus a list of employees (name, job title, LinkedIn URL, and email where available), grouped by function so the account team can see the buying committee.

skills.name: enrich-from-email
skills.description: Reverse-lookup an email address with Findymail to recover the full LinkedIn profile and current company.
skills.content:
# Enrich From Email

Use Findymail to turn a bare email address into a full contact record.

## Steps
1. Run Reverse Email Lookup on the email, requesting the full profile.
2. Pull the full name, headline, job title, location, current company, and profile details.
3. Optionally call Get Company Info on the recovered company domain for firmographics.

## Output
Return a structured contact record: name, title, company, location, LinkedIn URL, and the original email. Note any fields the lookup could not resolve.

skills.name: scrape-page-to-markdown
skills.description: Scrape a single URL with Firecrawl and return clean main-content markdown for an agent to read.
skills.content:
# Scrape Page to Markdown

Use Firecrawl to fetch a web page as clean, LLM-ready markdown.

## Steps
1. Use the Scrape operation on the target URL.
2. Enable Only Main Content to strip navigation, ads, and footers; set a Wait For delay if the page renders content with JavaScript.
3. Return the markdown output and capture page metadata (title, description).

## Output
Return the page markdown plus key metadata. If the page failed to load or returned empty content, report that instead of fabricating text.

skills.name: extract-structured-data
skills.description: Pull structured fields from one or more URLs using Firecrawl Extract with a prompt or schema.
skills.content:
# Extract Structured Data

Use Firecrawl to extract specific fields from web pages.

## Steps
1. Use the Extract operation with the list of target URLs.
2. Provide a clear extraction prompt describing exactly what to pull (for example product name, price, and description).
3. Run the extraction and read the structured data from the response.

## Output
Return the extracted records as structured JSON. List the source URLs and flag any URL that yielded no data.

skills.name: crawl-site
skills.description: Crawl an entire site or section with Firecrawl and return the page content for indexing or analysis.
skills.content:
# Crawl Site

Use Firecrawl to traverse a site and collect its pages.

## Steps
1. Use the Crawl operation on the root URL, setting a sensible page Limit to control cost.
2. Enable Only Main Content so each page comes back as clean markdown.
3. Collect the crawled pages and their URLs from the response.

## Output
Return the list of crawled pages with their URL and markdown content, plus the total page count. This output is ready to chunk and embed into a knowledge base.

skills.name: research-with-search
skills.description: Run a web search with Firecrawl, then scrape the top results into a cited research brief.
skills.content:
# Research With Search

Use Firecrawl to gather and synthesize web sources on a topic.

## Steps
1. Use the Search operation with the research query and a result Limit.
2. For the most relevant results, use Scrape to pull the full page markdown.
3. Synthesize the findings into a brief, attributing each claim to its source URL.

## Output
Return a structured research brief with key findings and a Sources list of the URLs used. Keep claims grounded in the scraped content.

skills.name: summarize-meeting-transcript
skills.description: Fetch a Fireflies transcript and produce a structured recap with decisions, action items, and owners.
skills.content:
# Summarize Meeting Transcript

Use Fireflies to turn a recorded meeting into a clean recap.

## Steps
1. Get the transcript for the given transcript ID (or pick the latest from List Transcripts).
2. Read the sentences and any provided summary to identify the main topics discussed.
3. Extract key decisions, action items with owners, and notable questions or risks.

## Output
Return a structured recap: a short overview, a bulleted list of decisions, and an action-item table (task, owner, due date). Keep it grounded in the transcript content.

skills.name: extract-action-items
skills.description: Pull a Fireflies transcript and extract a clean list of action items with owners and due dates.
skills.content:
# Extract Action Items

Use Fireflies to capture follow-ups from a meeting.

## Steps
1. Get the transcript for the meeting by its transcript ID.
2. Scan the sentences for commitments, assignments, and next steps.
3. Attribute each item to the speaker who owns it and capture any stated deadline.

## Output
Return a list of action items, each with the task, owner, and due date (or null). Add a one-line meeting summary at the top for context.

skills.name: create-meeting-soundbite
skills.description: Create a Fireflies soundbite (bite) clipping a key moment from a transcript for sharing.
skills.content:
# Create Meeting Soundbite

Use Fireflies to clip and share a highlight from a recorded meeting.

## Steps
1. Get the transcript and find the start and end timestamps of the moment to clip.
2. Use Create Bite with the transcript ID and the chosen time range.
3. Confirm the bite was created and capture its identifier or link.

## Output
Return the soundbite identifier or shareable link plus a short caption describing the clipped moment.

skills.name: generate-presentation
skills.description: Generate a polished presentation deck from a topic or outline using Gamma.
skills.content:
# Generate Presentation

Use Gamma to turn a topic or outline into a finished presentation.

## Steps
1. Gather the source content: a topic, a brief, or a structured outline of the points to cover.
2. Call Gamma to generate a presentation, choosing the number of cards and a theme that fits the audience.
3. Request an export format (such as PDF or PPTX) if a downloadable file is needed.

## Output
Return the link to the generated Gamma and, if requested, the export file URL. Summarize the deck structure (titles per card) so the requester can review before sharing.

skills.name: generate-document
skills.description: Generate a structured document or webpage from input text using Gamma.
skills.content:
# Generate Document

Use Gamma to produce a formatted document or webpage from raw input.

## Steps
1. Provide the input text and choose the output format (document or webpage).
2. Call Gamma to generate the content, setting a theme and the desired length or number of cards.
3. Capture the resulting Gamma URL and any export URL.

## Output
Return the generated Gamma link plus a short outline of the sections it produced. Include the export file URL if one was requested.

skills.name: personalize-deck-from-template
skills.description: Adapt an existing Gamma template into a prospect or client-specific deck with Generate from Template.
skills.content:
# Personalize Deck From Template

Use Gamma to scale on-brand, personalized decks from a proven template.

## Steps
1. Identify the template gamma ID to adapt (a master pitch or proposal deck) and collect the recipient details and the angle to tailor for.
2. Use Generate from Template with that template gamma ID and a prompt that retargets the audience, swaps in the recipient name and use case, and adjusts emphasis (for example highlight compliance for a healthcare buyer). The template structure is preserved by default.
3. Request an export (PDF or PPTX) if a downloadable file is needed.

## Output
Return the generated Gamma link and any export URL. Note the recipient it was generated for so it can be attached to the right CRM record or email.

skills.name: check-generation-status
skills.description: Poll a Gamma generation job by its generation ID and return the final deck link once ready.
skills.content:
# Check Generation Status

Gamma generation is asynchronous, so use this to wait for a deck to finish.

## Steps
1. Take the generation ID returned when the deck was requested.
2. Use Check Status to read the current status of the job.
3. Repeat until the status is completed (or failed), respecting a sensible polling interval.

## Output
Return the final status and, on success, the Gamma URL and any export URL. On failure, return the error details so the caller can retry or adjust the request.

skills.name: review-pull-request
skills.description: Fetch a GitHub PR, its changed files, and diff, then post a structured review comment.
skills.content:
# Review Pull Request

Use GitHub to read a pull request and leave a useful review.

## Steps
1. Get PR details for the given owner, repo, and PR number to read the title, description, and status.
2. Get the PR files to see the changed paths and diffs.
3. Assess the changes for correctness, missing tests, and risky edits.
4. Post a PR comment summarizing the review with specific, actionable feedback.

## Output
Confirm the comment was posted and return a short summary of the findings: what looks good, what needs changes, and any blocking concerns.

skills.name: triage-new-issue
skills.description: Read a GitHub issue, classify it, apply labels, and assign it to the right owner.
skills.content:
# Triage New Issue

Use GitHub to triage an incoming issue.

## Steps
1. Get the issue by owner, repo, and issue number to read its title and body.
2. Classify it (bug, feature, question, docs) and judge its severity.
3. Add the appropriate labels with Add issue labels.
4. Assign the issue to the relevant owner with Add issue assignees.

## Output
Return the applied labels, the assignee, and a one-line triage summary. If the issue lacks reproduction details, note what information is missing.

skills.name: summarize-repo-activity
skills.description: Pull recent GitHub PRs, commits, and issues for a repo and produce a concise activity digest.
skills.content:
# Summarize Repo Activity

Use GitHub to build a status digest for a repository.

## Steps
1. List open pull requests and recent issues for the owner and repo.
2. Get the latest commit to anchor the digest in time.
3. Group activity into in-progress work, newly opened items, and anything stalled or awaiting review.

## Output
Return a digest with three sections: open PRs (title, author, status), notable issues, and the latest commit. Keep it short enough to drop into a standup or Slack channel.

skills.name: open-pull-request-with-changes
skills.description: Create a branch, commit a file change, and open a GitHub pull request for review.
skills.content:
# Open Pull Request With Changes

Use GitHub to land a change as a reviewable PR.

## Steps
1. Create a new branch off the default branch with Create branch.
2. Create or update the target file on that branch with Create file or Update file, including a clear commit message.
3. Open a pull request from the new branch with Create pull request, writing a descriptive title and body.
4. Optionally request reviewers with Request PR reviewers.

## Output
Return the new PR number and URL, the branch name, and the files changed so the requester can track it to merge.

skills.name: review-merge-request
skills.description: Fetch a GitLab merge request and post a structured review comment with actionable feedback.
skills.content:
# Review Merge Request

Use GitLab to read a merge request and leave a useful review.

## Steps
1. Get the merge request by project ID and MR IID to read its title, description, and changes.
2. Assess the change for correctness, missing tests, and risky edits.
3. Post a review note on the MR with Add MR Comment, summarizing the feedback.

## Output
Confirm the comment was posted and return a short summary: what looks good, what needs changes, and any blocking concerns.

skills.name: triage-gitlab-issue
skills.description: Read a GitLab issue, classify it, and post a triage comment or update its fields.
skills.content:
# Triage GitLab Issue

Use GitLab to triage an incoming issue.

## Steps
1. Get the issue by project ID and issue IID to read its title and description.
2. Classify it (bug, feature, question) and judge severity.
3. Update the issue with the right labels and assignee using Update Issue, and add a triage note with Add Issue Comment.

## Output
Return the classification, applied labels, assignee, and a one-line triage summary. Note any missing reproduction details.

skills.name: monitor-pipeline-status
skills.description: Check GitLab pipeline status for a project and report failures, optionally retrying a failed pipeline.
skills.content:
# Monitor Pipeline Status

Use GitLab to keep an eye on CI pipelines.

## Steps
1. List pipelines for the project and identify the most recent runs.
2. Get the pipeline details for any that failed to read the status and reason.
3. If a failure looks transient, use Retry Pipeline to re-run it.

## Output
Return a summary of recent pipeline runs (ref, status, when) and call out any failures. If a retry was triggered, include the retried pipeline ID.
