skills.name: find-decision-maker-emails
skills.description: Find verified email addresses for key roles at a target company using domain search.
skills.content:
# Find Decision-Maker Emails

Given a company domain, find verified professional email addresses for the people who matter.

## Steps
1. Run a domain search for the target domain (e.g. example.com).
2. Filter results by department or seniority (executive, sales, IT) to surface decision-makers.
3. For each candidate, capture the full name, role, email, and confidence score.
4. Drop any result below your confidence threshold (e.g. < 80).

## Output
Return a list of contacts with name, title, email, and confidence score, sorted by seniority. Note the total emails available on the domain so the user knows coverage.

skills.name: verify-email-list
skills.description: Verify a batch of email addresses and flag undeliverable or risky ones before sending.
skills.content:
# Verify Email List

Clean a list of email addresses so a campaign only sends to deliverable inboxes.

## Steps
1. For each address, run the email verifier.
2. Record the verification status (valid, invalid, accept-all, disposable, webmail) and the deliverability score.
3. Bucket addresses into deliverable, risky, and undeliverable.

## Output
Return the three buckets with counts, and a recommended clean list containing only deliverable addresses.

skills.name: find-person-email
skills.description: Find the most likely email address for a named person at a specific company.
skills.content:
# Find a Person Email

Given a first name, last name, and company domain, find that person email address.

## Steps
1. Run the email finder with the full name and domain.
2. Capture the returned email, confidence score, and the sources Hunter used.
3. If confidence is low, optionally run a domain search to confirm the pattern.

## Output
Return the email, confidence score, and supporting sources. State clearly when no confident match was found.

templates.title: incident.io commander
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls incident.io for newly declared incidents, opens a Slack war-room for each, invites responders from the on-call schedule, pulls related PagerDuty alerts, and pins the runbook.

templates.title: incident.io postmortem starter
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls incident.io for recently resolved incidents, pulls the Slack thread, related Sentry errors, and deploy timeline, then drafts a postmortem doc in Google Docs.

templates.title: incident.io action-item tracker
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that watches incident.io for new follow-up actions, creates Linear tickets for each, and writes a tracking table that surfaces overdue actions on a weekly digest.

templates.title: incident.io weekly digest
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled weekly workflow that summarizes incident.io activity — declared incidents, MTTR, top affected services, action-item completion rate — and posts to Slack.

templates.title: incident.io customer comms drafter
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that during a high-severity incident.io incident drafts customer status-page copy and a tailored email update, holds for approval, and dispatches once approved.

templates.title: incident.io SLO impact mapper
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that on each incident.io incident maps impacted services to active SLOs, calculates SLO burn, and writes the impact analysis back to the incident timeline.

templates.title: incident.io noise filter
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that pulls incident.io declared incidents, classifies a subset as low-impact noise, auto-resolves them after auditing, and writes a noise-rate metric to a table.

skills.name: declare-incident-from-alert
skills.description: Open an incident.io incident from an inbound alert with the right severity and summary.
skills.content:
# Declare an Incident From an Alert

Turn a monitoring alert into a structured incident.io incident so responders can act fast.

## Steps
1. Look up available severities and pick the one matching the alert impact.
2. Create the incident with a clear name, a summary describing impact and affected service, and the chosen severity.
3. Set incident type and any required custom fields from the alert payload.
4. Capture the new incident reference and link.

## Output
Return the incident ID, reference, severity, and link. Confirm the responder channel was created so the team can jump in.

skills.name: post-incident-update
skills.description: Update an active incident with current status and a progress note for stakeholders.
skills.content:
# Post an Incident Update

Keep stakeholders informed by moving an active incident through its lifecycle.

## Steps
1. Look up the incident by reference or ID to confirm its current status.
2. List valid incident statuses and choose the next one (investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved).
3. Update the incident with the new status and a concise progress message.

## Output
Return the incident reference, the new status, and a one-line summary of what changed and when.

skills.name: on-call-handoff-report
skills.description: Summarize who is on call and recent open incidents for an on-call handoff.
skills.content:
# On-Call Handoff Report

Build a clean handoff so the next on-call engineer knows the state of the world.

## Steps
1. List current schedules and active escalation paths to determine who is on call.
2. List recent incidents and filter to those that are open or recently resolved.
3. For each open incident, capture severity, status, and outstanding follow-ups.

## Output
Return a handoff brief: who is on call now, open incidents with severity and status, and follow-ups that still need owners.

skills.name: export-incident-followups
skills.description: Pull follow-ups from recent incidents into an actionable list for post-incident review.
skills.content:
# Export Incident Follow-Ups

Gather the action items that came out of recent incidents so none slip through.

## Steps
1. List incidents within the target time window.
2. For each, list its follow-ups and capture title, owner, status, and linked incident.
3. Group follow-ups by owner and by open vs completed.

## Output
Return a table of follow-ups grouped by owner with status and source incident, highlighting overdue or unassigned items.

templates.title: Infisical secret rotation orchestrator
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists Infisical secrets, generates fresh values for those due for rotation, updates them across each environment, and writes rotation status to a compliance table.

templates.title: Infisical environment drift detector
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that diffs Infisical environments against expected schemas, alerts on missing or extra secrets, and writes a remediation queue.

templates.title: Infisical env bootstrapper
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that on a Workday new-hire event creates the standard set of Infisical secrets for the new engineer’s scoped dev environment from a template, and writes the provisioning record to a table.

templates.title: Infisical offboarding rotation
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that on a Workday termination rotates the shared Infisical secrets the departing engineer had access to by generating new values and updating them across environments, then writes the action log to a table.

templates.title: Infisical CI sync
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that mirrors Infisical secrets into GitHub Actions environments for CI deploys, keeping the secret store as the single source of truth.

templates.title: Infisical secret-inventory reviewer
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled quarterly workflow that lists Infisical secrets per project and environment, flags ones with weak or aged values for owner attestation in Slack, and writes the review to a compliance table.

templates.title: Infisical secret-inventory snapshot
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists Infisical secrets across environments, writes a redacted inventory snapshot to S3 for long-term retention, and tracks secret count trends in a table.

templates.title: Secrets Manager + Infisical mirror
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that mirrors secrets between AWS Secrets Manager and Infisical for cross-cloud applications, normalizes naming, and writes a sync log.

skills.name: fetch-secret-for-run
skills.description: Retrieve a named secret from Infisical to use as a credential during a workflow run.
skills.content:
# Fetch a Secret for a Run

Pull a single secret from Infisical so a downstream step can authenticate without hardcoding credentials.

## Steps
1. Identify the project, environment (e.g. dev, staging, prod), and secret path.
2. Get the secret by name from that scope.
3. Pass the value to the consuming step. Never echo the raw secret into logs or output.

## Output
Confirm the secret was retrieved (by name and environment) and that it was used. Do not print the secret value itself.

skills.name: rotate-secret
skills.description: Update an existing secret in Infisical with a new value as part of a rotation.
skills.content:
# Rotate a Secret

Replace a secret value in Infisical during a credential rotation.

## Steps
1. Confirm the project, environment, and secret name to rotate.
2. Update the secret with the new value at that path.
3. Optionally read the secret back by name to confirm it now exists (without printing the value).

## Output
Confirm the secret name and environment that was rotated and the timestamp. Never expose the old or new value.

skills.name: audit-environment-secrets
skills.description: List the secret names present in an Infisical environment for an inventory or audit.
skills.content:
# Audit Environment Secrets

Produce an inventory of which secrets exist in an Infisical environment without exposing their values.

## Steps
1. Choose the project, environment, and path to audit.
2. List secrets at that scope and collect only the keys and metadata.
3. Compare against the expected set if one is provided and flag missing or unexpected keys.

## Output
Return a list of secret names (keys only) with count, and any discrepancies versus the expected set. Never include secret values.

templates.title: Instantly lead loader
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads new prospects from a table and creates each as a lead in the right Instantly campaign, then writes the Instantly lead ID back so the sender table stays in sync.

templates.title: Instantly reply triager
templates.prompt: Create a workflow triggered when an Instantly reply is received that classifies intent, updates the lead interest status, and posts a Slack alert for positive replies so reps follow up fast.

templates.title: Instantly campaign launcher
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that creates a new Instantly campaign from a brief, builds a lead list, loads the prospects, and activates the campaign once the list is ready.

templates.title: Instantly performance report
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled weekly workflow that lists Instantly campaigns and emails, computes reply and interest rates per campaign, logs them to a table for trend tracking, and Slacks a summary to the sales team.

templates.title: Instantly meeting-booked sync
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered when an Instantly lead is marked meeting booked that creates or updates the matching HubSpot contact and deal so the CRM reflects pipeline from outbound.

templates.title: Hunter + Instantly outbound
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that finds verified prospect emails with Hunter, validates each, and loads the deliverable contacts into an active Instantly campaign.

templates.title: Instantly reply router
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists new Instantly campaign email replies, classifies each as interested, objection, or out-of-office with an agent, updates the lead's interest status, and posts hot replies to the sales Slack channel for a fast follow-up.

skills.name: add-leads-to-campaign
skills.description: Push a batch of prospects into an Instantly campaign as new leads with personalization fields.
skills.content:
# Add Leads to a Campaign

Load a set of prospects into an Instantly cold-email campaign so they enter the sending sequence.

## Steps
1. List campaigns and identify the target campaign by name.
2. For each prospect, create a lead with email, first name, last name, company, and any custom personalization variables.
3. Attach each lead to the chosen campaign.

## Output
Return how many leads were added, the campaign name, and any rows skipped for missing or invalid emails.

skills.name: launch-outreach-campaign
skills.description: Create a cold-email campaign, load a lead list, and activate it for sending.
skills.content:
# Launch an Outreach Campaign

Stand up a new Instantly campaign end to end and start sending.

## Steps
1. Create a lead list and add the target prospects to it.
2. Create the campaign with its sending sequence and schedule.
3. Add the leads to the campaign.
4. Activate the campaign so sending begins.

## Output
Return the campaign name, lead count, and activation status. Confirm the campaign is live.

skills.name: triage-campaign-replies
skills.description: Review recent campaign email replies and update each lead interest status.
skills.content:
# Triage Campaign Replies

Process inbound replies on a campaign and route each lead by interest.

## Steps
1. List recent emails for the campaign and identify replies from leads.
2. Read each reply and classify intent (interested, not interested, out of office, wrong person).
3. Update the matching lead interest status to reflect the classification.
4. For interested leads, draft a reply to the email.

## Output
Return a summary of replies by category, the leads marked interested, and any drafted responses for review.

skills.name: campaign-performance-snapshot
skills.description: Summarize active campaigns and their leads into a quick outreach performance snapshot.
skills.content:
# Campaign Performance Snapshot

Give a quick read on how outreach is going across campaigns.

## Steps
1. List campaigns and note which are active.
2. For each active campaign, list leads and tally counts by interest status.
3. Pull recent emails to gauge reply volume.

## Output
Return a per-campaign snapshot: total leads, breakdown by interest status, and reply activity, highlighting the top-performing campaign.

templates.title: Multilingual support replier
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that detects the language of a new Intercom message, translates it to the agent language with Google Translate, drafts a reply, then translates the reply back before sending.

templates.title: Customer feedback analyzer
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that pulls support tickets and conversations from Intercom daily, categorizes them by theme and sentiment, tracks trends in a table, and sends a weekly Slack report highlighting the top feature requests and pain points.

templates.title: Intercom auto-resolver
templates.prompt: Create a knowledge base from my help center and product docs, then build a workflow that watches new Intercom conversations, attempts an answer with cited sources, and only assigns to a human admin when confidence is low or the customer asks.

templates.title: Intercom to Linear bug ticketer
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered by new Intercom conversations that classifies whether the message is a bug report, extracts the repro steps and affected area, creates a Linear issue with the conversation transcript attached, and replies in Intercom with the issue ID.

templates.title: Intercom VIP escalation
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that monitors new Intercom conversations, looks up the contact in the CRM, and when the contact belongs to a top-tier account, snoozes the conversation, posts a Slack alert in #vip-support with full context, and tags the conversation as VIP.

templates.title: Intercom conversation summarizer
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered when an Intercom conversation is closed that summarizes the issue, resolution, and any follow-up actions, then appends the summary to a Notion knowledge log so the team can learn from past conversations.

templates.title: Intercom contact enrichment
templates.prompt: Create a workflow triggered when a new Intercom contact is created that enriches the contact with company, title, and seniority data from Apollo, updates the Intercom contact attributes, and adds a note with the enrichment source.

templates.title: Intercom-Zendesk migration mirror
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that mirrors new Intercom conversations into Zendesk as tickets during a migration window, syncs status and replies in both directions, and writes a table of every mapped conversation-to-ticket pair for audit.

templates.title: Telegram support bot
templates.prompt: Build a Telegram bot that answers product questions using a knowledge base with citations, escalates to a human via Intercom when it cannot answer, and logs every conversation to a table.

templates.title: Zep + Intercom support continuity
templates.prompt: Create a Zep-backed support agent for Intercom that remembers what each customer has tried before, prefers, or escalated, so support conversations never restart from scratch.

skills.name: triage-open-conversations
skills.description: Review open Intercom conversations and assign each to the right teammate with a priority.
skills.content:
# Triage Open Conversations

Keep the inbox moving by routing open Intercom conversations to the right people.

## Steps
1. List or search open conversations.
2. Read each conversation to understand the customer issue and urgency.
3. List admins to find the right owner, then assign the conversation.
4. Tag the conversation by topic (billing, bug, onboarding) and add an internal note summarizing next steps.

## Output
Return each conversation with its assigned owner, applied tags, and a one-line summary. Flag anything that looks urgent.

skills.name: reply-and-resolve
skills.description: Draft a reply to a customer conversation, send it, and close the conversation when resolved.
skills.content:
# Reply and Resolve

Respond to a customer in Intercom and wrap up the conversation.

## Steps
1. Get the conversation and read the full thread for context.
2. Draft a helpful, on-brand reply that addresses the customer question.
3. Reply to the conversation with the message.
4. If the issue is fully handled, close the conversation; otherwise snooze it until a follow-up time.

## Output
Return the reply that was sent and the final conversation state (closed or snoozed).

skills.name: enrich-contact-record
skills.description: Create or update an Intercom contact and link it to its company with current details.
skills.content:
# Enrich a Contact Record

Keep contact data accurate by creating or updating an Intercom contact.

## Steps
1. Search contacts by email to see if the person already exists.
2. Create the contact if missing, or update the existing record with name, role, and attributes.
3. Find or create the company and attach the contact to it.
4. Tag the contact to reflect segment or lifecycle stage.

## Output
Return the contact ID, the linked company, and the fields that were created or changed.

skills.name: open-support-ticket
skills.description: Create an Intercom ticket from a conversation and capture the key issue details.
skills.content:
# Open a Support Ticket

Escalate a customer issue into a tracked Intercom ticket.

## Steps
1. Get the source conversation and summarize the issue, impact, and steps to reproduce.
2. Create a ticket with a clear title, the summary, and the linked contact.
3. Add a note to the conversation referencing the new ticket so context is preserved.

## Output
Return the ticket ID, title, linked contact, and the conversation it came from.

templates.title: Jina URL-to-knowledge ingester
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads a list of source URLs with Jina Reader, converts each into clean text, and ingests the content into a research knowledge base for retrieval.

templates.title: Jina web-research digest
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that runs Jina web search on tracked topics, reads the top results with Jina Reader, and writes a summarized digest to a research table.

templates.title: Jina web-content reader
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that uses Jina Reader to convert any URL into clean text, summarizes with an agent, and stores the result in a research knowledge base.

templates.title: Jina competitor watch
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that reads competitor pricing and changelog pages with Jina Reader, diffs against the last snapshot, and posts notable changes to Slack.

templates.title: Jina answer enrichment
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes a user question, runs a Jina web search for current sources, reads the top pages with Jina Reader, and has an agent answer with citations.

templates.title: Jina Slack research bot
templates.prompt: Create a Slack bot that runs Jina web search on the asked question, reads the most relevant results with Jina Reader, and replies with a summarized answer and source links.

templates.title: Jina docs-to-Notion clipper
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads a submitted URL with Jina Reader, summarizes the content with an agent, and appends a clean clipped entry to a Notion research database.

skills.name: extract-article-content
skills.description: Read a URL and return clean, LLM-ready text stripped of navigation and ads.
skills.content:
# Extract Article Content

Turn a messy web page into clean, readable text an agent can reason over.

## Steps
1. Take the target URL.
2. Read the URL to get the parsed main content as markdown or text.
3. Strip boilerplate (nav, footers, ads) if any remains and keep the core article body.

## Output
Return the page title and the cleaned content, plus the source URL. Note if the page could not be fully extracted.

skills.name: research-topic-from-web
skills.description: Search the web for a topic and summarize the top results into a briefing.
skills.content:
# Research a Topic From the Web

Gather and condense current web information on a topic.

## Steps
1. Run a web search for the topic with a focused query.
2. Take the top results and read the most relevant URLs for full content.
3. Synthesize the findings, noting points of agreement and disagreement across sources.

## Output
Return a short briefing with key findings, each backed by the source URL it came from.

skills.name: summarize-url
skills.description: Fetch a single URL and produce a concise summary with the main takeaways.
skills.content:
# Summarize a URL

Give a quick, faithful summary of a single web page.

## Steps
1. Read the URL to extract its main content.
2. Identify the core thesis and the most important supporting points.
3. Condense into a short summary without adding outside information.

## Output
Return the page title, a 3-5 bullet summary of the key takeaways, and the source URL.

templates.title: Link GitHub pull requests to Jira tickets
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that monitors GitHub pull requests and automatically transitions linked Jira issues when PRs are opened or merged, keeping your project board accurate without any manual updates.

templates.title: Jira knowledge search
templates.prompt: Create a knowledge base connected to my Jira project so all tickets, comments, and resolutions are automatically synced and searchable. Then build an agent I can ask things like "how did we fix the auth timeout issue?" or "what was decided about the API redesign?" and get answers with ticket citations.

templates.title: Sprint report generator
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that runs at the end of each sprint, pulls all completed, in-progress, and blocked Jira tickets, calculates velocity and carry-over, and generates a sprint summary document with charts and trends to share with the team.

templates.title: Jira backlog grooming digest
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled weekly workflow that scans Jira backlog for tickets missing estimates, owners, or priorities, generates a grooming queue, and posts the top items to Slack.

templates.title: Jira stale-ticket sweeper
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that lists Jira tickets with no activity in 14 days, pings the assignee in Slack with a status prompt, and updates the ticket based on the response.

templates.title: Jira release notes builder
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that pulls Jira tickets resolved since the last release tag, groups by feature area, and drafts user-facing release notes for marketing review.

templates.title: Jira to Linear migrator
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that imports a Jira project into Linear, preserving status mapping, labels, comments, and assignees, and writes a mapping table for redirect URLs.

templates.title: Auto-generate Confluence pages from Jira sprints
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs at the end of each Jira sprint, pulls all completed and in-progress tickets, and automatically creates a structured Confluence documentation page so sprint reporting requires no manual effort.

templates.title: Microsoft Teams daily brief
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that pulls updates from your project tools — GitHub commits, Jira ticket status changes, and calendar events — and posts a formatted daily brief to your Microsoft Teams channel each morning.

templates.title: Zendesk to Jira engineering bridge
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that searches Zendesk for tickets newly tagged as a bug, creates a linked Jira issue with the ticket details and customer impact, and posts the Jira link back as an internal note on the Zendesk ticket.

skills.name: create-bug-from-report
skills.description: Turn a bug report into a well-structured Jira issue with steps, severity, and labels.
skills.content:
# Create a Bug From a Report

Convert a raw bug report into a clean, actionable Jira issue.

## Steps
1. Parse the report for summary, steps to reproduce, expected vs actual behavior, and environment.
2. Create an issue in the target project with type Bug, a clear summary, and a structured description.
3. Set priority based on impact and add relevant labels or components.
4. Optionally assign it to the right owner.

## Output
Return the issue key, URL, priority, and assignee. Confirm the description includes reproduction steps.

skills.name: triage-open-issues
skills.description: Search open issues with JQL and propose assignees, priorities, and labels.
skills.content:
# Triage Open Issues

Bring order to a backlog of unassigned or stale issues.

## Steps
1. Search issues using JQL (e.g. unassigned and recently created in a project).
2. Read each issue to understand scope and urgency.
3. For each, propose a priority, suggested assignee, and labels; apply updates where confident.
4. Add a short triage comment explaining the decision.

## Output
Return a table of issues with proposed/applied priority, assignee, and labels, flagging any that need a human decision.

skills.name: transition-and-comment
skills.description: Move an issue to a new workflow status and post a progress comment.
skills.content:
# Transition and Comment

Advance a Jira issue through its workflow with a clear note.

## Steps
1. Retrieve the issue and read its current status.
2. Get available transitions and choose the correct next status (e.g. In Progress, In Review, Done).
3. Transition the issue to that status.
4. Add a comment summarizing what changed and any next steps.

## Output
Return the issue key, the new status, and the comment that was posted.

skills.name: sprint-status-digest
skills.description: Summarize issues in a project or sprint grouped by status and assignee.
skills.content:
# Sprint Status Digest

Produce a quick read on where work stands.

## Steps
1. Search issues with JQL scoped to the project or current sprint.
2. Group results by status and by assignee.
3. Identify blocked issues, overdue items, and anything unassigned.

## Output
Return a digest: counts by status, work per assignee, and a callout list of blocked or at-risk issues with their keys.

templates.title: JSM major incident broadcaster
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered when a major-incident request is created in Jira Service Management that pulls the affected service from PagerDuty, identifies the current on-call, posts a structured incident brief to a Slack war-room channel, and adds the responders as JSM request participants.

templates.title: JSM request auto-triage
templates.prompt: Create a workflow triggered by new Jira Service Management requests that classifies the request type, sets the correct priority based on impact and urgency, transitions it to the right initial status, and adds the assignment-group customer organization as a participant.

templates.title: JSM approval router
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that watches Jira Service Management requests for new approval steps, posts a Slack DM to each approver with request context and quick-action buttons, and answers the approval in JSM based on their response while keeping the request in sync.

templates.title: JSM form auto-completer
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that when a Jira Service Management request is created with an attached ProForma form, pre-fills the answers from the requester profile, attached email, and CMDB lookup, and saves the answers so agents only review rather than retype.

templates.title: JSM weekly service desk report
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled weekly workflow that pulls Jira Service Management request volume by queue, SLA performance, top request types, and bottleneck assignees, and generates a service desk health report file for the operations review.

templates.title: JSM-to-ServiceNow bridge
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that mirrors Jira Service Management incident requests into ServiceNow incident records and vice versa, keeping status, assignment, and comments in sync so teams on either side see the same truth.

templates.title: JSM self-service deflection bot
templates.prompt: Create a knowledge base from internal IT docs, then build a Slack agent that answers employee help requests with cited steps and, when it can't resolve the issue, creates a Jira Service Management request with the right request type so nothing falls through.

templates.title: Outlook to JSM ticket router
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads support requests arriving in a shared Outlook mailbox, classifies the request type, and creates a Jira Service Management request in the correct service desk with the right request type, then replies from Outlook with the JSM portal link.

skills.name: raise-service-request
skills.description: Create a customer request on the right service desk with the correct request type.
skills.content:
# Raise a Service Request

Log an inbound customer request into the correct Jira Service Management queue.

## Steps
1. Get service desks and identify the right one for the request.
2. Get request types for that service desk and choose the matching type.
3. Create the request with a clear summary, description, and any required request-type fields.
4. Capture the request key and reporter.

## Output
Return the request key, the service desk and request type used, and the reporter. Confirm required fields were filled.

skills.name: respond-and-update-request
skills.description: Add a public reply to a customer request and move it to the right status.
skills.content:
# Respond and Update a Request

Reply to a customer on their request and advance it.

## Steps
1. Get the request and read its history and current status.
2. Add a comment with the response (public to the customer).
3. Get available transitions and move the request to the appropriate status.

## Output
Return the request key, the comment added, and the new status.

skills.name: sla-breach-watch
skills.description: Scan open requests on a queue and flag ones at risk of breaching SLA.
skills.content:
# SLA Breach Watch

Surface requests that are about to miss their SLA so the team can act.

## Steps
1. Get the service desk and its queues, then get requests in the target queue.
2. For each request, get its SLA information and time remaining.
3. Flag requests that are breached or close to breaching their target.

## Output
Return a prioritized list of at-risk requests with key, summary, SLA metric, and time remaining, worst first.

templates.title: Kalshi event-contract tracker
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls Kalshi for prices on tracked event contracts, writes the price history to a tables-based portfolio, and posts large-move alerts to Slack.

templates.title: Kalshi macroeconomic dashboard
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that pulls Kalshi probability markets for selected macroeconomic events, writes the implied probabilities to a tables-based dashboard, and emails a weekly summary.

templates.title: Kalshi + Polymarket arbitrage scanner
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that fetches comparable contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket, computes implied-probability spreads, writes the top arbitrage candidates to a table, and pings Slack on significant gaps.

templates.title: Kalshi + Profound macro signal
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that combines Kalshi event-contract prices with Profound AI signal to forecast macro events and writes a thesis file weekly.

templates.title: Kalshi position rebalancer
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that monitors Kalshi position weights against a target allocation, captures drift, and pings Slack with proposed rebalancing trades.

templates.title: Kalshi earnings event tracker
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that pulls Kalshi earnings-event contracts, captures implied probabilities the day before each event, and writes a per-ticker table for review.

templates.title: Kalshi election-market dashboard
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that pulls Kalshi election market prices, captures movement over time, and writes a per-race tracking table for political analysts.

skills.name: market-odds-snapshot
skills.description: Pull current prices and odds for a Kalshi event and summarize the implied probabilities.
skills.content:
# Market Odds Snapshot

Report the current state of a Kalshi prediction market.

## Steps
1. Find the event by ticker or search recent events.
2. Get the markets under that event and their current yes/no prices.
3. Convert prices to implied probabilities and capture volume and open interest.

## Output
Return each market with its current yes/no price, implied probability, and recent volume, plus a one-line read on where the market is leaning.

skills.name: track-position-pnl
skills.description: Report account balance, open positions, and unrealized profit or loss on Kalshi.
skills.content:
# Track Position P&L

Give a clear read on the current trading account state.

## Steps
1. Get the account balance.
2. Get current positions and, for each, the market and entry exposure.
3. Get current market prices to estimate unrealized P&L per position.

## Output
Return balance, each open position with its market and estimated unrealized P&L, and a total exposure figure.

skills.name: place-limit-order
skills.description: Place a limit order on a Kalshi market after confirming price and balance.
skills.content:
# Place a Limit Order

Submit a limit order on a chosen Kalshi market with guardrails.

## Steps
1. Get the target market and confirm its current price and orderbook.
2. Check the account balance to ensure the order is affordable.
3. Create a limit order with the side (yes/no), price, and quantity.
4. Confirm the order was accepted and capture its ID.

## Output
Return the order ID, market, side, price, quantity, and status. State clearly if the order was rejected or only partially filled.

skills.name: check-user-consent
skills.description: Look up a user current consent state in Ketch before processing their data.
skills.content:
# Check User Consent

Confirm what a user has consented to before a workflow uses their data.

## Steps
1. Identify the user (by identity key) and the jurisdiction/policy scope.
2. Get the user current consent for the relevant purposes (analytics, marketing, etc.).
3. Determine which downstream actions are permitted based on the consent state.

## Output
Return the consent state per purpose and a clear allow/deny decision for the intended data use. Stop the workflow if required consent is missing.

skills.name: record-consent-update
skills.description: Set or update a user consent choices in Ketch from a preference change.
skills.content:
# Record a Consent Update

Persist a user updated consent choices to Ketch.

## Steps
1. Capture the user identity and the new consent choices per purpose.
2. Set the consent for that user in the correct jurisdiction/policy scope.
3. Read the consent back to confirm it was applied.

## Output
Confirm the user identity, the purposes updated, and the resulting consent state.

skills.name: fulfill-data-subject-request
skills.description: Invoke a data subject right (access, delete) in Ketch and track the request.
skills.content:
# Fulfill a Data Subject Request

Kick off a DSR (e.g. access or deletion) on behalf of a user.

## Steps
1. Capture the requester identity and the right being exercised (access, deletion, correction).
2. Invoke the right in Ketch with the required identity and jurisdiction context.
3. Capture the request reference for tracking.

## Output
Return the request reference, the right invoked, and the requester identity so the request can be tracked to completion.

skills.name: sync-subscription-preferences
skills.description: Read a user subscription topics in Ketch and update them to honor an opt-in or opt-out.
skills.content:
# Sync Subscription Preferences

Keep a user communication preferences accurate in Ketch when they opt in or out of a channel or topic.

## Steps
1. Identify the user and get their current subscription topics and controls.
2. Determine the requested change (e.g. opt out of the newsletter, set a global unsubscribe).
3. Set the subscription topics and controls to the new state for that user.
4. Read the subscriptions back to confirm the change applied.

## Output
Return the topics and controls that changed and the resulting opt-in or opt-out state per channel. Confirm any global unsubscribe was honored.

skills.name: log-llm-run-to-langsmith
skills.description: Send a single LLM or chain run to LangSmith with inputs, outputs, and timing for tracing.
skills.content:
# Log an LLM Run to LangSmith

Forward one workflow step into LangSmith so it shows up in tracing and evals.

## Steps
1. Capture the run name, run type (llm, chain, tool), and the project to log into.
2. Record the inputs (prompt or arguments) and the outputs the step produced.
3. Include start and end times so latency is captured, plus any error if the step failed.
4. Create the run in LangSmith.

## Output
Confirm the run was logged with its name, type, and project, and surface the run ID for follow-up inspection.

skills.name: batch-export-runs
skills.description: Send a batch of completed workflow runs to LangSmith in one call for observability.
skills.content:
# Batch Export Runs

Ship multiple completed runs to LangSmith at once instead of one by one.

## Steps
1. Collect the runs to export, each with name, type, inputs, outputs, and timing.
2. Assign a shared project so the runs land together.
3. Submit them as a single batch.

## Output
Return how many runs were exported, the project they landed in, and any runs that failed validation.

skills.name: compile-document-to-pdf
skills.description: Compile LaTeX source into a finished PDF, choosing the right compiler and reporting any compilation errors. Use whenever a polished, print-ready document is needed.
skills.content:
# Compile Document to PDF

Turn LaTeX source into a finished PDF.

## Steps
1. Assemble the complete LaTeX source, from \documentclass to \end{document}.
2. Pick the compiler: pdflatex for standard documents, xelatex or lualatex when custom fonts or full unicode are needed.
3. Attach any supporting files (images, included .tex files, .bib bibliographies) as resources with the paths the source references.
4. Compile and capture the resulting PDF.

## Output
The compiled PDF file and its URL. If compilation fails, report the TeX errors verbatim so they can be fixed.

skills.name: generate-document-from-template
skills.description: Fill a LaTeX template with structured data and compile it to PDF. Use for repeatable documents like invoices, certificates, letters, and contracts.
skills.content:
# Generate Document from Template

Produce a templated document with real data filled in.

## Steps
1. Start from the LaTeX template and identify its placeholders.
2. Substitute each placeholder with the provided data, escaping LaTeX special characters (&, %, $, #, _, {, }) in user-supplied values.
3. Compile the filled-in source to PDF.
4. Name the output file after the document, e.g. invoice-1042.pdf.

## Output
A compiled PDF per record, named for its contents. List any records that failed to compile and why.

skills.name: typeset-math-content
skills.description: Write mathematical content — equations, proofs, problem sets — in LaTeX and compile a printable PDF. Use for worksheets, solution sheets, and technical notes.
skills.content:
# Typeset Math Content

Produce a clean PDF of mathematical material.

## Steps
1. Draft the content using proper LaTeX math: inline $...$, display equations, and environments like align and theorem as appropriate.
2. Load only the packages the content needs (amsmath, amssymb, amsthm).
3. Structure the document with sections and consistent numbering.
4. Compile to PDF and verify there are no errors.

## Output
A printable PDF of the typeset material, plus the LaTeX source so it can be edited later.

skills.name: build-report-with-bibliography
skills.description: Compile a report or paper that cites sources, attaching a BibTeX bibliography as a resource. Use for research reports, literature reviews, and academic writing.
skills.content:
# Build Report with Bibliography

Compile a citing document with its references resolved.

## Steps
1. Write the report source with \cite commands and a \bibliography{refs} (or biblatex equivalent) reference.
2. Attach the BibTeX entries as a resource at the cited path, e.g. refs.bib.
3. Compile — the bibliography pass runs automatically.
4. Check the output for unresolved citation warnings and fix missing entries.

## Output
The compiled PDF with a formatted reference list. Note any citations that could not be resolved.

skills.name: fix-compilation-errors
skills.description: Diagnose failed LaTeX builds from the compiler error output and iterate until the document compiles. Use when a compilation returns errors instead of a PDF.
skills.content:
# Fix Compilation Errors

Get a failing LaTeX document to build.

## Steps
1. Read the TeX error lines from the failed compile (lines starting with !), which name the problem and its location.
2. Apply the targeted fix: missing packages (verify availability with Get Package Details or Search Packages), unescaped special characters, unmatched braces or environments, or commands needing a different compiler (e.g. fontspec requires xelatex or lualatex — confirm the font exists with List Fonts).
3. Recompile and repeat until the build succeeds.
4. Keep edits minimal — fix the errors without rewriting the document.

## Output
The compiled PDF and a short list of the fixes that were applied.

skills.name: toggle-flag-in-environment
skills.description: Turn a LaunchDarkly feature flag on or off in a specific environment safely.
skills.content:
# Toggle a Flag in an Environment

Flip a feature flag for a target environment with a confirmation step.

## Steps
1. Identify the project and the environment (e.g. production, staging) and the flag key.
2. Get the current flag status to confirm its present state.
3. Toggle the flag to the desired on/off state in that environment.
4. Re-check the status to confirm the change took effect.

## Output
Return the flag key, environment, previous state, and new state. Confirm the toggle was applied.

skills.name: create-feature-flag
skills.description: Create a new LaunchDarkly feature flag in a project with a clear key and description.
skills.content:
# Create a Feature Flag

Stand up a new feature flag for an upcoming release.

## Steps
1. Choose the project and define a descriptive flag key and human-readable name.
2. Set a description explaining what the flag controls and whether it is temporary or permanent.
3. Create the flag, defaulting it to off so it can be rolled out deliberately.

## Output
Return the flag key, name, project, and initial state. Confirm the flag starts disabled.

skills.name: flag-rollout-audit
skills.description: Report on a flag state across environments and recent changes from the audit log.
skills.content:
# Flag Rollout Audit

Understand where a flag stands and who changed it recently.

## Steps
1. Get the flag and list environments for the project.
2. For each environment, capture the flag on/off state and targeting.
3. Pull the audit log entries for the flag to see recent changes and who made them.

## Output
Return a per-environment state table for the flag and a short changelog of recent modifications with actor and timestamp.

skills.name: emergency-flag-kill-switch
skills.description: Instantly disable a feature flag in production during an incident and confirm it is off.
skills.content:
# Emergency Flag Kill-Switch

Kill a misbehaving feature in production immediately.

## Steps
1. Identify the project, the production environment key, and the flag key to disable.
2. Toggle the flag off in that environment.
3. Get the flag status to confirm it is now off and no longer being served.

## Output
Return the flag key, environment, and confirmation that the flag is off, with the timestamp of the change.

skills.name: stale-flag-cleanup
skills.description: Find temporary or long-untouched feature flags and surface them for removal.
skills.content:
# Stale Flag Cleanup

Keep flag debt under control by surfacing flags that have outlived their purpose.

## Steps
1. List the flags in the project, noting which are marked temporary and their creation dates.
2. Cross-reference the audit log to find flags with no recent changes.
3. Compile the candidates that are temporary and inactive into a cleanup list.

## Output
Return a list of stale flag keys with their age, temporary status, and last-change date so an owner can decide whether to archive or delete them.

skills.name: triage-campaign-replies
skills.description: Pull recent Lemlist reply activity, classify each reply by intent, and surface the ones that need a human.
skills.content:
# Triage Campaign Replies

Monitor Lemlist replies and route them by intent so reps act on hot leads fast.

## Steps
1. Get Activities filtered to the Email Replied type, optionally scoped to a campaign ID, with a sensible limit.
2. For each reply, look up the lead with Get Lead to attach name, company, and job title.
3. Classify the reply intent: interested, not interested, out-of-office, unsubscribe, or question.
4. For interested or question replies, build a short summary with the lead name, campaign, and the reply text.

## Output
A list of replies grouped by intent. For each interested or question reply, include lead name, company, campaign, a one-line summary, and the raw reply text so a rep can respond.

skills.name: analyze-campaign-performance
skills.description: Compute open, click, reply, and bounce rates per campaign and per step from Lemlist activities and flag weak steps.
skills.content:
# Analyze Campaign Performance

Turn raw Lemlist activity into step-level metrics and concrete fixes.

## Steps
1. Get Activities for the target campaign with a high limit, paging with offset until all activity is collected.
2. Tally events by type: emails sent, opened, clicked, replied, and bounced.
3. Compute open rate, click rate, reply rate, and bounce rate overall and per sequence step.
4. Flag steps where reply rate is low, bounce rate is high, or drop-off between steps is steep.

## Output
A per-campaign and per-step metrics table plus a short list of recommendations, such as rewriting a low-reply subject line or pausing a high-bounce step.

skills.name: qualify-and-reply-to-lead
skills.description: Look up a Lemlist lead and send a personalized reply through their Lemlist mailbox.
skills.content:
# Qualify and Reply to Lead

Respond to an inbound lead with a tailored message sent from your Lemlist inbox.

## Steps
1. Get Lead by email or lead ID to pull first name, company, and job title.
2. Draft a concise, personalized reply that references the lead context and includes a clear next step or booking link.
3. Send Email through Lemlist using the sender user ID, sender email, mailbox ID, contact ID, lead ID, subject, and the drafted HTML message body.

## Output
Confirmation that the email was sent, the lead identity it went to, and the message body that was used.

skills.name: create-triaged-issue
skills.description: Create a Linear issue in the right team with a clear title, description, priority, and labels.
skills.content:
# Create Triaged Issue

Turn a request or bug report into a well-formed Linear issue.

## Steps
1. If the team is unknown, List Teams and pick the team that owns the area.
2. Write a concise title and a description with context, steps to reproduce, and acceptance criteria.
3. Create Issue with the team ID, title, description, and a priority that matches severity.
4. Optionally Add Label to Issue for type and area labels using IDs from List Labels.

## Output
The created issue ID, its identifier and URL, and the team, priority, and labels applied.

skills.name: triage-new-issue
skills.description: Read a Linear issue, apply type and priority labels, set assignee and state, and comment a triage summary.
skills.content:
# Triage New Issue

Triage an incoming Linear issue so it lands in the right place with the right metadata.

## Steps
1. Get Issue to read the title and description.
2. Determine the issue type, priority, and owning area from the content.
3. Add Label to Issue for type and priority, and Update Issue to set the assignee, state, and priority.
4. Create Comment with a short triage summary explaining the classification and next step.

## Output
The issue identifier, the labels added, the assignee and state set, and the triage comment posted.

skills.name: summarize-active-cycle
skills.description: Pull completed and open issues in the active cycle and produce a sprint progress digest.
skills.content:
# Summarize Active Cycle

Produce a sprint review digest from the current Linear cycle.

## Steps
1. Get Active Cycle for the team to find the current cycle.
2. Read Issues or Search Issues scoped to that cycle, separating completed from still-open issues.
3. Compute counts, completion percentage, and call out blocked or at-risk issues by priority.
4. Summarize progress, blockers, and what is likely to slip.

## Output
A digest with completed vs open counts, completion percentage, a list of blockers, and a short narrative of cycle health.

skills.name: post-project-update
skills.description: Assess a Linear project and post a project update with a health status and progress summary.
skills.content:
# Post Project Update

Write a stakeholder-ready project update in Linear.

## Steps
1. Get Project to read its current state, target date, and lead.
2. Read Issues for the project to gauge progress against the milestone or target date.
3. Decide a health status of on track, at risk, or off track based on remaining work and timeline.
4. Create Project Update with the chosen health and a concise body covering progress, risks, and next steps.

## Output
Confirmation of the posted update, the health status chosen, and the update body.

templates.title: Candidate research enricher

templates.title: Blog-to-LinkedIn repurposer

templates.title: LinkedIn thought-leadership cadence
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that picks the next idea from a content table, expands it into a full LinkedIn post with an agent, shares it to my LinkedIn feed, and logs the publish time back to the row.

skills.name: publish-linkedin-post
skills.description: Draft and share a post to your LinkedIn feed with a hook, value, and a clear call-to-action.
skills.content:
# Publish LinkedIn Post

Write and publish an engagement-optimized post to your LinkedIn feed.

## Steps
1. Take the source idea, article, or update to post about.
2. Draft post text with a strong first-line hook, two to three lines of value or insight, and a clear call-to-action, kept within LinkedIn length limits.
3. Share Post with the drafted text and a visibility of PUBLIC or CONNECTIONS.

## Output
Confirmation the post was shared, the created post ID, and the final post text used.

skills.name: repurpose-content-to-post
skills.description: Turn a blog post, release note, or announcement into a punchy LinkedIn post and share it.
skills.content:
# Repurpose Content to Post

Repurpose long-form content into a native LinkedIn post.

## Steps
1. Read the source content and pull out the single most compelling insight or takeaway.
2. Rewrite it as a standalone LinkedIn post with a hook, a concise body, and a call-to-action or link.
3. Share Post with PUBLIC visibility.

## Output
The published post ID and the post text, plus a note of the source it was derived from.

skills.name: get-my-profile
skills.description: Fetch your LinkedIn profile information for use in downstream personalization or logging.
skills.content:
# Get My Profile

Retrieve your authenticated LinkedIn profile.

## Steps
1. Run Get Profile to fetch the connected account profile.
2. Extract the fields you need, such as name and identifiers, for personalization or record-keeping.

## Output
The profile JSON and a short summary of the key fields available.

templates.title: Linkup research agent
templates.prompt: Build a research agent that uses Linkup to find authoritative sources on a topic, returns answers with citations, and saves long-form research to a knowledge base.

templates.title: Linkup daily digest

templates.title: Linkup competitor monitor

templates.title: Linkup CRM account refresh

templates.title: Linkup + Slack research bot

templates.title: Linkup deep-research file
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that for a chosen topic runs Linkup deep research, captures the structured findings, and writes a full report file with citations.

templates.title: Linkup pipeline-research feeder

skills.name: answer-with-citations
skills.description: Answer a question with Linkup using a sourced answer and surface the supporting source URLs.
skills.content:
# Answer with Citations

Ground an answer in live web facts using Linkup.

## Steps
1. Set the search query to the user question, phrased clearly.
2. Choose the Answer output type and include sources so the response carries verifiable URLs.
3. Use Deep search depth for complex or multi-part questions, otherwise Standard.
4. Present the answer and attach the source links.

## Output
A concise answer followed by a list of the source URLs that support it.

skills.name: gather-research-sources
skills.description: Run a Linkup search and return a ranked list of relevant sources with snippets for a topic.
skills.content:
# Gather Research Sources

Collect authoritative sources on a topic for downstream research.

## Steps
1. Set the search query to the research topic, narrowing with key terms.
2. Choose the Search output type to get raw results with sources.
3. Optionally restrict or exclude domains, and set a from and to date to bound recency.
4. Review the returned sources and order them by relevance.

## Output
A ranked list of sources with titles, URLs, and snippets, ready to feed a summarizer or knowledge base.

skills.name: monitor-topic-mentions
skills.description: Search Linkup for recent mentions of a topic, competitor, or brand within a date window.
skills.content:
# Monitor Topic Mentions

Track fresh mentions of a topic or competitor.

## Steps
1. Set the search query to the brand, competitor, or topic to monitor.
2. Use the Search output type and set the from date to the start of the window you want to cover.
3. Optionally restrict to news or specific domains.
4. Filter the results to genuinely new or relevant mentions and summarize each.

## Output
A list of new mentions with source URL, date, and a one-line summary of each.

templates.title: Linq iMessage campaign sender
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads a contact list from a table, composes a personalized iMessage for each recipient using an agent, and sends them via Linq in batches.

templates.title: Linq SMS support responder

templates.title: Linq RCS notification dispatcher

skills.name: send-personalized-message
skills.description: Start a Linq chat and send a personalized iMessage, SMS, or RCS message to a recipient.
skills.content:
# Send Personalized Message

Reach a person on iMessage, SMS, or RCS through Linq.

## Steps
1. Create Chat with your sending number in From and the recipient handle in To.
2. Draft a friendly, concise message body tailored to the recipient.
3. Send Message to the chat with the message text, optionally setting a preferred service or media URL.
4. Optionally Check iMessage or Check RCS first to pick the best service for the recipient.

## Output
The chat ID, the message ID, the delivery service used, and the delivery status.

skills.name: respond-to-unread-messages
skills.description: List recent Linq chats and messages, draft a reply for each unread conversation, and send it.
skills.content:
# Respond to Unread Messages

Clear an inbox by replying to recent unread Linq conversations.

## Steps
1. List Chats to find active conversations, then List Messages per chat to find unread inbound messages.
2. For each conversation needing a reply, read the recent thread for context.
3. Draft a relevant reply.
4. Send Message to that chat ID with the drafted text.

## Output
For each handled chat: the chat ID, the reply sent, and the delivery status.

skills.name: dispatch-alert-notifications
skills.description: Send an RCS or SMS notification to one or more recipients from a list of alerts.
skills.content:
# Dispatch Alert Notifications

Fan out notifications to recipients through Linq.

## Steps
1. Take the list of recipients and the alert content to send.
2. For each recipient, Create Chat from your sending number to their handle.
3. Format a clear notification message and Send Message, setting the preferred service to RCS or SMS as needed.
4. Use an idempotency key per message so retries do not double-send.

## Output
A per-recipient list of chat IDs, message IDs, and delivery statuses.

skills.name: onboard-new-contact
skills.description: Create a Loops contact on signup and send a transactional welcome email.
skills.content:
# Onboard New Contact

Add a new signup to Loops and welcome them.

## Steps
1. Create Contact with the email, first and last name, and any source or user group, plus custom properties like plan.
2. Send Transactional Email using the welcome template ID, passing the contact data as data variables.
3. Optionally Send Event with a signup event name so any onboarding automation begins.

## Output
The created contact ID, confirmation the welcome email was sent, and any event fired.

skills.name: send-product-event
skills.description: Fire a Loops event for a user with structured properties to trigger lifecycle automations.
skills.content:
# Send Product Event

Drive Loops automations from real product behavior.

## Steps
1. Identify the contact by email or user ID and the event that occurred.
2. Build event properties as a JSON object with the relevant values, such as plan and amount.
3. Send Event with the event name, the contact identifier, and the properties.
4. Optionally update mailing list subscriptions in the same call.

## Output
Confirmation the event was sent, the contact it was attributed to, and the properties included.

skills.name: enrich-contact-properties
skills.description: Find a Loops contact and update it with enriched custom properties and user group.
skills.content:
# Enrich Contact Properties

Keep Loops contact data complete and current.

## Steps
1. Find Contact by email or user ID to read existing fields and spot gaps.
2. Gather the missing or stale values from your source or research.
3. Update Contact with the new custom properties, user group, and any name fields.

## Output
The updated contact ID and a summary of the properties that were set or changed.

skills.name: send-transactional-email
skills.description: Send a Loops transactional email from a template with personalized data variables.
skills.content:
# Send Transactional Email

Deliver a templated transactional email through Loops.

## Steps
1. Confirm the transactional email template ID to use.
2. Build the data variables JSON to match the variable names in the template, such as name and a confirmation URL.
3. Send Transactional Email with the recipient email, template ID, and data variables, attaching files if needed.

## Output
Confirmation of send success and the template ID and recipient used.

skills.name: create-event
skills.description: Create a Luma event with a name, start time, timezone, description, and visibility.
skills.content:
# Create Event

Spin up a new Luma event ready to share.

## Steps
1. Decide the event name, start time as an ISO 8601 timestamp, and the IANA timezone.
2. Create Event with those fields plus an optional end time or duration, a Markdown description, and a meeting URL for virtual events.
3. Set visibility to public, members-only, or private as appropriate.

## Output
The created event ID and URL, with its start time, timezone, and visibility.

skills.name: add-guests-to-event
skills.description: Add a batch of guests to a Luma event from a list of emails and names.
skills.content:
# Add Guests to Event

Bulk-register guests on a Luma event.

## Steps
1. Confirm the target event ID.
2. Build the guests JSON array, one object per guest with an email and optional name or first and last name.
3. Add Guests with the event ID and the guest array.

## Output
Confirmation of how many guests were added and the event ID they were added to.

skills.name: export-guest-list
skills.description: Pull a Luma event guest list, optionally filtered by approval status, for follow-up or enrichment.
skills.content:
# Export Guest List

Retrieve registrants for an event.

## Steps
1. Get Guests for the event ID, optionally filtering by approval status such as approved or waitlist.
2. Page through results using the limit and pagination cursor until the full list is collected.
3. Extract the fields you need, such as email, name, approval status, and registered or checked-in timestamps.

## Output
The full guest list with key fields, ready to segment attendees from no-shows or feed into a CRM.

skills.name: send-event-reminders
skills.description: Pull the Luma guest list and prepare personalized reminders for upcoming registrants.
skills.content:
# Send Event Reminders

Prepare reminder content for an upcoming Luma event.

## Steps
1. Get Event to read the name, start time, timezone, and meeting or location details.
2. Get Guests filtered to approved registrants, paging until complete.
3. For each guest, draft a personalized reminder with the event time in their context and the join or location info.

## Output
A per-guest list of email addresses and drafted reminder messages, ready to hand to an email or messaging step.

skills.name: triage-event-registrations
skills.description: Review pending Luma registrations and approve, waitlist, or decline each guest.
skills.content:
# Triage Event Registrations

Process pending registrations for an event with limited capacity.

## Steps
1. Get Guests filtered to the pending_approval status, paging until complete.
2. Apply your approval criteria to each registrant (for example, work email domain or registration answers).
3. Update Guest Status for each guest to approved, waitlist, or declined, identifying them by email or guest ID.

## Output
Each pending guest moved to a final approval status, with the applied status reported back per guest.

skills.name: invite-guests-to-event
skills.description: Email Luma event invitations to a list of prospects with an optional custom message.
skills.content:
# Invite Guests to Event

Send invitations that recipients can accept, rather than registering them outright.

## Steps
1. Confirm the target event ID.
2. Build a guests JSON array, one object per invitee with an email and optional name.
3. Send Invites with the event ID, the guest array, and an optional short message.

## Output
The count of guests invited, ready to log or report.

skills.name: sync-contact-to-audience
skills.description: Add or update a contact in a Mailchimp audience with merge fields and tags.
skills.content:
# Sync Contact to Audience

Keep a Mailchimp audience in sync with your source of truth.

## Steps
1. If the audience is unknown, Get Audiences to find the right list ID.
2. Use Add or Update Member with the email, subscription status, and merge fields like first and last name.
3. Apply segmentation with Add Member Tags for lifecycle stage or ICP tags.

## Output
The member ID and status in the audience, plus the merge fields and tags applied.

skills.name: create-and-send-campaign
skills.description: Create a Mailchimp campaign, set its content, and send or schedule it to an audience.
skills.content:
# Create and Send Campaign

Launch an email campaign to an audience or segment.

## Steps
1. Create Campaign targeting the audience or a saved segment, with the subject line and from details.
2. Set Campaign Content with the HTML or a template ID.
3. Send Campaign immediately, or Schedule Campaign for a future send time.

## Output
The campaign ID, the audience or segment targeted, and whether it was sent or scheduled with the send time.

skills.name: build-targeted-segment
skills.description: Create a Mailchimp segment from conditions so a campaign can target a specific slice of an audience.
skills.content:
# Build Targeted Segment

Define a reusable audience segment for targeting.

## Steps
1. Identify the audience and the conditions that define the segment, such as tags, merge field values, or activity.
2. Create Segment on that audience with the conditions and a clear name.
3. Optionally Get Segment Members to verify the segment matches the intended contacts.

## Output
The segment ID and name, the conditions used, and the count of matching members.

skills.name: report-campaign-performance
skills.description: Pull Mailchimp campaign reports and summarize open, click, and bounce performance.
skills.content:
# Report Campaign Performance

Turn Mailchimp report data into a readable summary.

## Steps
1. Get Campaign Reports for the recent window, or Get Campaign Report for a specific campaign ID.
2. Extract opens, clicks, bounces, and unsubscribes per campaign.
3. Compute open rate, click rate, and bounce rate and flag campaigns that underperformed.

## Output
A per-campaign metrics summary with rates and a short list of underperformers worth revisiting.

templates.title: Mailgun mailing list builder

templates.title: Mailgun transactional sender

templates.title: Mailgun bounce list hygiene

templates.title: Mailgun domain verification monitor

templates.title: SendGrid + Mailgun send scorecard

templates.title: SES + Mailgun multi-region sender
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that routes transactional emails through SES in primary regions and through Mailgun for regions where SES is not provisioned, normalizing template variables and writing one unified send log to a table.

skills.name: send-transactional-email
skills.description: Send a transactional email through a Mailgun sending domain to one or more recipients.
skills.content:
# Send Transactional Email

Deliver an email through Mailgun.

## Steps
1. Confirm the verified sending domain to use, listing domains first if unsure.
2. Compose the message with from, to, subject, and an HTML or text body.
3. Send Message with those fields, adding CC, BCC, or attachments as needed.

## Output
Confirmation of acceptance with the Mailgun message ID and the recipients it was queued to.

skills.name: track-delivery-events
skills.description: Pull Mailgun events filtered by type to see what was delivered, opened, clicked, or failed.
skills.content:
# Track Delivery Events

Monitor what happened to your Mailgun sends.

## Steps
1. List Messages or query events filtered by an event type such as delivered, failed, opened, or clicked.
2. Group the events by recipient and by type to see delivery outcomes.
3. Highlight failures and bounces that need attention.

## Output
A summary of event counts by type and a list of failed or bounced recipients.

skills.name: sweep-bounces-and-complaints
skills.description: Collect Mailgun failed and complained events and compile the offending addresses for suppression.
skills.content:
# Sweep Bounces and Complaints

Keep your list clean by capturing bad addresses.

## Steps
1. Query Mailgun events filtered to failed and complained types over the chosen window.
2. Extract the recipient addresses and the reason for each.
3. Compile a suppression list of addresses to stop mailing.

## Output
A list of bounced and complained addresses with reasons, ready to write to a suppression table.

skills.name: add-member-to-list
skills.description: Create a Mailgun mailing list if needed and add a subscriber to it.
skills.content:
# Add Member to List

Grow a Mailgun mailing list.

## Steps
1. Get Mailing List to confirm the list exists, or Create Mailing List with the address and access level if it does not.
2. Add List Member with the subscriber email and any name or variables.

## Output
Confirmation the member was added, the list address, and the member email.

templates.title: Mem0 long-term agent memory

templates.title: Mem0 sales-assistant memory

templates.title: Mem0 + Zep hybrid memory agent

templates.title: Mem0 + Slack assistant memory

templates.title: Mem0 + Notion personal-knowledge agent

templates.title: Mem0 customer-preference store

templates.title: Mem0 onboarding-context agent

templates.title: Reducto + Mem0 contract memory
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that parses contracts with Reducto and writes the key terms into Mem0 per counterparty, so future interactions reference the real contract terms.

skills.name: remember-user-context
skills.description: Store new facts and preferences for a user in Mem0 from the latest conversation.
skills.content:
# Remember User Context

Persist what you learned about a user so future sessions stay informed.

## Steps
1. Identify the user ID this memory belongs to.
2. Build the messages array from the relevant conversation turns as role and content objects.
3. Add Memories with the user ID and messages so Mem0 extracts and stores the durable facts.

## Output
Confirmation the memories were added for the user, with the IDs of the facts created.

skills.name: recall-relevant-memories
skills.description: Search a user's Mem0 memories for the facts relevant to the current request before answering.
skills.content:
# Recall Relevant Memories

Ground a response in what Mem0 already knows about the user.

## Steps
1. Identify the user ID.
2. Phrase a search query that captures the current request or topic.
3. Search Memories with the user ID and query.
4. Use the returned memories as context when drafting the answer.

## Output
The most relevant memories for the user and a note of how they should shape the response.

skills.name: review-stored-memories
skills.description: Retrieve a user's stored Mem0 memories, optionally within a date range, to audit what is known.
skills.content:
# Review Stored Memories

Inspect what Mem0 holds for a user.

## Steps
1. Identify the user ID.
2. Get Memories for that user, optionally bounding by a start and end date or a specific memory ID.
3. Page through results if there are many.
4. Summarize the stored facts and flag anything stale or contradictory.

## Output
A readable list of the user's stored memories with a short summary and any items worth updating.

templates.title: Dataverse record sync

templates.title: Dataverse compliance archiver

templates.title: Dataverse case-routing agent

templates.title: Microsoft Planner template launcher
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls Microsoft Dataverse for new projects and creates a Planner plan from the project template, populates the standard buckets, and assigns the right owners.

skills.name: upsert-record
skills.description: Create or update a record in a Dataverse table by its key without duplicating.
skills.content:
# Upsert Record

Keep a Dataverse table in sync from an external source without creating duplicates.

## Steps
1. Identify the target table and the key field that uniquely identifies the record.
2. Map the incoming data to the table column names.
3. Use Upsert Record so an existing match is updated and a new key creates a record.

## Output
The record ID and whether it was created or updated, plus the fields written.

skills.name: query-records
skills.description: List or query Dataverse records with filters and return the matching rows.
skills.content:
# Query Records

Retrieve a filtered set of rows from a Dataverse table.

## Steps
1. Choose the table to query.
2. Use List Records with OData filters, selected columns, and ordering, or use a FetchXML Query for complex joins and aggregates.
3. Page through results until the needed rows are collected.

## Output
The matching records with the selected columns, ready for downstream processing.

skills.name: relevance-search
skills.description: Run a relevance search across Dataverse tables to find records matching a term.
skills.content:
# Relevance Search

Find records across Dataverse using full-text relevance search.

## Steps
1. Take the search term, such as a customer name or case keyword.
2. Use Search with the term, choosing simple or Lucene query syntax and match-any or match-all behavior.
3. Review the ranked matches and pick the relevant record.

## Output
A ranked list of matching records with their table and key fields.

skills.name: bulk-write-records
skills.description: Create or update many Dataverse records in one batch operation.
skills.content:
# Bulk Write Records

Write many Dataverse rows efficiently in a single call.

## Steps
1. Assemble the array of records, mapping each to the table column names.
2. Use Create Multiple to insert new rows, or Update Multiple to change existing rows by ID.
3. Verify the operation succeeded and capture any per-record errors.

## Output
The count of records written, their IDs, and any rows that failed with their error.

skills.name: read-sheet-range
skills.description: Read data from a Microsoft Excel worksheet range and return the rows.
skills.content:
# Read Sheet Range

Pull data out of an Excel workbook for analysis or downstream steps.

## Steps
1. Identify the workbook and the worksheet and range to read.
2. Use Read Data with the spreadsheet ID and range.
3. Parse the returned rows into a structured form for the next step.

## Output
The values from the range as rows, plus the sheet and range they came from.

skills.name: write-sheet-data
skills.description: Write or update values in a Microsoft Excel worksheet range, with formula parsing control.
skills.content:
# Write Sheet Data

Update cells in an Excel workbook.

## Steps
1. Identify the workbook, worksheet, and target range.
2. Prepare the values as rows matching the range shape.
3. Use Write/Update Data, choosing User Entered to parse formulas or Raw to write values literally.

## Output
Confirmation of the cells updated and the range that was written.

skills.name: append-table-row
skills.description: Append a new row to a Microsoft Excel table so it stays structured and formatted.
skills.content:
# Append Table Row

Add a record to an existing Excel table.

## Steps
1. Identify the workbook and the table to append to.
2. Build the row values in the table column order.
3. Use Add to Table to append the row so table formatting and references update automatically.

## Output
Confirmation the row was appended and the table it was added to.

skills.name: add-worksheet
skills.description: Add a new worksheet to a Microsoft Excel workbook to hold a new dataset or report.
skills.content:
# Add Worksheet

Create a fresh worksheet inside a workbook.

## Steps
1. Identify the workbook to add the sheet to.
2. Choose a name for the new worksheet.
3. Use Add Worksheet to create it, then write headers or data with Write/Update Data if needed.

## Output
The new worksheet name and confirmation it was created in the workbook.

skills.name: create-task-in-bucket
skills.description: Create a Microsoft Planner task in a specific plan and bucket with title, due date, and assignee.
skills.content:
# Create Planner Task

Create a new task in a Microsoft Planner plan, placing it in the right bucket and setting a due date and owner.

## Steps
1. Use List Plans to find the target plan, then List Buckets for that plan to locate the bucket id.
2. Run Create Task with the plan id, a clear title, and the bucket id so it lands in the right column.
3. If a due date was described in natural language, convert it to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) before passing dueDateTime.
4. Set assigneeUserId when an owner is known.

## Output
Confirm the created task id and report title, bucket, due date, and assignee. Surface the etag for any follow-up updates.

skills.name: set-up-plan-buckets
skills.description: Create a set of stage or phase buckets in a Planner plan to organize tasks by workflow column.
skills.content:
# Set Up Plan Buckets

Structure a Microsoft Planner plan into the workflow columns a team needs, such as To Do, In Progress, Review, and Done, or project phases.

## Steps
1. Use List Plans to find the target plan, then List Buckets to see which buckets already exist and avoid duplicates.
2. Run Create Bucket once per desired column, passing the plan id and a clear bucket name.
3. Keep names short and ordered so the board reads left to right as work progresses.

## Output
List every bucket id and name that now exists in the plan, marking which were newly created. Suggest the next bucket only if a stage is clearly missing.

skills.name: add-task-checklist
skills.description: Add a step-by-step checklist to a Planner task so each subtask can be tracked and checked off.
skills.content:
# Add Task Checklist

Break a Microsoft Planner task into trackable subtasks using its checklist.

## Steps
1. Identify the target task id, using Read Task to confirm the title if needed.
2. Use Get Task Details to read the current checklist and capture the etag required for updates.
3. Run Update Task Details with the checklist items to add, passing the etag from the previous step.
4. Set percentComplete on the task with Update Task when progress should reflect the checklist state.

## Output
Confirm the task id and list the checklist items now present. Note the refreshed etag for any further edits.
