skills.name: post-channel-announcement
skills.description: Write a formatted message to a specific Microsoft Teams channel.
skills.content:
# Post Channel Announcement

Send an announcement or update to a Microsoft Teams channel.

## Steps
1. Identify the team and channel to post to, selecting the channel id.
2. Compose the message body, using clear headings and bullets so it reads well in Teams.
3. Run Write Channel Message with the channel id and the formatted content.
4. If a thread already exists for the topic, use Reply to Channel Message instead to keep context together.

## Output
Confirm the posted message id and channel. Quote the first line of what was posted.

skills.name: summarize-channel-activity
skills.description: Read recent Microsoft Teams channel messages and produce a concise digest of decisions and action items.
skills.content:
# Summarize Channel Activity

Turn a busy Microsoft Teams channel into a short readable digest.

## Steps
1. Run Read Channel Messages for the target channel.
2. Group messages by topic or thread and drop noise such as greetings and reactions.
3. Extract decisions made, open questions, and any explicit action items with owners.
4. Optionally post the digest back to the channel as a new message.

## Output
Three short sections: Decisions, Open Questions, Action Items. Each item one line with the person responsible when known.

skills.name: acknowledge-with-reaction
skills.description: React to a specific Microsoft Teams message to acknowledge it.
skills.content:
# Acknowledge with Reaction

Add or remove an emoji reaction on a Microsoft Teams message.

## Steps
1. Locate the message using Get Message or the known message id and channel/chat id.
2. Run Add Reaction with the desired reactionType to acknowledge or signal status.
3. Use Remove Reaction when the acknowledgment should be cleared.

## Output
Confirm the reaction applied and on which message. Keep the response to one line.

skills.name: list-team-members
skills.description: List the members of a Microsoft Teams team or channel for routing or auditing.
skills.content:
# List Team Members

Retrieve who belongs to a Microsoft Teams team or channel.

## Steps
1. Decide whether you need team-wide membership or a single channel and pick List Team Members or List Channel Members.
2. Run the operation with the team id (and channel id when needed).
3. Normalize the result into a clean roster of names and roles.

## Output
A roster list with display name and role. Note the total count at the top.

skills.name: pdf-to-markdown
skills.description: Convert a PDF document into clean structured Markdown using Mistral OCR.
skills.content:
# PDF to Markdown

Use Mistral Parser to turn a PDF, including scanned image-only pages, into clean Markdown.

## Steps
1. Provide the PDF as a URL or uploaded file to the parser.
2. Run the parse to extract text, headings, tables, and layout into Markdown.
3. Review the Markdown for page-break artifacts and stray headers or footers and clean them.

## Output
Return the full Markdown. Note the page count and flag any pages where OCR confidence looked low.

skills.name: extract-document-fields
skills.description: Parse a PDF and pull specific structured fields such as totals, dates, or names.
skills.content:
# Extract Document Fields

Extract a defined set of fields from a document such as an invoice, statement, or contract.

## Steps
1. Run Mistral Parser on the source PDF to get the text content.
2. Locate the requested fields (for example vendor, total, due date, line items) within the parsed text.
3. Return the fields as a structured object, leaving any field that is genuinely absent as null rather than guessing.

## Output
A JSON object keyed by the requested field names. List any fields that could not be found.

skills.name: summarize-long-document
skills.description: Parse a long PDF and produce a concise summary of its key points.
skills.content:
# Summarize Long Document

Produce a readable summary from a long PDF such as a report, paper, or agreement.

## Steps
1. Parse the PDF with Mistral Parser to get its full text.
2. Identify the main sections and the most important claims, findings, or obligations.
3. Write a tight summary that preserves specifics like figures and dates.

## Output
A short summary with a few bullet highlights. Keep numbers and named entities exact.

skills.name: create-board-item
skills.description: Create a new item on a Monday board in the right group with column values set.
skills.content:
# Create Board Item

Add an item to a Monday.com board and populate its columns.

## Steps
1. Use List Boards to find the board, then Get Board to read its groups and column ids.
2. Run Create Item with the board id, item name, and the target group.
3. Map the requested fields to the correct column ids, formatting status and date columns as Monday expects.
4. Add a follow-up Create Update if a comment or context note is needed on the item.

## Output
Confirm the new item id, board, and group. List the column values that were set.

skills.name: find-items-by-criteria
skills.description: Search a Monday board for items matching a value such as status or owner.
skills.content:
# Find Items by Criteria

Locate Monday.com items that match a given condition.

## Steps
1. Identify the board and the column to filter on with Get Board.
2. Use Search Items or Get Items to retrieve candidates.
3. Filter to the items whose column value matches the requested criteria.

## Output
A list of matching items with name, group, and the relevant column values. Note the total match count.

skills.name: progress-item-status
skills.description: Move a Monday item forward by updating its status column and group.
skills.content:
# Progress Item Status

Advance a Monday.com item through its workflow.

## Steps
1. Get the item with Get Item to read its current status and group.
2. Run Update Item to set the new status column value.
3. If the stage maps to a different group, use Move Item to Group to keep the board organized.
4. Optionally post a Create Update noting the transition.

## Output
Confirm the item id, the old and new status, and the group it now sits in.

skills.name: find-documents
skills.description: Query a MongoDB collection with a filter and return the matching documents.
skills.content:
# Find Documents

Retrieve documents from a MongoDB collection that match a filter.

## Steps
1. If the collection shape is unknown, run Introspect Database first to learn the fields.
2. Build a MongoDB filter document for the requested condition, using operators like $gte, $in, and $regex as needed.
3. Run Find Documents against the target collection with the filter, plus projection and limit when appropriate.

## Output
Return the matching documents. State the filter used and the number of results. Suggest an index if a scan looks slow.

skills.name: aggregate-report
skills.description: Run a MongoDB aggregation pipeline to group and summarize collection data.
skills.content:
# Aggregate Report

Produce a summary from a MongoDB collection using an aggregation pipeline.

## Steps
1. Introspect the collection to confirm the fields to group and measure on.
2. Compose a pipeline with stages such as $match, $group, $sort, and $limit to compute the requested metric.
3. Run the Aggregate Pipeline operation and read back the grouped results.

## Output
A compact table of the grouped metrics. Include the pipeline used so the query can be rerun.

skills.name: upsert-document
skills.description: Insert a new MongoDB document or update an existing one matched by a key.
skills.content:
# Upsert Document

Write a document to MongoDB, creating it or updating the existing match.

## Steps
1. Determine the key field that identifies the record uniquely.
2. Run Find Documents on that key to see whether a record already exists.
3. If it exists, run Update Documents with the new values; otherwise run Insert Documents.

## Output
Report whether a document was inserted or updated and echo the key value. Confirm the affected count.

skills.name: answer-graph-question
skills.description: Translate a plain-English question into Cypher, run it on Neo4j, and explain the result.
skills.content:
# Answer Graph Question

Turn a natural-language question into a Cypher query against the Neo4j graph.

## Steps
1. Run Introspect Schema to learn the node labels, relationship types, and properties.
2. Translate the question into a Cypher MATCH that uses the real labels and relationships from the schema.
3. Run the Query operation and read the returned rows.
4. If the query returns nothing, relax the pattern and explain what was tried.

## Output
A plain-language answer plus the Cypher used and the key matching nodes or paths.

skills.name: create-graph-relationship
skills.description: Create or merge nodes and connect them with a relationship in Neo4j.
skills.content:
# Create Graph Relationship

Add nodes and a relationship between them without creating duplicates.

## Steps
1. Introspect Schema to confirm the labels and relationship type to use.
2. Use Merge (Find or Create) for each node so existing nodes are reused rather than duplicated.
3. Create the relationship between them with the requested direction and any properties.

## Output
Confirm the nodes involved and the relationship created, noting whether each node was found or newly created.

skills.name: find-connected-nodes
skills.description: Traverse the Neo4j graph from a starting node to find related entities.
skills.content:
# Find Connected Nodes

Explore the neighborhood of a node to find connected entities.

## Steps
1. Introspect Schema to know the relationship types available.
2. Build a Cypher MATCH that starts at the given node and traverses the relevant relationships to the desired depth.
3. Run the Query operation and collect the connected nodes.

## Output
A list of connected nodes grouped by relationship type, with the traversal path described in one line.

skills.name: query-golden-signals
skills.description: Run NRQL to pull latency, error rate, and throughput for a service over a time window.
skills.content:
# Query Golden Signals

Use New Relic NRQL to read the golden signals for a service.

## Steps
1. Identify the service or application name, using Search Entities if it is unknown.
2. Build NRQL queries for throughput, average and p95 latency, and error rate over the requested window using SELECT ... FROM Transaction WHERE appName = ... SINCE ...
3. Run NRQL Query for each signal and collect the values.

## Output
A short table of throughput, latency p50/p95, and error rate with the time window stated. Flag any signal that looks anomalous.

skills.name: investigate-error-spike
skills.description: Use NRQL to break down a New Relic error spike by type and impacted transaction.
skills.content:
# Investigate Error Spike

Drill into an error spike for a service in New Relic.

## Steps
1. Run an NRQL query counting errors over time to confirm and bound the spike window.
2. Break the errors down by error.class, message, and transactionName using FACET.
3. Use Get Entity to add context such as the service health and recent alerts.
4. Check for a recent Create Deployment Event near the spike start to correlate with a release.

## Output
The top error types by count, the most impacted transactions, and whether a recent deployment lines up with the spike.

skills.name: record-deployment-marker
skills.description: Create a New Relic deployment event so releases line up with metric changes.
skills.content:
# Record Deployment Marker

Mark a deployment in New Relic to correlate releases with performance.

## Steps
1. Identify the target entity with Search Entities to get its GUID.
2. Run Create Deployment Event with the version, and include the commit or changelog and the user who deployed.
3. Confirm the marker is associated with the right entity.

## Output
Confirm the deployment event created, with the entity name, version, and timestamp.

skills.name: create-structured-page
skills.description: Create a Notion page under a parent with headings, bullets, and a clean layout.
skills.content:
# Create Structured Page

Create a well-formatted Notion page, such as meeting notes or a project brief.

## Steps
1. Identify the parent page or database, using Search Workspace if the destination is not known.
2. Run Create Page with the title and parent.
3. Use Append Content to add the body as Notion blocks: headings for sections, bulleted lists for items, and to-do blocks for action items.

## Output
Return the new page URL and id. Summarize the sections that were added.

skills.name: add-database-entry
skills.description: Add a row to a Notion database with the correct property values.
skills.content:
# Add Database Entry

Insert a new row into a Notion database with its properties set.

## Steps
1. Run Read Database on the target database to learn its property names and types.
2. Map the requested values to the matching properties, formatting select, date, and relation fields correctly.
3. Run Add Database Row with the property values.

## Output
Confirm the new row id and URL, and list the property values that were written.

skills.name: query-database
skills.description: Filter and sort a Notion database to return matching entries.
skills.content:
# Query Database

Retrieve entries from a Notion database that match a condition.

## Steps
1. Read the database with Read Database to confirm the property to filter on.
2. Build a filter and optional sort for the requested condition (for example Status equals Done, sorted by date).
3. Run Query Database and collect the matching pages.

## Output
A list of matching entries with their key properties and page links. Note the total count.

skills.name: search-and-summarize
skills.description: Search the Notion workspace for a topic and summarize the relevant pages.
skills.content:
# Search and Summarize

Find and summarize Notion content on a given topic.

## Steps
1. Run Search Workspace with the topic keywords.
2. Read the most relevant pages with Read Page.
3. Synthesize the key points across the pages, citing each source page by title and link.

## Output
A short synthesized answer with citations to the Notion pages used. Note if the workspace had no relevant content.

skills.name: capture-note
skills.description: Create a new Obsidian note with Markdown content at a chosen vault path.
skills.content:
# Capture Note

Write a new note into the Obsidian vault.

## Steps
1. Decide the vault path and filename for the note, keeping folder conventions consistent.
2. Compose the Markdown body with a clear title heading and any tags or frontmatter wanted.
3. Run Create Note with the path and content. If the note may already exist, use Append to Note instead to avoid overwriting.

## Output
Confirm the note path created and summarize what was captured.

skills.name: append-to-daily-note
skills.description: Append an entry to the Obsidian periodic daily note.
skills.content:
# Append to Daily Note

Add a timestamped entry to the current daily note.

## Steps
1. Use Get Periodic Note to confirm the daily note exists and read its current content if needed.
2. Format the entry as a Markdown bullet or section, including a timestamp where useful.
3. Run Append to Periodic Note to add it to the day.

## Output
Confirm the entry was appended to the daily note and quote the line added.

skills.name: search-vault
skills.description: Search the Obsidian vault for notes matching a query and summarize matches.
skills.content:
# Search Vault

Find notes in the Obsidian vault that mention a topic.

## Steps
1. Run Search with the query terms.
2. Open the most relevant results with Get Note to read their content.
3. Summarize the findings, linking each note by its path.

## Output
A short synthesis of what the vault says about the topic, with the source note paths listed.

skills.name: onboard-user
skills.description: Create an Okta user, set their profile, and add them to the right groups.
skills.content:
# Onboard User

Provision a new user in Okta and grant their group access.

## Steps
1. Run Create User with the profile fields: first name, last name, email, and login.
2. Determine the groups the role requires, using List Groups to resolve group ids.
3. Run Add User to Group for each required group.
4. Activate the user if it was created in a staged state.

## Output
Confirm the new user id and login, and list the groups they were added to.

skills.name: offboard-user
skills.description: Deactivate an Okta user and remove their group memberships during offboarding.
skills.content:
# Offboard User

Revoke access for a departing user in Okta.

## Steps
1. Find the user with List Users or Get User to confirm the user id.
2. Run Deactivate User (or Suspend User for a temporary hold) to block sign-in.
3. Remove the user from sensitive groups with Remove User from Group.
4. Only run Delete User when permanent removal is explicitly requested, since it is irreversible.

## Output
Confirm the user status and the groups removed. State clearly whether the account was deactivated or deleted.

skills.name: audit-group-membership
skills.description: List Okta groups and their members to audit access for a security review.
skills.content:
# Audit Group Membership

Review who belongs to Okta groups, focusing on privileged access.

## Steps
1. Run List Groups to enumerate the groups, or Get Group for a specific one.
2. For each group of interest, run List Group Members.
3. Highlight privileged or admin groups and call out any unexpected members.

## Output
A per-group roster with member counts, and a short list of access concerns to review.

skills.name: reset-user-password
skills.description: Trigger an Okta password reset for a user who is locked out.
skills.content:
# Reset User Password

Help a user regain access by resetting their Okta password.

## Steps
1. Locate the user with Get User to confirm identity.
2. Run Reset Password to start the reset flow for that user.
3. If the account is suspended, run Unsuspend User first so the reset can proceed.

## Output
Confirm the reset was initiated for the named user and note any prerequisite step that was taken.

templates.title: OneDrive contract intake
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls a OneDrive intake folder for new contract PDFs, extracts clauses with Reducto, writes the structured terms to a table, and pings legal in Teams.

templates.title: OneDrive sharing audit
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled weekly workflow that lists OneDrive files shared externally, flags ones above a sensitivity score, and writes a security review report.

templates.title: OneDrive to knowledge base sync
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that mirrors OneDrive folders into a knowledge base, chunks and embeds new content on change, and removes deleted files so retrieval stays accurate.

templates.title: OneDrive backup verifier
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that verifies OneDrive backups by sampling files and comparing checksums against the originating SharePoint copy, writing the report to an SRE table.

templates.title: OneDrive retention cleaner
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that finds OneDrive files older than the retention horizon, requires manager approval through Teams, and archives or deletes per the policy.

templates.title: OneDrive Excel-pipeline opener
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls OneDrive for new Excel data drops, normalizes each, writes to a downstream table, and emails the analyst that the latest file is ready.

templates.title: OneDrive new-hire kit deployer
templates.prompt: Create a workflow triggered by a Workday new hire that creates a OneDrive new-hire folder, uploads the standard onboarding documents into it, and writes the folder link into the onboarding tracker.

skills.name: upload-file-to-folder
skills.description: Upload a file to a specific OneDrive folder, creating the folder if needed.
skills.content:
# Upload File to Folder

Place a file into the right OneDrive folder.

## Steps
1. Use List Files to confirm the destination folder exists; if not, run Create Folder.
2. Run Upload File with the file content and the target folder.
3. Use a clear, consistent filename so the document is easy to find later.

## Output
Confirm the uploaded file name, its folder, and the file id or link.

skills.name: find-and-download-file
skills.description: Locate a file in OneDrive by name and download its contents.
skills.content:
# Find and Download File

Retrieve a file from OneDrive for processing.

## Steps
1. Run List Files in the likely folder to find the file and its id.
2. Run Download File with the matched file id.
3. Pass the downloaded content to the next step, such as a parser or summarizer.

## Output
Confirm the file downloaded with its name and size, and hand off the content.

skills.name: save-generated-document
skills.description: Create a new text or document file in OneDrive from generated content, in the right folder.
skills.content:
# Save Generated Document

Write generated content, such as a report or notes, into OneDrive as a new file.

## Steps
1. Use List Files to confirm the destination folder exists; if not, run Create Folder.
2. Compose the document content and choose a clear filename and type.
3. Run Create File with the content, filename, and target folder.

## Output
Confirm the created file name, its folder, and the file id or link.

templates.title: Outlook auto-responder
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that monitors my Outlook inbox, drafts a contextual reply for every email that needs a response using my recent threads as tone reference, and saves each reply as an Outlook draft for me to review and send.

templates.title: Outlook customer escalation to Zendesk
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that reads new Outlook emails from customers, classifies whether each one is a support issue, and when it is, creates a Zendesk ticket with the email body, attachments, and contact details, then replies from Outlook with the ticket number.

templates.title: Outlook executive triage
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that scans Outlook every hour, ranks new emails by urgency, summarizes the top items, and posts a prioritized digest to a Slack channel so executives can act without opening the inbox.

templates.title: Outlook invoice extractor
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that monitors Outlook for invoice attachments, extracts vendor, amount, due date, and line items from each PDF, and logs the results to a tracking table while moving the original email to an Invoices folder.

templates.title: Outlook follow-up reminder
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that scans Outlook for sent emails awaiting a reply older than three business days, drafts a polite follow-up email per thread, and saves each one as a draft in Outlook ready to send.

templates.title: Outlook to JSM ticket router
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads support requests arriving in a shared Outlook mailbox, classifies the request type, and creates a Jira Service Management request in the correct service desk with the right request type, then replies from Outlook with the JSM portal link.

templates.title: Outlook newsletter clipper
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that reads newsletters arriving in Outlook, summarizes each one into key takeaways, and appends the digest to a daily Notion page so the inbox stays clean and the insights stay searchable.

templates.title: Outlook contract clause flagger
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that scans Outlook for inbound contracts and amendments, extracts key clauses (payment terms, liability, termination, renewal), flags deviations from my standard terms, and replies internally with a summary and red-flag list.

skills.name: send-email
skills.description: Compose and send an Outlook email to one or more recipients.
skills.content:
# Send Email

Send a message from the connected Outlook account.

## Steps
1. Gather the recipients, subject, and the body content.
2. Write a clear subject and a concise, well-structured body.
3. Run Send Email with the recipients, subject, and body. Use Draft Email instead when the message should be reviewed before sending.

## Output
Confirm the email was sent, listing recipients and subject. If drafted, note that it awaits review.

skills.name: triage-inbox
skills.description: Read recent Outlook emails and summarize which ones need a reply or action.
skills.content:
# Triage Inbox

Turn a noisy Outlook inbox into a short action list.

## Steps
1. Run Read Email to pull recent unread messages.
2. Classify each as needs reply, needs action, FYI, or ignore.
3. For handled messages, run Mark as Read; leave items that still need a reply unread.

## Output
A prioritized list of emails that need attention, each with sender, subject, and the suggested next action.

skills.name: forward-with-context
skills.description: Forward an Outlook email to the right person with an added note.
skills.content:
# Forward with Context

Route an email to the correct owner with a short explanation.

## Steps
1. Read the target email to capture its content with Read Email.
2. Identify the correct recipient for the topic.
3. Run Forward Email to that recipient, adding a brief note on why it is being forwarded and what is needed.

## Output
Confirm the email was forwarded, to whom, and the note that was added.

skills.name: file-email-to-folder
skills.description: Move an Outlook email to the appropriate folder to keep the inbox clean.
skills.content:
# File Email to Folder

Organize the inbox by moving a message into the right folder.

## Steps
1. Identify the email and the destination folder.
2. Run Move Email to relocate the message.
3. Optionally run Mark as Read so it does not linger as unread.

## Output
Confirm the email moved, naming the source and destination folders.

templates.title: CloudWatch log triage

templates.title: CloudWatch SLO burn-rate watcher

templates.title: CodePipeline flaky-stage retrier

templates.title: Incident response coordinator

templates.title: CrowdStrike sensor coverage gaps

templates.title: Datadog deploy guardrail

templates.title: Elasticsearch log triage
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that runs saved Elasticsearch queries hourly for error patterns, clusters the matches, writes the top groups to a triage table, and pings on-call.

templates.title: Elasticsearch security event correlator
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that pulls Elasticsearch security events, correlates them across sources, and opens a CrowdStrike or PagerDuty incident on a confirmed pattern.

templates.title: BigQuery anomaly notifier
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that runs BigQuery anomaly-detection queries on key metrics hourly, writes any anomalies to a tracking table, and pages the on-call data team on severe deltas.

templates.title: PageSpeed CWV regression watcher
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that runs Google PageSpeed Insights daily for the top pages, captures Core Web Vitals, and pages on-call when LCP or CLS regress beyond threshold.

templates.title: Grafana alert auto-context
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls Grafana for firing alert rules, pulls related logs and recent deploys, summarizes them with an agent, and posts the enriched alert to PagerDuty and Slack.

templates.title: Grafana incident annotator

templates.title: incident.io commander

templates.title: JSM major incident broadcaster
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered when a major-incident request is created in Jira Service Management that pulls the affected service from PagerDuty, identifies the current on-call, posts a structured incident brief to a Slack war-room channel, and adds the responders as JSM request participants.

templates.title: Teams incident war room
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered by a PagerDuty incident that creates a Microsoft Teams war-room channel, invites responders, posts the incident summary, and keeps the channel name in sync with incident state.

templates.title: New Relic incident war-room kickoff
templates.prompt: Create a workflow triggered by a PagerDuty incident that runs NRQL queries for the impacted service, pulls the latest deployment change event from New Relic, and posts a war-room summary with golden-signal charts to the incident Slack channel.

templates.title: PagerDuty incident war room
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls PagerDuty for new severity-1 incidents, opens a Slack war-room channel, invites responders, posts the incident summary, and updates the channel topic with status.

templates.title: PagerDuty on-call digest

templates.title: PagerDuty escalation auditor

templates.title: PagerDuty postmortem starter

templates.title: PagerDuty auto-triage enricher
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls PagerDuty for new incidents, pulls the affected service details, queries recent logs and the latest deploy, and posts an enriched triage summary with likely cause back as an incident note for the responder.

templates.title: PagerDuty customer-impact notifier
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls PagerDuty for incidents on customer-facing services, looks up affected accounts in Salesforce, and drafts a status-page update plus a Slack alert to the customer success team for high-impact outages.

templates.title: PagerDuty alert-to-ticket bridge
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that creates a PagerDuty incident from inbound monitoring alerts, opens a matching Linear issue with the same severity and links the two, and logs the pairing in a table so engineering can track alert-to-fix time.

templates.title: Reddit crisis-signal alerter
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls Reddit for sudden bursts of negative posts about the brand, classifies severity, and pages the PR team via Slack and PagerDuty when a real crisis emerges.

templates.title: Alert fan-out queue
templates.prompt: Create a workflow triggered by PagerDuty or Datadog alerts that classifies severity, decorates the payload with runbook context, and pushes the enriched alert to an Amazon SQS queue so multiple downstream notifiers and ticketing systems can consume it independently.

templates.title: Telegram alert relay
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that listens for critical alerts from Sentry or PagerDuty and forwards a concise summary with severity, link, and the on-call person to a Telegram group.

templates.title: Temporal incident escalation bridge
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that signals a Temporal incident-response workflow with escalation details when a monitoring alert fires, using signal-with-start so a new incident workflow is created if one is not already running.

templates.title: Tinybird realtime metric watcher
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that polls a Tinybird pipe every minute for a realtime KPI, compares against a rolling baseline, and pages PagerDuty when the metric crosses a SLO threshold.

templates.title: Twilio incident escalation alerts
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered by a PagerDuty incident that sends a Twilio SMS to the on-call engineer with the service name and severity so critical alerts reach them even when they are away from Slack.

templates.title: Twilio Voice incident dialer
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that on a PagerDuty severity-1 incident places a Twilio Voice call to the on-call engineer with an automated message, escalates to backup if no answer, and logs the cascade.

templates.title: Upstash cache warmer
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that precomputes expensive query results and writes them into Upstash Redis with a TTL using SET, so hot paths stay warm and pages PagerDuty if a warm-up run fails.

skills.name: open-incident
skills.description: Create a PagerDuty incident on a service with a title, urgency, and description so responders get paged.
skills.content:
# Open Incident

Create a new PagerDuty incident and page the on-call responder.

## Steps
1. Use the Create Incident operation with the target Service ID and a clear, specific Title summarizing the problem.
2. Set Urgency (high or low) based on customer impact and add a Description with affected systems, symptoms, and any error signatures.
3. Optionally set an Escalation Policy ID or Assignee User ID to route the page directly.
4. Capture the returned incident ID, number, and web URL for follow-up.

## Output
Report the new incident number, urgency, assigned service, and the PagerDuty URL so the team can jump straight to the incident.

skills.name: triage-active-incidents
skills.description: List triggered and acknowledged PagerDuty incidents and produce a prioritized triage summary.
skills.content:
# Triage Active Incidents

Review what is currently on fire and summarize it for the team.

## Steps
1. Use List Incidents filtered to Triggered then Acknowledged statuses, sorted by created at (newest first).
2. Optionally scope to specific Service IDs or a Since window to focus on a team or recent activity.
3. Group results by service and urgency, flagging high-urgency triggered incidents that are still unacknowledged.
4. For each, note title, age, status, and the responsible service.

## Output
A prioritized list leading with unacknowledged high-urgency incidents, including incident number, service, age, and URL.

skills.name: resolve-and-note-incident
skills.description: Update a PagerDuty incident status and add a resolution note documenting what was done.
skills.content:
# Resolve and Note Incident

Close out an incident with a clear audit trail.

## Steps
1. Use Update Incident with the Incident ID and set Status to acknowledged or resolved as appropriate.
2. Use Add Note on the same Incident ID to record the root cause, the fix applied, and any follow-up actions.
3. Provide a valid From Email (a real PagerDuty user) since these write operations require it.
4. Confirm the new status from the response.

## Output
State the incident number, its new status, and a one-line summary of the note that was attached.

skills.name: check-whos-on-call
skills.description: List current PagerDuty on-call assignments for given schedules or escalation policies.
skills.content:
# Check Who Is On Call

Find the right person to reach right now.

## Steps
1. Use List On-Calls, optionally scoped by Escalation Policy IDs or Schedule IDs.
2. Set a Since and Until window to look at the current or an upcoming shift.
3. Map each on-call entry to its escalation level so primary versus backup responders are clear.

## Output
A concise roster: who is on call at level 1 (primary) and level 2 (backup) per schedule, with the time window covered.

templates.title: Parallel AI account research agent
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes a company name, runs Parallel AI deep research for recent funding, leadership changes, and product launches, and writes a structured account brief with citations back to the matching CRM record.

templates.title: Parallel AI competitor monitor
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that uses Parallel AI search to find new announcements from a list of competitors, extracts the key details from each source URL, and posts a cited digest to Slack for the product team.

templates.title: Parallel AI URL fact extractor
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads a table of source URLs, uses Parallel AI extract to pull the structured facts requested for each page, and writes the normalized results back to the table for review.

templates.title: Parallel AI market landscape report
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that runs Parallel AI deep research on a market category, synthesizes the players, pricing, and trends into a Markdown report file, and shares the link with the strategy team.

templates.title: Parallel AI lead enrichment pipeline
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs Parallel AI search and extract on each new inbound lead to find company size, industry, and tech stack, scores fit against the ICP, and updates the lead record with the enriched profile.

templates.title: Parallel AI due-diligence brief
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that runs Parallel AI deep research on a target company for litigation, leadership, and financial signals, extracts supporting detail from each cited source, and writes a due-diligence brief file for the deal team.

templates.title: Parallel AI daily topic digest
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled daily workflow that uses Parallel AI search across the topics a team follows, extracts the key facts from the top results, and emails a concise cited digest each morning.

skills.name: research-company-brief
skills.description: Run Parallel AI deep research on a company and produce a cited brief covering funding, leadership, and product.
skills.content:
# Research Company Brief

Generate a sourced account brief for a target company.

## Steps
1. Use the Deep Research operation with a Research Query naming the company and the angles to cover: recent funding, leadership changes, product launches, and notable news.
2. Choose a processor tier (Pro for balance, Ultra for depth) and optionally constrain Include or Exclude Domains.
3. Read the structured content plus the basis field for citations and confidence per claim.

## Output
A brief organized by topic, where every claim links to its source URL from the basis, and note any low-confidence items that need verification.

skills.name: web-search-with-objective
skills.description: Use Parallel AI search to answer a question across the web and return ranked, cited results.
skills.content:
# Web Search With Objective

Answer a factual question grounded in fresh web sources.

## Steps
1. Use the Search operation and state a clear Objective describing what you want to know and which sources to prefer.
2. Optionally add specific Search Queries, set a Search Mode (one-shot, agentic, or fast), and limit results with Include or Exclude Domains.
3. Tune Max Results and Max Chars Per Result for breadth versus depth.

## Output
A direct answer to the objective followed by the supporting results, each with title, URL, and the relevant excerpt.

skills.name: extract-facts-from-urls
skills.description: Use Parallel AI extract to pull structured facts from a list of source URLs.
skills.content:
# Extract Facts From URLs

Turn a set of pages into structured data.

## Steps
1. Use the Extract operation and provide the comma-separated URLs to read.
2. Set an Extract Objective describing exactly which fields to pull from each page.
3. Enable Include Excerpts for supporting snippets and Include Full Content only when the whole page text is needed.

## Output
A normalized record per URL with the requested fields and an excerpt backing each value, plus a note on any URL that could not be parsed.

skills.name: monitor-competitor-news
skills.description: Search Parallel AI for recent announcements from named competitors and summarize the changes.
skills.content:
# Monitor Competitor News

Track what rivals shipped or announced recently.

## Steps
1. Use the Search operation with an Objective naming the competitors and the timeframe of interest.
2. Optionally restrict Include Domains to the competitors official sites and reputable news outlets.
3. For high-signal hits, follow up with the Extract operation to pull the specific details from each announcement URL.

## Output
A dated digest grouped by competitor, each item a one-line summary with its source URL and why it matters.

templates.title: PDL person enricher
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that watches CRM contacts, enriches each via People Data Labs with role, seniority, and company signals, and writes the enriched data back.

templates.title: PDL company enricher
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that takes a list of company domains, runs People Data Labs company-search, and writes firmographics, employee count, and tech stack into a tables-based research base.

templates.title: PDL ICP scorer
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that scores inbound leads against the ICP using People Data Labs enrichment fields, routes high-fit leads to sales, and writes the score back to the CRM.

templates.title: PDL CRM gap-filler
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that finds CRM contacts missing key fields, runs People Data Labs to fill gaps, and writes coverage metrics to a hygiene table.

templates.title: PDL lookalike expander
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that derives firmographic attributes from a seed account list and uses People Data Labs company-search to find similar companies, expanding the TAM and writing the new prospects into Salesforce.

templates.title: PDL hiring-signal alerter
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that runs People Data Labs person-search for new hires in relevant roles at tracked accounts and posts a Slack alert when a match appears.

templates.title: PDL + Email Bison outbound
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs People Data Labs on prospects, drafts a personalized first-touch email based on enrichment fields, and sends via Email Bison.

skills.name: enrich-person
skills.description: Enrich a single person from an email, LinkedIn URL, or name plus company using People Data Labs.
skills.content:
# Enrich Person

Fill in a full profile for one contact.

## Steps
1. Use the Person Enrich operation and provide the strongest identifier available: Email or LinkedIn URL first, otherwise First and Last Name plus Company.
2. Set a Min Likelihood (for example 6) to avoid weak matches.
3. Read the matched person record for job title, seniority, company, location, and contact fields, and check the likelihood score.

## Output
The enriched profile (title, seniority, company, location, emails) plus the match likelihood; if not matched, say so and list which identifiers were tried.

skills.name: search-people-by-criteria
skills.description: Search the People Data Labs person dataset by role, location, or company using SQL or Elasticsearch DSL.
skills.content:
# Search People By Criteria

Find people matching a target profile.

## Steps
1. Use the Person Search operation and write a SQL query (for example filter on job_title and location_country) or an Elasticsearch DSL query for finer control.
2. Set Result Size for the page, and optionally a Dataset filter (such as email or mobile_phone) to require certain coverage.
3. To page through more results, pass the returned scroll token on the next call.

## Output
The list of matched people with key fields, the total dataset match count, and the scroll token to fetch the next page.

skills.name: enrich-company
skills.description: Enrich a company from a name, website, or LinkedIn URL to get firmographics with People Data Labs.
skills.content:
# Enrich Company

Build a firmographic profile for one company.

## Steps
1. Use the Company Enrich operation and provide a Website (most reliable), Company Name, ticker, or LinkedIn URL.
2. Optionally add a Location or PDL Company ID to disambiguate common names, and set Min Likelihood.
3. Read the matched company record for industry, employee count, headquarters, and tech-related signals.

## Output
The company firmographics (industry, size, location, founded, website) with the match confidence noted.

skills.name: bulk-enrich-contacts
skills.description: Enrich many people or companies in one call with People Data Labs bulk enrichment.
skills.content:
# Bulk Enrich Contacts

Enrich a batch of records efficiently.

## Steps
1. Use Bulk Person Enrich (or Bulk Company Enrich) and pass a JSON array of request objects, each with its own params such as a LinkedIn URL, email, or website.
2. Optionally set a Required Fields expression (for example emails AND job_title) so only records with that coverage are returned.
3. Iterate the results array in order, matching each result back to its input record.

## Output
A per-record summary listing which inputs matched, the enriched fields returned, and which inputs had no match for follow-up.

templates.title: DuckDuckGo agent fallback
templates.prompt: Create an agent that uses Perplexity for primary search and falls back to DuckDuckGo on rate-limit errors so research workflows remain reliable.

templates.title: Perplexity research briefer
templates.prompt: Build an agent that takes a topic or company name, runs deep web research via Perplexity with citations, and saves a structured brief file with sources, key findings, and open questions.

templates.title: Daily news brief via Perplexity
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled daily workflow that queries Perplexity for the latest news on topics I follow, summarizes each thread with citations, and posts the digest to Slack.

templates.title: Multi-source research agent
templates.prompt: Create an agent that triangulates a topic across Perplexity, Exa, and Tavily, deduplicates findings, and produces a consensus brief with confidence scores per claim.

templates.title: Perplexity sales account refresh
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that walks accounts in my CRM, runs Perplexity research on each for new funding, headcount changes, or product launches, and writes the digest back to the account record.

templates.title: Perplexity + DSPy structured-output evaluator
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs DSPy programs against a Perplexity-backed retrieval layer, evaluates outputs with Hugging Face and Mistral parsers, and writes regression scores to a tracking table.

templates.title: Perplexity + Hugging Face semantic dedup
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs Perplexity research, embeds findings with a Hugging Face encoder, deduplicates near-identical claims, and writes a clean research file.

templates.title: Perplexity competitor-watch monitor
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that asks Perplexity for any new launches, pricing changes, or announcements from a list of competitors, summarizes what changed since last run, and posts a cited digest to a Slack channel for the product team.

skills.name: answer-with-citations
skills.description: Ask Perplexity a question and get an answer grounded in current web sources with citations.
skills.content:
# Answer With Citations

Get a current, sourced answer to a question.

## Steps
1. Use the Chat operation and write the question as the User Prompt. Add a System Prompt to set tone and require inline citations.
2. Pick a model: sonar for quick answers, sonar-pro for harder questions, or sonar-deep-research for thorough multi-source work.
3. Keep temperature low (around 0.2) for factual tasks and set Max Tokens to cap length.

## Output
The answer with its supporting sources, and a note flagging anything the model could not confirm.

skills.name: search-recent-news
skills.description: Use Perplexity search with a recency filter to find the latest results on a topic.
skills.content:
# Search Recent News

Find the freshest sources on a topic.

## Steps
1. Use the Search operation and enter the topic as the Search Query.
2. Set a Recency Filter (hour, day, week, month, or year) or pin an After Date and Before Date window.
3. Optionally constrain a Domain Filter to trusted outlets and set a Country code for regional results.
4. Adjust Max Results for breadth.

## Output
A dated list of results, each with title, URL, and a one-line summary, ordered by relevance and recency.

skills.name: domain-restricted-research
skills.description: Run a Perplexity search restricted to specific authoritative domains and summarize findings.
skills.content:
# Domain-Restricted Research

Research a topic using only trusted sources.

## Steps
1. Use the Search operation with a precise Search Query.
2. Set the Domain Filter to the allowed domains (comma-separated, up to twenty) such as official, academic, or .gov sites.
3. Tune Max Page Tokens to control how much text is pulled per source.
4. Synthesize the returned results into a short summary.

## Output
A concise summary drawn only from the allowed domains, with each finding attributed to its source URL.

templates.title: Manual review case triage agent

templates.title: Re-verification campaign for stale accounts
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists Persona accounts, finds ones whose latest approved inquiry is older than a year, creates a new inquiry for each from our re-verification template, and emails customers a one-time verification link.

skills.name: verify-customer-identity
skills.description: Create a Persona inquiry for a customer and send them a one-time verification link.
skills.content:
# Verify Customer Identity

Start an identity verification for a customer using Persona.

## Steps
1. Use the Create Inquiry operation with your inquiry template ID. Pass the customer reference ID so the inquiry links to an account in your user model, and pre-fill known fields (e.g. {"name-first": "Jane", "name-last": "Doe"}).
2. Use the Generate Inquiry Link operation with the new inquiry ID to mint a one-time verification link. Set a custom expiry only if the default (24 hours) does not fit.
3. Deliver the one-time link to the customer (email, SMS, or chat).

## Output
Return the inquiry ID, its status, and the one-time link. Note when the link expires so follow-ups can be scheduled.

skills.name: check-verification-status
skills.description: Look up a Persona inquiry and report whether the individual passed, failed, or needs review.
skills.content:
# Check Verification Status

Read the current state of an identity verification from Persona.

## Steps
1. Use the Get Inquiry operation with the inquiry ID (or List Inquiries filtered by reference ID to find it).
2. Read the status: approved or completed means verified; needs_review means a human should look; failed, expired, or declined means not verified.
3. For deeper detail, use Get Verification with a verification ID to inspect the individual checks that ran.

## Output
Return the status, decision timestamps, and collected fields. Recommend the next action (proceed, route to review, or re-verify).

skills.name: screen-against-watchlists
skills.description: Run a Persona watchlist, adverse media, or PEP report on a person and surface matches.
skills.content:
# Screen Against Watchlists

Screen an individual for sanctions, adverse media, or political exposure using Persona reports.

## Steps
1. Use the Create Report operation with the report type (watchlist, adverse-media, or politically-exposed-person) and your report template ID. Provide the name parts or a full-name term, plus birthdate and country code when known to reduce false positives.
2. Reports run asynchronously: poll Get Report with the report ID until the status is ready.
3. Check hasMatch and the report attributes for matched lists and match details.

## Output
Return whether the screening found matches, the matched lists, and the report ID for the audit trail.

skills.name: triage-pending-reviews
skills.description: List Persona inquiries awaiting manual review and approve or decline them after assessment.
skills.content:
# Triage Pending Reviews

Work through identity verifications that need a manual decision in Persona.

## Steps
1. Use the List Inquiries operation with status needs_review (optionally bounded by created-after/created-before).
2. For each inquiry, use Get Inquiry for collected fields and List Cases / Get Case to see any linked review case.
3. After assessment, use Approve Inquiry or Decline Inquiry. Both are final: they prevent further progress and trigger associated workflows and webhooks.

## Output
Return a summary of inquiries reviewed and the decision taken for each, with inquiry IDs for the audit trail.

skills.name: import-accounts-from-csv
skills.description: Bulk-import existing users into Persona as accounts from a CSV file.
skills.content:
# Import Accounts from CSV

Migrate an existing user base into Persona using the account importer.

## Steps
1. Prepare a CSV of users (one row per account, with reference IDs and account fields).
2. Use the Import Accounts (CSV) operation with the file.
3. The importer runs asynchronously and returns pending at first; report the importer ID and counts once available.

## Output
Return the importer ID, status, and the successful, errored, and duplicate row counts.

skills.name: archive-verification-pdf
skills.description: Download the PDF summary of a Persona inquiry for compliance record-keeping.
skills.content:
# Archive Verification PDF

Keep a permanent record of an identity verification decision.

## Steps
1. Use the Print Inquiry PDF operation with the inquiry ID.
2. The PDF lands in execution files; pass it to a storage integration (Google Drive, S3, SharePoint) named by customer reference ID and date.

## Output
Return the stored file and where it was archived.

templates.title: Pinecone duplicate detector

templates.title: Pinecone support knowledge retriever

skills.name: upsert-text-records
skills.description: Embed and upsert text records into a Pinecone namespace using integrated embeddings.
skills.content:
# Upsert Text Records

Load documents into a Pinecone index for retrieval.

## Steps
1. Use the Upsert Text operation and provide the Index Host and target Namespace.
2. Pass newline-delimited JSON Records, each with a unique _id, a text or chunk_text field, and any metadata fields such as category for later filtering.
3. Keep chunks reasonably sized so each record carries one coherent idea.
4. Confirm the upsert status from the response.

## Output
Report how many records were upserted into which namespace and surface any records that failed validation.

skills.name: semantic-search
skills.description: Run a text query against a Pinecone index with metadata filtering and optional reranking.
skills.content:
# Semantic Search

Retrieve the most relevant records for a query.

## Steps
1. Use the Search With Text operation with the Index Host, Namespace, and a natural-language Search Query.
2. Set Top K for how many matches to return and list the Fields to Return.
3. Optionally apply a metadata Filter (operators like $eq, $in, $gte) to scope the search, and pass Rerank Options to reorder by a cross-encoder for higher precision.

## Output
The top matches with their scores, returned fields, and IDs, ordered by relevance after any reranking.

skills.name: generate-embeddings
skills.description: Generate vector embeddings for a set of texts with a Pinecone-hosted embedding model.
skills.content:
# Generate Embeddings

Turn text into vectors for storage or comparison.

## Steps
1. Use the Generate Embeddings operation and choose a model such as multilingual-e5-large or llama-text-embed-v2.
2. Provide the Text Inputs as a JSON array of objects each with a text field.
3. Use the returned vectors for downstream upserts or similarity work.

## Output
The embedding vector per input, the model used, and the usage statistics for cost tracking.

skills.name: fetch-vectors-by-id
skills.description: Fetch specific vectors and their metadata from a Pinecone namespace by ID.
skills.content:
# Fetch Vectors By ID

Look up known records directly.

## Steps
1. Use the Fetch Vectors operation with the Index Host and Namespace.
2. Provide the Vector IDs as a JSON array of the records to retrieve.
3. Inspect the returned values and metadata to confirm content or debug retrieval.

## Output
The requested records with their stored metadata, and a note listing any IDs that were not found.

skills.name: create-deal
skills.description: Create a Pipedrive deal with a title, value, pipeline stage, and linked person or organization.
skills.content:
# Create Deal

Add a new opportunity to the sales pipeline.

## Steps
1. Use the Create Deal operation with a clear Title.
2. Set Value and Currency, the target Pipeline and Stage ID, and Status (open, won, or lost).
3. Link the deal to a Person ID or Organization ID, and set an Expected Close Date.
4. Capture the returned deal ID for follow-up activities.

## Output
Confirm the new deal title, value, pipeline stage, and ID so it can be referenced in later steps.

skills.name: review-pipeline
skills.description: List Pipedrive deals in a pipeline and summarize stage distribution and deals at risk.
skills.content:
# Review Pipeline

Get a snapshot of the current sales pipeline.

## Steps
1. Use Get All Deals (or Get Pipeline Deals for one pipeline) filtered to open status.
2. Optionally scope by Pipeline, Person ID, or Organization ID and set Updated Since to focus on recent movement.
3. Group deals by stage and total their value, flagging stale deals with no recent update.
4. Page with the cursor or start offset for large pipelines.

## Output
A stage-by-stage breakdown with deal counts and total value, plus a short list of at-risk deals that have gone quiet.

skills.name: log-activity
skills.description: Create a Pipedrive activity such as a call, meeting, or task linked to a deal or contact.
skills.content:
# Log Activity

Schedule or record follow-up work against a record.

## Steps
1. Use the Create Activity operation with a Subject and an activity Type (call, meeting, task, deadline, email, or lunch).
2. Set the Due Date and optional Due Time, Duration, and Notes.
3. Link the activity to the relevant Deal ID, Person ID, or Organization ID.
4. Use Update Activity later to mark it done.

## Output
Confirm the activity subject, type, due date, and the record it is linked to.

skills.name: manage-leads
skills.description: Create or update Pipedrive leads with value, contacts, and expected close date.
skills.content:
# Manage Leads

Capture and maintain top-of-funnel leads.

## Steps
1. Use Create Lead with a Title and link a Person ID or Organization ID and an Owner ID.
2. Set the Value Amount and Value Currency and an Expected Close Date.
3. Use Update Lead to revise details or archive a lead once it converts or goes cold.
4. Use Get Leads to review active or archived leads.

## Output
The lead title, linked contact, value, and current state (active or archived) with its ID.

skills.name: find-market-odds
skills.description: Look up a Polymarket market and report the current implied odds and price for each outcome.
skills.content:
# Find Market Odds

Get the live implied probability for a question.

## Steps
1. Use Search or Get Markets to locate the market, or Get Market with a known market ID or slug.
2. Read the outcome token IDs from the market, then use Get Price or Get Midpoint per token to get the current price.
3. Treat the price (0 to 1) as the implied probability of that outcome.

## Output
For the market, list each outcome with its current price as a percentage probability, plus the market volume and whether it is still open.

skills.name: list-top-markets
skills.description: List the highest-volume or most-liquid Polymarket markets, optionally filtered by category tag.
skills.content:
# List Top Markets

Surface the markets attracting the most attention.

## Steps
1. Use Get Markets (or Get Events) sorted by Volume or Liquidity in descending order.
2. Optionally filter by a Tag ID for a category and set Closed Status to open only.
3. Set a Limit and use the offset to page through results.

## Output
A ranked list of markets with title, volume, liquidity, and current implied odds for the leading outcome.

skills.name: track-price-history
skills.description: Pull Polymarket price history for an outcome token over an interval and summarize the trend.
skills.content:
# Track Price History

See how an outcome moved over time.

## Steps
1. Identify the outcome token ID from the market.
2. Use Get Price History with that Token ID and either a preset Interval (1h, 6h, 1d, 1w, max) or a Start and End timestamp with a Fidelity in minutes.
3. Compare the latest price against the start of the window to compute the move.

## Output
The price at the start and end of the window, the net change, and a one-line read on the trend (rising, falling, or flat).

skills.name: analyze-wallet-positions
skills.description: Fetch a Polymarket wallet's open positions and summarize value and profit and loss.
skills.content:
# Analyze Wallet Positions

Review what a trader holds and how it is performing.

## Steps
1. Use Get Positions with the User Wallet Address, optionally sorted by Cash P&L or Current Value.
2. Filter with a Size Threshold or by redeemable status to focus on meaningful holdings.
3. Optionally use Get Activity for the same wallet to see recent trades and redemptions.

## Output
A summary of the wallet positions: total current value, aggregate profit and loss, and the largest winners and losers by market.

skills.name: capture-event
skills.description: Send a product analytics event to PostHog for a user with custom properties.
skills.content:
# Capture Event

Record a user action in PostHog.

## Steps
1. Use the Capture Event operation with the Project API Key and Project ID.
2. Set the Event Name (for example purchase_completed) and the Distinct ID identifying the user.
3. Add Properties as a JSON object with relevant context such as plan, price, or page, and optionally a Timestamp.
4. For many events at once, use Batch Events with a JSON array instead.

## Output
Confirm the event name and user it was captured for, and report success or any validation error returned.

skills.name: query-product-data
skills.description: Run a HogQL query against PostHog to answer a product analytics question.
skills.content:
# Query Product Data

Pull custom analytics with HogQL.

## Steps
1. Use the Run Query operation with your Personal API Key, Project ID, and Region.
2. Write the HogQL Query (SQL-like) to compute the metric, for example daily active users or top events over a window.
3. Pass Query Values for any parameters.
4. Aggregate or format the returned rows for the answer.

## Output
The query result rows summarized into a direct answer, noting the time window and any assumptions in the query.

skills.name: manage-feature-flag
skills.description: Create, update, or toggle a PostHog feature flag and control its rollout.
skills.content:
# Manage Feature Flag

Control a feature rollout in PostHog.

## Steps
1. Use Create Feature Flag with a Flag Key, Name, and a Rollout Percentage, or Update Feature Flag by Feature Flag ID to change state.
2. Set Active on or off and supply Filters as JSON to target specific cohorts or person properties.
3. Provide the Personal API Key, Project ID, and Region.
4. Use List Feature Flags to confirm the current state.

## Output
Report the flag key, whether it is active, and the rollout percentage or targeting now in effect.

skills.name: analyze-survey-responses
skills.description: List PostHog surveys and pull responses to summarize themes and satisfaction.
skills.content:
# Analyze Survey Responses

Turn survey feedback into insight.

## Steps
1. Use List Surveys to find the active survey, then Get Survey for its definition.
2. Use Run Query (HogQL) to pull the survey response events for that survey over a date window.
3. Group open-text answers by theme and compute the rating or NPS distribution.

## Output
A short summary of the top themes from open responses plus the rating or NPS breakdown and any notable movement.

skills.name: add-release-annotation
skills.description: Create a PostHog annotation marking a deploy or release on the analytics timeline.
skills.content:
# Add Release Annotation

Mark an event on the PostHog timeline for context.

## Steps
1. Use the Create Annotation operation with the Personal API Key, Project ID, and Region.
2. Provide the Content describing what happened (for example a deploy or campaign launch) and a Date Marker timestamp.
3. Set the Scope to project or dashboard item.

## Output
Confirm the annotation content and the date it was placed on so charts show the marker.

skills.name: check-brand-visibility
skills.description: Pull a Profound visibility report to see how a brand surfaces in AI answers for tracked prompts.
skills.content:
# Check Brand Visibility

Measure how often a brand appears in AI engine answers.

## Steps
1. Use the Visibility Report operation with the Category ID and a Start Date and End Date.
2. Set Metrics such as share_of_voice, visibility_score, and mentions_count.
3. Optionally break the data out by Dimensions (date, model) and set a Date Interval.
4. Compare the latest period against the prior one.

## Output
The visibility and share-of-voice scores for the period, broken down by model where requested, with the change versus the previous window.

skills.name: track-citation-sources
skills.description: Pull a Profound citations report to see which sources AI engines cite for brand prompts.
skills.content:
# Track Citation Sources

Find the sources AI engines cite when answering about a brand.

## Steps
1. Use the Citations Report operation with the Category ID, Start Date, and End Date, and set Metrics such as count and citation_share.
2. For a specific domain, use Citation Prompts with the Domain to see which prompts cite it.
3. Optionally add Dimensions to group by source domain or page.

## Output
A ranked list of citing domains and pages with their citation share, highlighting any new sources the content team should target.

skills.name: compare-competitor-share
skills.description: Use Profound visibility metrics to compare a brand against competitors in AI answers.
skills.content:
# Compare Competitor Share

Benchmark share-of-voice across competitors.

## Steps
1. Use the Visibility Report operation for the Category ID over a date window with the share_of_voice metric.
2. Add Dimensions to break results out by asset or brand name, and apply Filters as JSON to scope to the competitor set.
3. Rank the brands by share-of-voice.

## Output
A leaderboard of brands by share-of-voice in AI answers, flagging any competitor that gained or lost notable ground.

skills.name: find-content-gaps
skills.description: Use Profound prompt and answer data to find prompts where the brand is absent from AI answers.
skills.content:
# Find Content Gaps

Surface prompts where the brand is missing from AI answers.

## Steps
1. Use Category Prompts with the Category ID to list tracked prompts, paging with the cursor.
2. Use Prompt Answers over a date window to see how the brand appears (or does not) for each prompt.
3. Flag prompts with low or zero visibility as content gaps.

## Output
A prioritized list of prompts where the brand is absent or weak in AI answers, ready to drive content briefs.

templates.title: Prospeo email finder
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes a prospect name and company from a table, runs Prospeo to find and verify their work email, and writes the deliverable contact back to the row.

templates.title: Prospeo person enricher
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches CRM contacts, runs Prospeo enrichment to fill in title, company, and verified contact details, and writes the enriched fields back.

templates.title: Prospeo ICP search
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs a Prospeo people search against my ICP filters, reveals verified emails and mobile numbers, and writes the prospect list into a sender table.

templates.title: Prospeo + Email Bison outbound
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that uses Prospeo to find and verify prospect emails, drafts a personalized first-touch message, and pushes valid prospects into an Email Bison campaign.

templates.title: Prospeo CRM gap-filler
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that finds Salesforce contacts missing email addresses, runs Prospeo to find and verify them, and updates each contact record.

templates.title: Prospeo bulk list enrichment
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads a large prospect list from a table, runs Prospeo bulk person enrichment in batches to reveal verified emails and titles, and writes the enriched results back row by row with a status column for any that could not be matched.

templates.title: Prospeo company enrichment
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that takes a list of target company domains, runs Prospeo company enrichment to pull firmographics like size, industry, and location, and writes the structured company profiles into an account table for territory planning.

skills.name: find-work-email
skills.description: Find and verify a prospect's work email and optional mobile number with Prospeo.
skills.content:
# Find Work Email

Get a deliverable work email for a prospect.

## Steps
1. Use the Enrich Person operation and provide the strongest match key: a LinkedIn URL, or First and Last Name plus Company Name or Company Website.
2. Set Only Verified Email to Yes when deliverability matters, and Enrich Mobile to also reveal a phone number.
3. Read the enriched person object for the email, its verification status, and the mobile if requested.

## Output
The verified work email (and mobile if requested) with its status, or a clear note that no match was found and which keys were tried.

skills.name: search-prospects
skills.description: Search Prospeo for people matching an ICP using seniority, title, industry, and company filters.
skills.content:
# Search Prospects

Build a targeted prospect list from the B2B database.

## Steps
1. Use the Search Person operation and supply a Filters JSON object using documented keys such as person_seniority, person_job_title, company_industry, and company_headcount_range with include or exclude lists.
2. Avoid using only exclude filters; always include at least one positive filter.
3. Page through results with the Page field.

## Output
The matching prospects with names, titles, and companies, plus the pagination details so the list can be fully retrieved.

skills.name: enrich-company
skills.description: Enrich a company from its website or LinkedIn URL to get Prospeo firmographics.
skills.content:
# Enrich Company

Pull firmographics for a target account.

## Steps
1. Use the Enrich Company operation and provide the Company Website or Company LinkedIn URL (most reliable), or a Company Name.
2. Read the returned company object for size, industry, location, and other firmographic fields.
3. For many accounts, use Bulk Enrich Company with a JSON array of records, each with an identifier and a match key.

## Output
The company firmographics (size, industry, location) for the account, or the matched and not-matched breakdown when running in bulk.

skills.name: bulk-enrich-list
skills.description: Enrich a list of people or companies in batches with Prospeo bulk enrichment.
skills.content:
# Bulk Enrich List

Enrich up to fifty records per call efficiently.

## Steps
1. Use Bulk Enrich Person (or Bulk Enrich Company) and pass a JSON array of records, each with a unique identifier and one valid match key set.
2. Set Only Verified Email or Enrich Mobile as needed for the person variant.
3. Map results back to inputs using the identifier, and check the not-matched and invalid-datapoints lists.

## Output
A per-identifier summary of matched records with their enriched fields, the total credit cost, and the identifiers that did not match for retry.

templates.title: ElevenLabs + Pulse meeting voice digest
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes Pulse meeting insights, narrates them with an ElevenLabs voice, and emails the audio digest to the team for asynchronous review.

templates.title: Pulse invoice extractor
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that runs each uploaded invoice PDF through Pulse OCR, extracts vendor, line items, and totals into structured fields, and writes the parsed records to an accounts-payable table.

templates.title: Pulse contract clause extractor

templates.title: Pulse scanned-document indexer

templates.title: Pulse form data extractor
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that extracts text from uploaded form PDFs and images with Pulse OCR, maps the values into structured fields with an agent, and writes each submission to a table.

templates.title: Pulse table-to-spreadsheet extractor
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that runs uploaded reports through Pulse OCR, pulls the embedded tables into structured rows, and writes the consolidated data to a tracking table.

templates.title: Pulse document summarizer
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that extracts the text of an uploaded PDF or Office file with Pulse OCR, has an agent write a concise summary, and posts it to Slack.

templates.title: Pulse document OCR pipeline
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs each uploaded PDF, image, or Office file through Pulse OCR, extracts the text into structured rows in a table, and indexes the cleaned content into a knowledge base so agents can search across every scanned document.

skills.name: extract-document-text
skills.description: Run a PDF, image, or Office file through Pulse OCR and return clean markdown.
skills.content:
# Extract Document Text

Turn a document into structured markdown text.

## Steps
1. Upload the Document (PDF, image, DOCX, PPTX, or XLSX) or provide a file reference.
2. Optionally set Specific Pages (for example 1-3,5) to limit extraction to part of the document.
3. Provide the Pulse API Key.
4. Use the returned markdown as the source for downstream summarization or parsing.

## Output
The extracted markdown text and the page count, plus any bounding-box or figure data when available.

skills.name: extract-structured-fields
skills.description: Use Pulse OCR output to pull structured fields like vendor, totals, or dates from a document.
skills.content:
# Extract Structured Fields

Pull specific data points out of a scanned document.

## Steps
1. Run the document through Pulse OCR to get the markdown text.
2. In a following agent step, map the markdown to the target fields (for example invoice vendor, line items, totals, or contract parties and renewal dates).
3. Validate the parsed values against the source text before using them.

## Output
A structured record of the requested fields, with a note on any field that could not be confidently extracted from the document.

skills.name: chunk-for-knowledge-base
skills.description: Extract and chunk a document with Pulse OCR so it can be indexed for retrieval.
skills.content:
# Chunk For Knowledge Base

Prepare a document for vector indexing.

## Steps
1. Upload the Document and provide the Pulse API Key.
2. Set a Chunking Strategy (semantic, header, page, or recursive) and a Chunk Size in characters.
3. Use the returned chunks as the units to embed and index into a knowledge base.

## Output
The chunked content ready for embedding, with each chunk sized per the strategy, plus the total page count for reference.

templates.title: Qdrant document ingestion
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that watches a Google Drive folder for new docs, chunks each, generates embeddings, and upserts the vectors into a Qdrant collection with rich metadata.

templates.title: Qdrant retrieval agent
templates.prompt: Create an agent that performs hybrid search against a Qdrant collection — semantic + filter conditions — and answers user questions with the matched documents cited.

templates.title: Qdrant payload schema migrator
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that scans a Qdrant collection, migrates payload schema to a new version with backfilled fields, and writes the migration plan and outcome to an audit table.

templates.title: Qdrant + knowledge base sync
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that mirrors a Sim knowledge base into a Qdrant collection so downstream applications outside Sim can perform retrieval against the same vectors.

templates.title: Qdrant snapshot manager
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that takes a Qdrant collection snapshot each night, uploads it to S3 with retention rotation, and writes the snapshot manifest to a tracking table.

templates.title: Qdrant abandoned-document detector
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that scans a Qdrant collection for vectors whose source document no longer exists, deletes the orphans, and writes a hygiene report each week.

templates.title: Qdrant support-answer retriever
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that embeds each new Zendesk ticket with OpenAI, runs a filtered Qdrant search scoped to the customer’s product, and drafts a cited reply from the closest matching resolved tickets for the agent to approve.

skills.name: upsert-points
skills.description: Insert or update vector points with payload metadata into a Qdrant collection.
skills.content:
# Upsert Points

Load vectors into a Qdrant collection.

## Steps
1. Use the Upsert operation with the Qdrant URL, Collection name, and API Key.
2. Provide Points as a JSON array, each with an id, a vector matching the collection dimension, and an optional payload of metadata for later filtering.
3. Confirm the upserted count from the response.

## Output
Report how many points were upserted into which collection and surface any payload validation issues.

skills.name: search-vectors
skills.description: Run a vector similarity search in Qdrant with optional payload filters.
skills.content:
# Search Vectors

Find the nearest points to a query vector.

## Steps
1. Use the Search operation with the Qdrant URL, Collection, and the Query Vector.
2. Set the Limit for how many matches to return and choose what Return Data you need (payload only, vector only, both, or none).
3. Optionally pass a Filter JSON object using must, should, or must_not conditions to scope the search by payload fields.

## Output
The top matches with their scores and requested payload or vector data, ordered by similarity.

skills.name: fetch-points-by-id
skills.description: Retrieve specific Qdrant points and their payloads by ID.
skills.content:
# Fetch Points By ID

Look up known points directly.

## Steps
1. Use the Fetch operation with the Qdrant URL, Collection, and API Key.
2. Provide the IDs as a JSON array of the points to retrieve.
3. Choose the Return Data option to control whether payloads and vectors are included.

## Output
The requested points with their payloads (and vectors if requested), plus a note on any IDs that were not found.

templates.title: Quartr earnings call digest
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that lists yesterday’s Quartr events for my watchlist tickers, fetches the AI-generated summary for each event, and posts a digest with source links to Slack.

templates.title: Quartr transcript knowledge base
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists new Quartr earnings call transcripts for companies I follow, downloads each transcript file, and indexes the content into a knowledge base so agents can answer questions about past calls.

templates.title: Quartr filing watcher
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that checks Quartr daily for new annual and interim reports from my portfolio companies, downloads each report PDF to Files, and emails me a summary of what was filed.

templates.title: Quartr slide deck analyst

templates.title: Quartr live earnings monitor
