templates.title: Quartr competitor earnings tracker
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads competitor tickers from a table, lists each company’s recent Quartr events and event summaries, and logs revenue and guidance highlights back to the table for quarter-over-quarter comparison.

templates.title: Quartr earnings Q&A agent
templates.prompt: Create an agent that answers questions about a company’s earnings by looking up the company on Quartr, finding its latest earnings call event, and grounding answers in the event summary and transcript.

skills.name: summarize-earnings-call
skills.description: Find a company’s latest earnings call on Quartr and return its AI-generated summary with sources.
skills.content:
# Summarize an Earnings Call

Turn a ticker into a sourced summary of the company’s most recent earnings call.

## Steps
1. Use the List Companies operation with the ticker in Tickers to resolve the Quartr company ID.
2. Use List Events with that ID in Company IDs, Sort By set to Date, and Sort Direction set to Descending to find the latest earnings event.
3. Use Get Event Summary with the event ID. Pick Summary Length: One Line for a headline, Short for a digest, or Long for full detail.
4. Keep Plain Text Summary off if you want the embedded source tags, and use the sources output to cite documents.

## Output
Return the summary text followed by the event title, date, and the source document IDs it references.

skills.name: download-earnings-transcript
skills.description: Download the structured transcript JSON for a company’s earnings call for downstream analysis.
skills.content:
# Download an Earnings Call Transcript

Fetch a transcript with timestamps and speaker identification as a workflow file.

## Steps
1. Resolve the company with List Companies (ticker, ISIN, or CIK).
2. Use List Transcripts with the company ID in Company IDs and a date range to find the right transcript document.
3. Use Get Transcript with that document ID. The transcript JSON is downloaded and stored as an execution file.
4. Pass the file to an agent or knowledge base to analyze paragraphs, sentences, timestamps, and speakers.

## Output
Return the transcript file plus the document metadata (event title, fiscal period, and date).

skills.name: fetch-latest-filings
skills.description: List a company’s recent filings and reports on Quartr and download the report PDFs.
skills.content:
# Fetch the Latest Filings and Reports

Pull recent 10-Ks, 10-Qs, earnings releases, or annual reports for a company.

## Steps
1. Resolve the company with List Companies using its ticker or CIK.
2. Use List Reports with the company ID in Company IDs. Narrow with Document Group IDs (1 = Earnings Release, 3 = Interim Report, 4 = Annual Report) or a date range.
3. Use Get Report with each document ID to download the PDF into execution files.
4. Optionally use List Document Types to map type IDs to filing forms like 10-Q.

## Output
Return the report files with each document’s type, event, and filing date.

skills.name: monitor-live-earnings
skills.description: Check which companies are live on Quartr right now and surface their audio and transcript streams.
skills.content:
# Monitor Live Earnings Calls

Watch for companies going live and grab their stream URLs.

## Steps
1. Use List Live Events with Live States set to live (or willBeLive to see what is coming up).
2. Filter to your watchlist with Company IDs or Tickers.
3. Read each live event’s state, audio stream URL, and transcript stream URL from the output.
4. Run the workflow on a schedule and alert when a watched company’s state changes to live.

## Output
Return the live companies with their event IDs, states, and audio/transcript stream URLs.

skills.name: analyze-investor-slides
skills.description: Download a company’s latest investor presentation from Quartr and extract key takeaways.
skills.content:
# Analyze an Investor Slide Deck

Get the latest presentation PDF and have an agent extract what matters.

## Steps
1. Resolve the company with List Companies and find the relevant event with List Events.
2. Use List Slide Decks with the event ID in Event IDs (or the company ID and a date range) to find the deck.
3. Use Get Slide Deck with the document ID to download the PDF into execution files.
4. Pass the file to an agent to extract guidance, KPIs, and notable changes.

## Output
Return the slide deck file plus the extracted highlights.

templates.title: Quiver SVG icon generator
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes a product name and brand color as inputs, generates a matching SVG icon with Quiver, and saves it to the files store.

templates.title: Quiver diagram creator
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that reads structured data from a table and uses Quiver to generate a clean SVG diagram visualizing the data, then attaches it to a Slack message.

templates.title: Quiver image vectorizer
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that accepts a raster image upload, vectorizes it to SVG with Quiver, and returns the clean SVG for use in presentations or exports.

skills.name: generate-brand-icon
skills.description: Generate a clean SVG icon from a text prompt and save it to the files store.
skills.content:
# Generate Brand Icon

Turn a text description into a production-ready SVG icon using Quiver text-to-SVG.

## Steps
1. Collect the icon concept (for example, a product name plus a brand color and style cues).
2. Run the text_to_svg operation with a focused prompt that names the subject, color palette, and visual style (flat, line, filled).
3. Optionally set n greater than 1 to generate several variations to choose from.
4. Save the returned SVG file to the files store, or pass svgContent downstream for embedding.

## Output
Report the saved file location and the request id. When multiple variations are generated, list each so the user can pick one.

skills.name: vectorize-raster-image
skills.description: Convert an uploaded raster image (PNG or JPG) into a clean editable SVG.
skills.content:
# Vectorize Raster Image

Convert a bitmap logo or graphic into a scalable SVG with Quiver image-to-SVG.

## Steps
1. Accept the raster image upload and pass it as the image input.
2. Run the image_to_svg operation, optionally setting auto_crop and a target_size to tighten the output.
3. Inspect svgContent for fidelity; rerun with adjusted instructions if details are lost.
4. Save the SVG file for use in presentations, exports, or the web.

## Output
Return the vectorized SVG file and confirm dimensions. Note any visual elements that did not vectorize cleanly.

skills.name: create-data-diagram
skills.description: Generate an SVG diagram that visualizes structured data, then share it.
skills.content:
# Create Data Diagram

Produce a clean SVG diagram from structured data and attach it to a message.

## Steps
1. Read the structured data (for example, rows from a table) that should be visualized.
2. Summarize the data into a precise prompt describing the diagram type and relationships.
3. Run the text_to_svg operation to generate the diagram.
4. Save the SVG file and attach it to the target channel or document.

## Output
Share the generated diagram file and a one-line description of what it depicts.

templates.title: Railway deployment monitor
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists the latest Railway deployments across my services every few minutes, detects failed or crashed deployments, summarizes the failure with an agent, and posts an actionable Slack alert with a link to the service.

templates.title: Railway deploy on merge
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches GitHub for merges to the main branch, triggers a Railway service deployment for the matching environment, and posts the deployment status back as a Slack notification.

templates.title: Railway environment variable auditor
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled weekly workflow that lists environment variables across every Railway project, compares them to a reference list in a table, flags drift and missing keys, and emails a remediation report to the platform team.

templates.title: Railway project inventory
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that lists every Railway project, its services, and environments weekly, logs them into a tracking table, and Slacks a diff of any added or removed resources so infrastructure changes never go unnoticed.

templates.title: Railway config sync
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads service configuration from a table and upserts the matching Railway environment variables for each service, then posts a Slack summary of every variable that was created or changed.

templates.title: Railway preview environment provisioner
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches GitHub for new pull requests, creates a fresh Railway environment for the branch, upserts the required environment variables, deploys the service, and comments the live preview URL back on the PR.

templates.title: Railway project onboarding kit
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes a new service name, creates a Railway project, sets up staging and production environments, seeds baseline environment variables from a table, and posts the project members and access summary to Slack for the team.

skills.name: monitor-failed-deployments
skills.description: List recent Railway deployments, detect failures, and alert with a summary.
skills.content:
# Monitor Failed Deployments

Watch Railway deployments and surface failures fast.

## Steps
1. Run list_deployments for the target project, service, and environment.
2. Identify deployments with a failed or crashed status from the returned list.
3. For each failure, run get_deployment_logs to pull the runtime logs and determine the likely cause.
4. Summarize each failure: service, environment, status, and the diagnosed cause.
5. Post an actionable alert (for example to Slack) with a link to the affected service.

## Output
Return the count of failed deployments and a concise summary of each. If all healthy, report a clean status.

skills.name: deploy-service
skills.description: Trigger a Railway service deployment for a given environment and commit.
skills.content:
# Deploy Service

Trigger a deployment of a Railway service.

## Steps
1. Identify the service id and environment id to deploy (use get_project to look them up if needed).
2. Run deploy_service, optionally pinning a specific commitSha.
3. Capture the returned deploymentId.
4. Optionally poll list_deployments to confirm the deployment reaches a success state.

## Output
Report the deploymentId, target environment, and final status.

skills.name: sync-environment-variables
skills.description: Upsert Railway environment variables from a reference source and report changes.
skills.content:
# Sync Environment Variables

Keep Railway environment variables aligned with a reference list.

## Steps
1. Read the desired variable set (for example from a table) for each service.
2. Run list_variables to capture the current state for the project, environment, and service.
3. For each variable that is missing or differs, run upsert_variable. Use skipDeploys when batching multiple changes.
4. Trigger a single deploy at the end if needed.

## Output
Return a summary of every variable created or changed, grouped by service.

skills.name: provision-preview-environment
skills.description: Create an ephemeral Railway environment, seed variables, and deploy it.
skills.content:
# Provision Preview Environment

Spin up a fresh Railway environment for a branch or pull request.

## Steps
1. Run create_environment for the project, optionally cloning from a source environment and marking it ephemeral.
2. Upsert the required environment variables for the new environment.
3. Run deploy_service to bring the preview online.
4. Capture the deployment status and the preview URL.

## Output
Return the new environment id and the live preview URL so it can be shared on the PR.

skills.name: audit-project-inventory
skills.description: List every Railway project with services and environments for tracking.
skills.content:
# Audit Project Inventory

Build a current inventory of Railway resources.

## Steps
1. Run list_projects, paginating with first and after until complete.
2. For each project, run get_project to capture its services and environments.
3. Optionally run list_project_members to record access.
4. Compare against a prior snapshot to detect added or removed resources.

## Output
Return the full inventory and a diff of any changes since the last run.

skills.name: rollback-failed-deployment
skills.description: Detect a bad Railway deployment and roll back or restart to recover.
skills.content:
# Roll Back Failed Deployment

Recover a Railway service automatically when a deployment goes bad.

## Steps
1. Run list_deployments for the service and environment to find the most recent deployment and its status.
2. If the latest deployment failed or crashed, optionally run get_deployment_logs to confirm and capture the cause.
3. To revert: pick the most recent healthy deployment with canRollback true (from list_deployments) and run rollback_deployment with its id.
4. To recover a locked-up but otherwise healthy deployment instead, run restart_deployment with the deployment id.
5. Run get_deployment on the resulting deployment to confirm it reaches a healthy status.

## Output
Report whether a rollback or restart was performed, the target deployment id, and the final status.

templates.title: Hashed email enrichment pipeline

templates.title: LinkedIn to mobile phone finder

templates.title: Intent-to-CRM identity sync

templates.title: High-intent visitor Slack alerts
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that reads a list of website visitor IPs, uses RB2B to resolve each person and their company, and posts an alert with the identified LinkedIn profile and company to the sales Slack channel.

templates.title: LinkedIn slug resolver
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes a first name, last name, and company domain, uses RB2B LinkedIn slug search to resolve the matching profile, and enriches it into a business profile written to a prospect table.

templates.title: Account engagement freshness sweep
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that runs my list of prospect emails through RB2B email-to-last-active-date lookups, flags recently active contacts, and logs the engagement snapshot to a table for prioritized follow-up.

skills.name: identify-website-visitor
skills.description: Resolve a visitor IP into a person and company profile for sales follow-up.
skills.content:
# Identify Website Visitor

Turn an anonymous visit into a named, enrichable lead.

## Steps
1. Take the visitor ip_address and run ip_to_company to resolve the firmographic match.
2. Run ip_to_hem to obtain the hashed email identifier for the person.
3. Run hem_to_business_profile and hem_to_best_linkedin to build a full contact profile.
4. Score the lead by company fit and route high-intent matches to sales.

## Output
Return the resolved company, person name, title, and LinkedIn. Flag whether the match clears your fit threshold.

skills.name: enrich-linkedin-contact
skills.description: Enrich a LinkedIn profile with business email and phone for outreach.
skills.content:
# Enrich LinkedIn Contact

Turn a LinkedIn profile into reachable contact details.

## Steps
1. Provide the LinkedIn URL or slug; use linkedin_slug_search first if you only have a name.
2. Run linkedin_to_business_profile to capture role and company.
3. Run linkedin_to_best_personal_email and linkedin_to_mobile_phone for direct contact points.
4. Push the enriched record into the CRM or an outreach sequence.

## Output
Return the contact name, company, best email, and phone. Note any field that could not be resolved.

skills.name: check-credit-balance
skills.description: Check the RB2B credit balance before running a batch of enrichment lookups.
skills.content:
# Check Credit Balance

Verify enrichment credits remain before a batch run.

## Steps
1. Run credit_check to read the current balance.
2. Estimate the credits needed for the planned lookups.
3. If the balance is insufficient, alert the team rather than starting a partial run.

## Output
Return the remaining credit balance and whether the planned batch can proceed.

templates.title: Social mention tracker
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that monitors Reddit and X for mentions of my brand and competitors, scores each mention by sentiment and reach, logs them to a table, and sends a daily Slack digest of notable mentions.

templates.title: Reddit subreddit monitor
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that uses Reddit to watch target subreddits for posts matching brand or product keywords, scores each for relevance and sentiment, and posts notable hits to Slack with the original link.

templates.title: Reddit user-question knowledge mining
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that pulls top questions from Reddit industry subreddits weekly, classifies by theme, and writes a content-opportunity table the marketing team can prioritize.

templates.title: Reddit AMA preparer
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that aggregates top Reddit AMA-style questions for a topic, clusters them, drafts polished answers using a knowledge base, and posts a Q&A document for review.

templates.title: Reddit competitor watch
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that monitors Reddit threads mentioning competitors weekly, summarizes sentiment and pain points, and writes a competitive intelligence note to a tracking table.

templates.title: Reddit crisis-signal alerter
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls Reddit for sudden bursts of negative posts about the brand, classifies severity, and pages the PR team via Slack and PagerDuty when a real crisis emerges.

templates.title: Reddit content-idea collector
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls marketing-relevant Reddit subreddits, captures upvoted long-form posts, summarizes each, and adds them to a content-ideas table with effort and impact scores.

skills.name: monitor-subreddit-mentions
skills.description: Search a subreddit for brand or keyword mentions and summarize what people say.
skills.content:
# Monitor Subreddit Mentions

Track what people say about a topic on Reddit.

## Steps
1. Run search with the brand or keyword query, scoped to the relevant subreddit when appropriate.
2. For high-signal threads, run get_comments to pull the discussion.
3. Summarize sentiment, recurring themes, and notable complaints or praise.
4. Route urgent or negative threads to the right channel.

## Output
Return a digest of top mentions with links, sentiment, and key takeaways.

skills.name: surface-trending-posts
skills.description: Pull top and controversial posts from a subreddit for a content or research brief.
skills.content:
# Surface Trending Posts

Find what is rising and contentious in a community.

## Steps
1. Run get_posts for the subreddit using a hot or top sort to capture momentum.
2. Run get_controversial to surface divisive discussions.
3. Read get_comments on the standouts for context.
4. Cluster the posts into themes.

## Output
Return a ranked brief of trending and controversial posts with titles, links, and a one-line takeaway each.

skills.name: reply-to-mention
skills.description: Draft and post a helpful, on-brand reply to a Reddit post or comment.
skills.content:
# Reply To Mention

Respond to a relevant Reddit thread.

## Steps
1. Read the target post or comment with get_posts or get_comments for full context.
2. Draft a concise, non-promotional reply that adds genuine value.
3. Run reply to post it on the chosen thread.
4. Optionally save the thread for later follow-up.

## Output
Return the posted reply text and a link to the comment. Respect subreddit rules and avoid spammy self-promotion.

skills.name: submit-announcement-post
skills.description: Submit a new post to a target subreddit for an announcement or launch.
skills.content:
# Submit Announcement Post

Share an announcement on Reddit.

## Steps
1. Run get_subreddit_rules to confirm the target subreddit allows the post type and self-promotion.
2. Run submit_post with a clear title and body tailored to the community.
3. Capture the returned post id and link.
4. Monitor early get_comments and respond to questions.

## Output
Return the new post link and an initial engagement check.

skills.name: research-a-redditor
skills.description: Profile a Reddit user from their public posts, comments, and karma.
skills.content:
# Research A Redditor

Build a picture of a Reddit user for vetting or community research.

## Steps
1. Run get_user to pull profile, karma, and account age.
2. Run get_user_posts and get_user_comments to sample their recent activity.
3. Identify the subreddits, topics, and tone they engage with most.
4. Flag anything notable (expertise, affiliations, red flags).

## Output
Return a short profile: account summary, top communities, themes, and a sample of representative posts/comments with links.

skills.name: discover-communities
skills.description: Find the most relevant subreddits for a topic before posting or monitoring.
skills.content:
# Discover Communities

Locate the right subreddits for a topic or campaign.

## Steps
1. Run search_subreddits with the topic keywords to find candidate communities.
2. Run get_subreddit_info on the strongest matches to compare size and activity.
3. Run get_subreddit_rules to check posting and self-promotion rules.
4. Optionally run list_my_subreddits to see which you already follow.

## Output
Return a ranked shortlist of subreddits with subscriber counts, activity, fit, and key rules.

skills.name: manage-saved-research
skills.description: Curate a research reading list from saved Reddit posts and comments.
skills.content:
# Manage Saved Research

Turn saved Reddit items into an organized research list.

## Steps
1. Run get_saved to pull your saved posts and comments.
2. Run get_info to re-hydrate any specific fullnames you are tracking.
3. Summarize and cluster the items by theme.
4. Use save / unsave to keep the list current.

## Output
Return a themed reading list with titles, links, and one-line summaries.

skills.name: triage-mod-queue
skills.description: Moderate a subreddit: review reported content and act on it against the rules.
skills.content:
# Triage Mod Queue

Review and action content in a subreddit you moderate.

## Steps
1. Run get_posts / get_comments to pull the content under review.
2. Run get_subreddit_rules and evaluate each item against them.
3. Take action: mod_approve to keep, mod_remove (optionally as spam) to remove, lock to stop replies, mod_distinguish or mod_sticky to highlight official posts.
4. Log each decision and the rule it maps to.

## Output
Return a decision list: item link, action taken, and the rule or reason. Only act on subreddits you moderate.

templates.title: Redis response cache
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that checks Redis for a cached result by key before running an expensive step, and writes the computed result back with a TTL when there is a miss so repeat requests stay fast.

templates.title: Redis rate limiter
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that increments a per-user Redis counter on each request, sets an expiry on the first hit, and blocks the request when the counter passes the allowed threshold within the window.

templates.title: Redis feature-flag reader
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads feature-flag values from a Redis hash, branches downstream logic on whether each flag is enabled, and falls back to a default when a flag key is missing.

templates.title: Redis job queue worker
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that pops the next job off a Redis list, processes it with an agent, and writes the outcome to a table so a backlog of work is drained on an interval.

templates.title: Redis cache warmer
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that reads a list of hot keys from a table and sets each one in Redis with fresh values and a TTL, so popular lookups stay warm.

templates.title: Redis daily counter digest
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that reads the day’s Redis counters by key pattern, builds a summary of the totals with an agent, and posts the digest to Slack.

templates.title: Redis session lookup
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads a session hash from Redis by token, returns the stored user context to the caller, and refreshes the key’s expiry so active sessions stay alive.

skills.name: cache-with-expiry
skills.description: Cache a computed value in Redis with a TTL and read it back on later runs.
skills.content:
# Cache With Expiry

Store an expensive result in Redis so later runs reuse it.

## Steps
1. Run get on the cache key first; if a value is returned, use it and stop.
2. On a miss, compute the value, then run set with an ex expiry in seconds.
3. Use setnx instead of set when only the first writer should win.
4. Return the value to the caller.

## Output
Report whether the result was a cache hit or a fresh computation, and the key TTL.

skills.name: rate-limit-counter
skills.description: Track per-key request counts in Redis with a sliding expiry to enforce limits.
skills.content:
# Rate Limit Counter

Enforce a request budget using a Redis counter.

## Steps
1. Run incr on a counter key derived from the user or client id.
2. If the returned count is 1, run expire to start the window.
3. Compare the count to the allowed limit.
4. Allow or reject the request based on the result.

## Output
Return the current count, the limit, and whether the request is allowed. Include ttl for the reset time.

skills.name: manage-session-data
skills.description: Store and refresh session context in a Redis hash keyed by token.
skills.content:
# Manage Session Data

Keep session state in a Redis hash and keep active sessions alive.

## Steps
1. On write, run hset to store session fields under the session key.
2. On read, run hgetall by token to return the full session context.
3. Run expire to refresh the TTL so active sessions do not lapse.
4. Run delete on logout to clear the session.

## Output
Return the session context and confirm the refreshed expiry, or confirm deletion on logout.

skills.name: manage-work-queue
skills.description: Push jobs onto a Redis list and pop them for processing in order.
skills.content:
# Manage Work Queue

Use a Redis list as a simple job queue.

## Steps
1. Run rpush to enqueue a job payload onto the queue key.
2. Run lpop to dequeue the next job for processing (FIFO).
3. Check llen to monitor backlog depth.
4. Use lrange to inspect pending jobs without removing them.

## Output
Return the dequeued job, the remaining queue length, and processing status.

templates.title: Google Drive contract intake
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches a Google Drive intake folder for new contract PDFs, extracts clauses with Reducto, writes structured terms to a table, and pings legal in Slack.

templates.title: OneDrive contract intake
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls a OneDrive intake folder for new contract PDFs, extracts clauses with Reducto, writes the structured terms to a table, and pings legal in Teams.

templates.title: Reducto contract parser
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that uses Reducto to parse uploaded contract PDFs into structured clauses, writes payment terms, liability caps, and termination conditions to a table, and flags non-standard clauses.

templates.title: Reducto + knowledge base loader
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that parses every PDF in a Drive folder with Reducto, normalizes the structure, and upserts chunks into a knowledge base with section-aware metadata so retrieval returns the right passage.

templates.title: Reducto medical-record digester
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that parses medical record PDFs with Reducto, extracts diagnoses, medications, and visit summaries to structured rows, and produces a patient-facing one-pager file.

templates.title: Reducto + Mem0 contract memory
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that parses contracts with Reducto and writes the key terms into Mem0 per counterparty, so future interactions reference the real contract terms.

templates.title: Reducto invoice line-item extractor
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that parses incoming invoice PDFs with Reducto, extracts vendor, line items, tax, and totals into an accounts-payable table, and flags any invoice that fails to reconcile against its purchase order.

templates.title: Reducto financial-statement digitizer
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that parses quarterly financial-statement PDFs with Reducto, extracts the balance sheet and income statement figures into structured rows, and writes a normalized table the finance team can chart over time.

templates.title: Reducto form-intake router
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs each uploaded intake form through Reducto, extracts the applicant fields into a table, and routes the parsed submission to the right reviewer in Slack based on the form type.

templates.title: Textract + Reducto cross-format extractor
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that ingests mixed PDF and image files, routes images through AWS Textract and dense PDFs through Reducto, normalizes fields, and writes rows to a table.

skills.name: extract-document-text
skills.description: Parse an uploaded PDF into clean text for downstream summarizing or search.
skills.content:
# Extract Document Text

Turn a PDF into clean, structured text with Reducto.

## Steps
1. Pass the uploaded document (file or file path) to the parser.
2. Optionally limit to specific pages by passing a comma-separated page list.
3. Capture the extracted text and structure from the result.
4. Pass the text downstream for summarizing, classification, or indexing.

## Output
Return the extracted text and a brief note of the page count processed.

skills.name: extract-form-fields
skills.description: Parse an intake form PDF and pull structured fields into a table or record.
skills.content:
# Extract Form Fields

Lift structured fields out of a form PDF.

## Steps
1. Run the parser on the uploaded form document.
2. From the parsed text, identify the target fields (for example name, date, amount, form type).
3. Map the fields into a structured record and write them to a table.
4. Route the record to the right reviewer based on form type.

## Output
Return the extracted field record and confirm where it was stored or routed. Flag any field that could not be located.

skills.name: extract-invoice-tables
skills.description: Parse an invoice or financial PDF into structured line-item tables for AP automation.
skills.content:
# Extract Invoice Tables

Pull line-item tables out of invoices, receipts, or statements with Reducto.

## Steps
1. Run the parser on the uploaded invoice or financial document.
2. Set the table output format so tables come back in a structured, machine-readable shape.
3. Limit to the relevant pages with a comma-separated page list when the document is long.
4. Map header fields and line items into a record and write the rows to a table.

## Output
Return the parsed line items and invoice totals. Flag any row or amount that could not be confidently extracted.

templates.title: Mailgun + Resend transactional fallback
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that sends transactional emails through Mailgun by default and automatically falls back to Resend when Mailgun returns a send error or rate-limit response, normalizing the payload and writing every send and the provider used to a delivery table.

templates.title: Resend + Loops onboarding emails
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that listens for new signups, creates a Loops contact with the right user group, and sends the welcome email through Resend with a personalized subject and body so the first impression is on-brand and fast.

templates.title: Resend domain monitor
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that lists Resend domains, checks DNS verification status for each, and posts a Slack alert the moment any domain shows a verification or DKIM problem so we never silently lose deliverability.

templates.title: Resend transactional flow
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that listens for product events, renders the right transactional email body, sends it through Resend, then retrieves the message status after a short delay and writes delivery, open, and click events to a per-user activity table.

templates.title: Resend + AgentMail reply handler
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that sends outbound messages through Resend but routes replies into a per-customer AgentMail inbox, threads them with the original send, and posts unread inbox digests to the support owner.

templates.title: Resend marketing broadcast
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes a marketing message and a Resend audience, splits the recipient list into safe-volume batches, sends each batch through Resend with rate-limit pacing, and logs per-batch send results to a table.

templates.title: Resend audience sync
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that reads my subscriber list from a table, creates or updates each Resend contact in the matching audience, and removes contacts that have unsubscribed by deleting them so the Resend audience stays in sync with my source of truth.

templates.title: Resend unsubscribe handler
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that listens for unsubscribe events, looks up the matching Resend contact, updates it to unsubscribed, logs the opt-out reason to a table, and sends a confirmation email through Resend acknowledging the change.

templates.title: SendGrid + Resend failover
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that sends transactional emails through SendGrid by default and automatically falls back to Resend when the primary send fails or rate limits, logging every send and the provider used to a delivery table.

skills.name: send-transactional-email
skills.description: Send a personalized transactional email and confirm delivery via Resend.
skills.content:
# Send Transactional Email

Send a one-off transactional email through Resend.

## Steps
1. Compose the recipient, from address, subject, and HTML or text body, filling in personalization fields.
2. Run the send operation.
3. Capture the returned email id.
4. Optionally run get_email with the id to confirm the delivery status.

## Output
Return the email id and delivery status. If sending fails, report the error reason.

skills.name: add-contact-to-audience
skills.description: Create or update a Resend contact in an audience for marketing sends.
skills.content:
# Add Contact To Audience

Keep a Resend audience in sync with new contacts.

## Steps
1. Run list_contacts or get_contact to check whether the person already exists.
2. If new, run create_contact with email and name fields and the subscribed state.
3. If existing, run update_contact to refresh fields.
4. Confirm the contact is in the correct audience.

## Output
Return the contact id and whether it was created or updated.

skills.name: handle-unsubscribe
skills.description: Mark a Resend contact as unsubscribed and send a confirmation email.
skills.content:
# Handle Unsubscribe

Process an opt-out request cleanly.

## Steps
1. Run get_contact to look up the matching contact by email.
2. Run update_contact to set unsubscribed to true.
3. Log the opt-out reason for compliance records.
4. Run the send operation to deliver a brief confirmation acknowledging the change.

## Output
Confirm the contact is unsubscribed and the acknowledgement email id.

templates.title: RevenueCat MRR dashboard
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled daily workflow that pulls RevenueCat subscriber and offering data, calculates MRR, ARPU, and trial-to-paid conversion, logs the metrics to a tracking table with historical trends, and posts a daily Slack summary for the growth team.

templates.title: Entitlement granter
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that listens for a customer-success approval — for example a Slack reaction or a row in a table — looks up the RevenueCat subscriber, grants a promotional entitlement with the right expiry, and logs the grant in an audit table for compliance.

templates.title: Failed renewal recovery
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that lists RevenueCat subscribers with failed renewals, segments them by plan and tenure, drafts a tailored win-back email, sends it via Gmail, and tracks recovery outcomes in a table with retry cadence rules.

templates.title: Subscriber attribute sync
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that listens for changes in your customer table — like email, display name, or company — and updates the matching RevenueCat subscriber attributes so analytics and targeted offers always reflect the latest customer state.

templates.title: Trial expiry digest
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled daily workflow that lists RevenueCat subscribers whose trials expire in the next three days, ranks them by engagement, drafts a personalized conversion nudge, and emails the success team a prioritized list to call.

templates.title: Google Play refund operator
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that takes a refund approval from a support ticket, calls the RevenueCat Google Play refund operation with the right transaction identifier, revokes access, posts the outcome back on the ticket, and logs the action in a compliance table.

templates.title: Offering performance report
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled weekly workflow that pulls RevenueCat offerings and recent purchases, computes conversion rate per offering and per package, writes a narrative analysis file with recommendations, and Slacks growth leadership the top findings.

skills.name: check-subscription-status
skills.description: Look up a customer in RevenueCat and report their active entitlements.
skills.content:
# Check Subscription Status

Determine what a customer is entitled to right now.

## Steps
1. Run get_customer with the app user id.
2. Inspect the returned entitlements for active grants and expiration dates.
3. Determine whether the customer has the entitlement you are gating on.
4. Return a clear allow or deny decision.

## Output
Return the active entitlements, their expiration dates, and whether the gated feature should be unlocked.

skills.name: grant-promotional-access
skills.description: Grant a promotional entitlement to a customer for support or a campaign.
skills.content:
# Grant Promotional Access

Give a customer temporary access via a promotional entitlement.

## Steps
1. Confirm the target app user id with get_customer.
2. Run grant_entitlement with the entitlement identifier and duration.
3. Verify the grant by re-checking get_customer.
4. To reverse a grant later, run revoke_entitlement.

## Output
Confirm the granted entitlement, its duration, and the customer it was applied to.

skills.name: process-subscription-refund
skills.description: Refund and revoke a Google Play subscription for a customer support request.
skills.content:
# Process Subscription Refund

Handle a refund request for a store subscription.

## Steps
1. Look up the customer with get_customer to find the relevant subscription.
2. For Google Play, run refund_google_subscription with the store transaction id.
3. If access should end immediately, run revoke_google_subscription.
4. Log the action for the support record.

## Output
Confirm the refund and revocation status, and the affected customer and product.

skills.name: sync-subscriber-attributes
skills.description: Update RevenueCat subscriber attributes to power targeting and analytics.
skills.content:
# Sync Subscriber Attributes

Keep RevenueCat subscriber attributes current.

## Steps
1. Gather the attributes to set (for example email, plan tier, or campaign source).
2. Run update_subscriber_attributes for the app user id with the attribute map.
3. Confirm the update with get_customer.

## Output
Return the updated attributes and confirm they were applied to the subscriber.

templates.title: Google Groups onboarding sync
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches Rippling or Greenhouse for new hires, adds them to the right Google Groups based on team and department, and emails the new hire a list of the groups joined.

templates.title: Google Groups departure cleanup
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches Workday or Rippling for terminations and removes the departing user from every Google Group they belonged to, writing the change to a security audit log.

templates.title: Neo4j org-chart sync
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that pulls Workday or Rippling worker data, upserts employees and reporting relationships into Neo4j, and exposes a queryable org graph for downstream tools.

templates.title: Rippling new-hire provisioning
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls Rippling for new workers, creates accounts in the matching downstream tools, drops each new hire into the right Slack channels, books day-one onboarding via Google Calendar, and writes provisioning status to a tracking table.

templates.title: Rippling departure offboarder
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls Rippling for workers transitioning out, gathers their owned resources, deactivates downstream accounts, schedules data handoff meetings, posts a structured offboarding checklist to a table, and notifies the people team in Slack.

templates.title: Org chart export and review
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled weekly workflow that pulls Rippling workers, departments, teams, and titles, writes an updated org chart file, diffs against last week to find structural changes, and Slacks people operations any unexpected moves for review.

templates.title: Custom object data sync
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that reads rows from a Sim table representing custom Rippling objects — perks, equipment, allowances — and upserts them into Rippling so HR can manage company-specific data with the same governance as core worker records.

templates.title: Team and title auditor
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled monthly workflow that lists Rippling teams, titles, and job functions, flags duplicates, unused values, and inconsistent naming, writes a cleanup report file, and opens a Linear task for the people operations owner of each issue.

templates.title: Manager change notifier
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls Rippling workers for manager reassignments, notifies the worker and the new manager via email, schedules a thirty-minute intro on Google Calendar, and logs the transition in a tracking table for HR visibility.

templates.title: Department headcount digest
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled weekly workflow that pulls Rippling workers grouped by department and employment type, computes headcount, open requisitions, and growth versus the prior week, writes a narrative summary, and emails it to department heads.

skills.name: lookup-employee-profile
skills.description: Find a Rippling worker and return their role, department, and team details.
skills.content:
# Lookup Employee Profile

Retrieve a complete profile for an employee.

## Steps
1. Run list_workers filtered by name or attributes to find the worker, or list_users if you have a user id.
2. Run get_worker for the full record once identified.
3. Enrich with get_department, get_team, and get_title as needed for context.
4. Assemble the profile.

## Output
Return the worker name, title, department, team, and employment type. Note any field that is unavailable.

skills.name: department-headcount-report
skills.description: Group Rippling workers by department and employment type to report headcount.
skills.content:
# Department Headcount Report

Build a headcount snapshot across the org.

## Steps
1. Run list_departments to enumerate departments.
2. Run list_workers and group by department and employment type.
3. Compute headcount per group and compare against a prior snapshot for growth.
4. Write a narrative summary of the changes.

## Output
Return headcount per department and employment type, plus week-over-week change where available.

skills.name: manage-department
skills.description: Create or update a department record in Rippling for an org change.
skills.content:
# Manage Department

Keep the Rippling org structure current.

## Steps
1. Run list_departments to check whether the department already exists.
2. If new, run create_department with the name and parent details.
3. If it exists, run update_department to adjust the record.
4. Confirm with get_department.

## Output
Return the department id and whether it was created or updated.

skills.name: sync-custom-object-records
skills.description: Push external data (training, licenses, assets) onto Rippling custom object records.
skills.content:
# Sync Custom Object Records

Write product data onto Rippling profiles via custom objects.

## Steps
1. Run list_custom_objects to find the target object, then list_custom_object_fields to confirm its schema.
2. Build the records to write (for example training completion dates, license assignments, or asset ids).
3. Use create_custom_object_record or update_custom_object_record for single writes, or bulk_create_custom_object_records and bulk_update_custom_object_records for batches.
4. Verify with query_custom_object_records or get_custom_object_record_by_external_id.

## Output
Return the count of records created or updated and flag any that failed validation.

skills.name: run-rippling-report
skills.description: Trigger a Rippling report run and retrieve the completed results.
skills.content:
# Run Rippling Report

Generate and collect a Rippling report for downstream analysis.

## Steps
1. Run trigger_report_run for the target report id to start a run.
2. Capture the returned run id.
3. Poll get_report_run until the run completes.
4. Pass the results downstream to a table or summary.

## Output
Return the report run id, completion status, and a summary of the returned rows.

templates.title: Rootly incident war-room
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls Rootly for newly opened incidents, creates a Slack war-room channel for each, invites responders, posts the incident summary, and keeps the channel topic in sync with severity.

templates.title: Rootly retro generator
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls Rootly for recently closed incidents, drafts the retrospective doc, pulls the Slack thread and timeline, and assigns owners for follow-up actions in Linear.

templates.title: Rootly weekly digest
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled weekly workflow that summarizes Rootly incident counts, MTTR, top affected services, and outstanding action items, and posts a digest to leadership Slack.

templates.title: Rootly customer-comms drafter
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that drafts and queues customer-facing status updates during a Rootly incident based on severity and impacted services, holding for approval before publishing.

templates.title: Rootly action-item tracker
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that tracks Rootly follow-up actions across incidents, opens Linear tickets, and writes a tables-based dashboard that flags overdue items by owner.

templates.title: Rootly on-call digest
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled daily workflow that summarizes the past 24 hours of Rootly pages, the on-call responder load by person, and writes a digest to the SRE Slack channel.

templates.title: Rootly + LangSmith agent-incident tracker
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that for each Rootly incident involving an AI agent attaches the LangSmith trace, captures the failure mode, and writes the agent-quality regression analysis.

skills.name: declare-incident
skills.description: Open a Rootly incident with the right severity, service, and team assigned.
skills.content:
# Declare Incident

Spin up a structured Rootly incident from an alert or report.

## Steps
1. Run list_severities, list_services, and list_teams to resolve the correct ids.
2. Run create_incident with a clear title, summary, severity, affected service, and owning team.
3. Capture the returned incident id.
4. Add an opening timeline note with add_incident_event.

## Output
Return the incident id, severity, assigned team, and a link. Confirm the opening event was logged.

skills.name: post-incident-update
skills.description: Append a status update event to an active Rootly incident timeline.
skills.content:
# Post Incident Update

Keep an incident timeline current.

## Steps
1. Run get_incident to confirm the current state.
2. Run add_incident_event with the update text (mitigation steps, customer impact, next checkpoint).
3. Run update_incident if the severity or status has changed.

## Output
Return the appended event and the current incident status.

skills.name: triage-alerts
skills.description: List open Rootly alerts, acknowledge them, and escalate to an incident if needed.
skills.content:
# Triage Alerts

Work through the open alert queue.

## Steps
1. Run list_alerts to pull open alerts.
2. For each, run get_alert for detail and run acknowledge_alert to claim it.
3. If an alert warrants response, run create_incident and link it.
4. Run resolve_alert once the alert is handled.

## Output
Return how many alerts were acknowledged, resolved, and escalated to incidents.

skills.name: check-on-call
skills.description: Look up who is currently on call across Rootly schedules and escalation policies.
skills.content:
# Check On Call

Find the right person to page right now.

## Steps
1. Run list_schedules to enumerate on-call schedules.
2. Run list_on_calls to read the current rotation members.
3. Cross-reference list_escalation_policies for the escalation path.

## Output
Return the current on-call person per schedule and the escalation order.

skills.name: track-action-items
skills.description: Create and list retrospective action items tied to a Rootly incident.
skills.content:
# Track Action Items

Capture and follow up on postmortem action items.

## Steps
1. Run get_incident to confirm the incident context.
2. Run create_action_item for each follow-up with a clear owner and description.
3. Run list_action_items to review open items for the incident.

## Output
Return the created action items and the list of outstanding follow-ups.

templates.title: Athena S3 access audit
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that runs Athena queries against S3 access logs weekly, identifies unusual access patterns or new principals, and writes findings to a security audit table.

templates.title: Box to S3 backup
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that mirrors a Box folder tree into S3 nightly with incremental sync, captures the manifest, and pings Slack on any failed files.

templates.title: Clerk user roster archiver
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that exports the full Clerk user and organization roster to S3 on a retention schedule, and writes the snapshot manifest to a compliance table.

templates.title: CloudWatch metric archiver
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that exports CloudWatch metric snapshots into S3 long-term storage, preserving granularity for compliance, and writing a manifest table.

templates.title: Convex nightly backup to S3
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that runs each night, pages through every Convex table with List Documents, writes the exported JSON to S3 with date partitions, and records the run in an audit table.

templates.title: Datadog monitor config backup

templates.title: DynamoDB to S3 archive

skills.name: upload-and-share-asset
skills.description: Upload a generated file to an S3 bucket and return its object URL.
skills.content:
# Upload And Share Asset

Publish a file to S3 and hand back a usable link.

## Steps
1. Take the generated image or document as the object body.
2. Run put_object with the bucket, key, and content type.
3. Construct or capture the resulting object URL.
4. Write the link back to the originating record (for example a table row).

## Output
Return the object key and URL. Note the bucket and whether the object is publicly accessible.

skills.name: fetch-object-contents
skills.description: Download an object from S3 and pass its contents to downstream steps.
skills.content:
# Fetch Object Contents

Retrieve a file from S3 for processing.

## Steps
1. Identify the bucket and object key.
2. Run get_object to download the file.
3. Pass the contents downstream for parsing, summarizing, or transformation.

## Output
Return the object contents (or a file reference) and confirm the source key.

skills.name: list-bucket-objects
skills.description: List objects in an S3 bucket under a prefix for inventory or cleanup.
skills.content:
# List Bucket Objects

Enumerate what lives under an S3 prefix.

## Steps
1. Run list_objects with the bucket and an optional prefix to scope the listing.
2. Page through results if the listing is truncated.
3. Filter the keys by name, date, or size as needed.

## Output
Return the matching object keys with sizes and last-modified dates.

skills.name: archive-object
skills.description: Copy an S3 object to an archive location and delete the original.
skills.content:
# Archive Object

Move an object to an archive prefix or bucket.

## Steps
1. Run copy_object from the source key to the archive destination key.
2. Verify the copy succeeded.
3. Run delete_object on the original to complete the move.

## Output
Confirm the archived destination key and that the original was removed.

skills.name: capture-inbound-lead
skills.description: Create or update a Salesforce lead from an inbound signal and assign follow-up.
skills.content:
# Capture Inbound Lead

Get an inbound lead into Salesforce cleanly.

## Steps
1. Run get_leads to check for an existing lead with the same email.
2. If new, run create_lead with name, company, email, and source; otherwise run update_lead to enrich it.
3. Run create_task to assign a follow-up to the owner.

## Output
Return the lead id, whether it was created or updated, and the follow-up task id.

skills.name: log-opportunity-update
skills.description: Advance a Salesforce opportunity stage and record the change for the account.
skills.content:
# Log Opportunity Update

Keep a deal current in Salesforce.

## Steps
1. Run get_opportunities to locate the deal.
2. Run update_opportunity to set the new stage, amount, or close date.
3. Run create_task to capture the next action.

## Output
Return the opportunity id, its new stage, and the next-step task. Note if the stage moved to closed-won or closed-lost.

skills.name: sync-account-contacts
skills.description: Pull a Salesforce account with its contacts for a 360 view.
skills.content:
# Sync Account Contacts

Assemble a full picture of an account.

## Steps
1. Run get_accounts to resolve the target account.
2. Run get_contacts filtered to the account to list its people.
3. Optionally run get_opportunities and get_cases for active deals and support context.

## Output
Return the account, its contacts with roles, and a summary of open opportunities and cases.

skills.name: create-support-case
skills.description: Open a Salesforce case for a customer issue and assign the owner.
skills.content:
# Create Support Case

File a support case in Salesforce.

## Steps
1. Run get_contacts or get_accounts to link the case to the right record.
2. Run create_case with subject, description, priority, and origin.
3. Run create_task for the assigned owner if a follow-up is required.

## Output
Return the case id, priority, and linked account or contact.

skills.name: run-sales-report
skills.description: Run a Salesforce report and summarize the results for a stakeholder.
skills.content:
# Run Sales Report

Pull live numbers from a Salesforce report.

## Steps
1. Run list_reports to find the report, or use a known report id.
2. Run run_report to execute it and capture the result set.
3. Summarize the key metrics and notable changes.

## Output
Return the headline metrics and a short narrative of what the report shows.

skills.name: review-expense-reports
skills.description: List submitted SAP Concur expense reports, inspect line items, and flag policy exceptions.
skills.content:
# Review Expense Reports

Surface expense reports that need attention and check them against policy.

## Steps
1. Run List Expense Reports to pull recently submitted reports, or List Reports To Approve for items awaiting the current approver.
2. For each report of interest, run Get Expense Report and List Expenses to read the individual line items, then List Exceptions to see Concur policy flags.
3. Summarize totals, flagged line items, and any missing receipts.

## Output
Return a per-report summary with the report ID, owner, total amount, and a list of policy exceptions or anomalies that warrant follow-up.

skills.name: route-report-approval
skills.description: Approve or send back a submitted SAP Concur expense report after review.
skills.content:
# Route Report Approval

Act on an expense report once a review decision is made.

## Steps
1. Confirm the report ID and the decision.
2. To approve, run Approve Expense Report. To return it for correction, run Send Back Expense Report with a clear comment explaining what must change.
3. Optionally run Create Report Comment first to leave context for the submitter.

## Output
Confirm the report ID, the action taken (approved or sent back), and the comment provided so the decision is auditable.

skills.name: capture-quick-expense
skills.description: Create a quick expense in SAP Concur from a receipt, attaching the receipt image.
skills.content:
# Capture Quick Expense

Log an out-of-pocket expense quickly, with the receipt attached.

## Steps
1. If you have a receipt image, run Upload Receipt Image and keep the returned receipt ID, or use Create Quick Expense (With Image) to do both in one step.
2. Run Create Quick Expense with the vendor, amount, currency, and transaction date.
3. Verify the entry with Get Expense.

## Output
Report the created quick expense ID, the captured vendor and amount, and confirm the receipt image is attached.

skills.name: manage-travel-requests
skills.description: List and act on SAP Concur travel requests, moving them through the approval workflow.
skills.content:
# Manage Travel Requests

Handle pre-trip travel requests through their approval lifecycle.

## Steps
1. Run List Travel Requests to find pending requests, then Get Travel Request for full detail on a specific one.
2. Review the expected expenses and any linked cash advance via Get Request Cash Advance.
3. Run Move Travel Request (Workflow Action) to advance, approve, or send back the request based on the decision.

## Output
Return the travel request ID, destination, estimated cost, and the workflow action applied so the trip approval state is clear.

skills.name: look-up-business-partner
skills.description: Find a customer, supplier, or business partner in SAP S4HANA and return their master data.
skills.content:
# Look Up Business Partner

Retrieve master data for a customer, supplier, or general business partner.

## Steps
1. Run List Business Partners (or List Customers / List Suppliers for the typed view) with a filter on name, ID, or other criteria.
2. Once the right record is identified, run Get Business Partner, Get Customer, or Get Supplier to pull full detail.
3. Note key fields such as the partner ID, addresses, roles, and payment terms.

## Output
Return the matched partner ID and the relevant master-data fields, and call out if no match or multiple matches were found.

skills.name: check-sales-order-status
skills.description: Look up a SAP S4HANA sales order and trace its related deliveries and billing documents.
skills.content:
# Check Sales Order Status

Trace a sales order from creation through delivery and billing.

## Steps
1. Run List Sales Orders to find the order, or Get Sales Order if you already have the order number.
2. Run List Outbound Deliveries and List Billing Documents to find the delivery and invoice tied to that order.
3. Get any specific delivery or billing document for line-level detail.

## Output
Return the sales order number, its status, the linked delivery numbers, and billing document numbers so the order-to-cash state is clear.

skills.name: create-purchase-requisition
skills.description: Create a purchase requisition in SAP S4HANA via OData from supplied line-item details.
skills.content:
# Create Purchase Requisition

Raise a purchase requisition for procurement.

## Steps
1. Gather the requisition header and line items: material or product, quantity, plant, and delivery date.
2. Optionally run List Products and Get Product to confirm material numbers before submitting.
3. Run Create Purchase Requisition with the assembled payload.
4. Confirm by running Get Purchase Requisition on the returned number.

## Output
Report the created purchase requisition number and a summary of its line items, and surface any OData validation error verbatim.

skills.name: check-material-stock
skills.description: Read current material stock and recent material documents for an item in SAP S4HANA.
skills.content:
# Check Material Stock

Report on-hand stock and recent inventory movements for a material.

## Steps
1. Run List Material Stock filtered by the material and plant to read current quantities.
2. Run List Material Documents to see recent goods movements for that material, and Get Material Document for line detail on a specific posting.
3. Compare on-hand stock against expected levels.

## Output
Return the material number, plant, current stock quantity, and a short list of recent material movements with their document numbers.

templates.title: Sendblue lead speed-to-text

templates.title: Sendblue inbound reply autoresponder
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered when a Sendblue message is received that classifies the inbound text, drafts a context-aware reply with an agent, and sends it back to the same number as an iMessage.

templates.title: Sendblue iMessage vs SMS routing
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that evaluates whether a recipient number supports iMessage with Sendblue, then sends a rich iMessage when supported or a plain SMS fallback otherwise.

templates.title: Sendblue conversational support agent
