skills.name: send-imessage-notification
skills.description: Send an iMessage or SMS notification to a single recipient via Sendblue.
skills.content:
# Send an iMessage or SMS Notification

Deliver a message to one recipient through your Sendblue number.

## Steps
1. Choose the Send Message operation.
2. Enter the Recipient Number and your From Number in E.164 format (for example +19998887777).
3. Write the Message text. To send media instead of or alongside text, add a Media URL.
4. Provide your Sendblue API Key ID and API Secret Key.

## Output
Return the message status (QUEUED, SENT, DELIVERED, ERROR) and the message handle so the send can be tracked.

skills.name: route-imessage-or-sms
skills.description: Check whether a number supports iMessage before sending with Sendblue.
skills.content:
# Route iMessage vs SMS

Decide how to reach a recipient based on their service.

## Steps
1. Use the Evaluate Service operation with the Recipient Number to learn whether the number supports iMessage or only SMS.
2. Branch on the returned service value.
3. Send a rich iMessage when supported, or a plain SMS fallback otherwise, using the Send Message operation.

## Output
Return the evaluated number and its supported service so downstream steps can branch correctly.

skills.name: reply-to-inbound-message
skills.description: Trigger on an inbound Sendblue message and reply automatically.
skills.content:
# Reply to an Inbound Message

Respond to customers as soon as they text in.

## Steps
1. Add the Sendblue Message Received trigger and point your Sendblue Receive Webhook at the generated URL.
2. Read the inbound content, from_number, and service from the trigger output.
3. Draft a reply with an agent and send it back with the Send Message operation, using the from_number as the recipient.

## Output
Return the reply message handle and status so the conversation can be tracked.

templates.title: Mailchimp + SendGrid hybrid sender
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that uses Mailchimp for marketing audience management and segmentation but sends the actual campaign through SendGrid for deliverability, syncing send results, opens, and clicks back to the Mailchimp audience as merge fields.

templates.title: SendGrid transactional pipeline
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that listens for product events from my tables — signup, password reset, receipt — picks the matching SendGrid dynamic template, populates the variables, sends the email, and writes the message ID back to the table for audit.

templates.title: SendGrid send-failure monitor
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that sends emails through SendGrid, logs each send result and any error to a delivery table, and posts a Slack alert summarizing failure patterns by recipient domain and template when the failure rate crosses a threshold.

templates.title: SendGrid + Resend failover
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that sends transactional emails through SendGrid by default and automatically falls back to Resend when the primary send fails or rate limits, logging every send and the provider used to a delivery table.

templates.title: SendGrid contact list cleaner
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that searches SendGrid marketing contacts for invalid or duplicate entries, removes the bad addresses, merges duplicates, and writes a cleanup report to a tracking table.

templates.title: SendGrid + SES enterprise sender
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that splits transactional traffic between SendGrid and AWS SES based on message category and recipient region, balances volume to stay under per-provider limits, and writes provider, status, and latency to a delivery table.

templates.title: SendGrid + Mailgun send scorecard
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled weekly workflow that sends categorized test messages through both SendGrid and Mailgun, records each provider response, latency, and error to a delivery table, and generates a scorecard file recommending which provider to use per send category.

templates.title: SendGrid segmented list builder
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that reads a freshly scored audience from a table, creates a new SendGrid marketing list, adds each matching contact to the list, and removes anyone who no longer qualifies so the segment is ready for the next campaign send.

skills.name: send-transactional-email
skills.description: Send a transactional email through SendGrid, optionally using a dynamic template and variables.
skills.content:
# Send Transactional Email

Send a single transactional email (receipt, confirmation, password reset) through SendGrid.

## Steps
1. Set the verified From address and the recipient To address.
2. For a one-off message, set the Subject and Content (choose HTML or plain text). For a templated message, set the Template ID and provide Dynamic Template Data as a JSON object whose keys match the template variables.
3. Add CC, BCC, or Reply-To addresses if needed, and attach files via Attachments.
4. Run the Send Mail operation and capture the returned message ID.

## Output
Report whether the send succeeded and include the SendGrid message ID for later delivery tracking and audit.

skills.name: sync-contacts-to-list
skills.description: Add or update marketing contacts and place them on a specific SendGrid list for a campaign segment.
skills.content:
# Sync Contacts to List

Upsert marketing contacts and assign them to a SendGrid list so a segment is ready to receive a campaign.

## Steps
1. If the target list does not exist, run Create List with a descriptive name and keep the returned list ID.
2. Build a JSON array of contacts, each with at least an email plus optional first name, last name, and custom fields.
3. Run Add Contacts to List with the list ID and the contacts array.
4. Optionally run Remove Contacts from List to drop addresses that no longer qualify for the segment.

## Output
Report the list ID, the count of contacts added, and the job ID returned for the async upsert.

skills.name: clean-contact-list
skills.description: Search SendGrid marketing contacts for invalid or unwanted addresses and remove them.
skills.content:
# Clean Contact List

Find and remove low-quality marketing contacts using SendGrid Query Language.

## Steps
1. Run Search Contacts with an SGQL query that targets the unwanted records (for example addresses matching a bad domain or stale by created date).
2. Collect the contact IDs from the results.
3. Run Delete Contacts with the comma-separated contact IDs, or Remove Contacts from List to drop them only from a specific segment.
4. Record what was removed for a cleanup report.

## Output
Report the search criteria used, the number of contacts found, and how many were deleted or removed from the list.

skills.name: create-dynamic-template
skills.description: Create a SendGrid dynamic template and an active version with HTML and a subject line.
skills.content:
# Create Dynamic Template

Stand up a reusable SendGrid dynamic template for a recurring transactional message.

## Steps
1. Run Create Template with a descriptive name and the dynamic generation.
2. Keep the returned template ID.
3. Run Create Template Version against that template ID, supplying a version name, the Template Subject (Handlebars variables allowed), and the HTML content. Set the version active so it is used on send.
4. Optionally supply plain text content as a fallback.

## Output
Report the template ID and version, and confirm the active version is ready to reference from Send Mail operations.

templates.title: incident.io postmortem starter
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that polls incident.io for recently resolved incidents, pulls the Slack thread, related Sentry errors, and deploy timeline, then drafts a postmortem doc in Google Docs.

templates.title: LaunchDarkly flag-flip safety gate
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that reads the LaunchDarkly audit log for recent production flag flips, checks Sentry error rate and Datadog SLO burn against each, toggles the flag back off on regression, and posts to Slack.

templates.title: Bug triage agent
templates.prompt: Build an agent that monitors Sentry for new errors, automatically triages them by severity and affected users, creates Linear tickets for critical issues with full stack traces, and sends a Slack notification to the on-call channel.

templates.title: Sentry error triage
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that polls Sentry for new unresolved issues, classifies severity, groups similar issues, creates a Linear ticket on first occurrence above the threshold, and pings the owning team in Slack.

templates.title: Sentry release health gate
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that runs after a Vercel deploy, checks Sentry release health, and rolls back the deploy if the error rate exceeds the threshold, posting an alert to Slack.

templates.title: Sentry weekly regression brief
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled weekly workflow that compares Sentry error rates week-over-week, identifies top regressors, and writes a brief to engineering leadership in Slack.

templates.title: Sentry source-map verifier
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that scans Sentry for issues with missing or stale source maps, writes a tracking table, and opens Linear tickets for the worst offenders.

templates.title: Sentry customer-impact mapper
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes a Sentry issue and matches affected users to CRM accounts, scoring customer impact, and creates a customer-facing incident note in HubSpot for the worst-affected accounts.

templates.title: Sentry release tracker on deploy
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches GitHub for merges to main, creates a new Sentry release with the commit range, marks the deploy in Sentry for the production environment, and posts the release notes and linked issues to Slack so the team knows what shipped.

templates.title: Incident postmortem writer
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that when triggered after an incident, pulls the Slack thread from the incident channel, gathers relevant Sentry errors and deployment logs, and drafts a structured postmortem with timeline, root cause, and action items.

templates.title: Telegram alert relay
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that listens for critical alerts from Sentry or PagerDuty and forwards a concise summary with severity, link, and the on-call person to a Telegram group.

skills.name: triage-unresolved-errors
skills.description: List unresolved Sentry issues, rank them by impact, and summarize the most urgent errors to fix.
skills.content:
# Triage Unresolved Errors

Produce a prioritized view of the Sentry errors that most need attention.

## Steps
1. Run List Issues with the query is:unresolved, sorting by frequency or user count and setting a stats period such as 24h or 7d.
2. For the top issues, run Get Issue to pull the title, culprit, event count, and number of affected users.
3. Rank by a blend of event volume, affected users, and recency.

## Output
Return a ranked list of issues with their ID, title, event count, affected users, and a one-line recommendation for each. Link each issue so an engineer can open it directly.

skills.name: resolve-or-assign-issue
skills.description: Update a Sentry issue to change status, assign an owner, or bookmark it for follow-up.
skills.content:
# Resolve or Assign Issue

Act on a specific Sentry issue once a decision has been made.

## Steps
1. Identify the issue ID (from a triage step or a notification).
2. Run Update Issue, setting the new status (resolved, ignored, or resolved in next release) as appropriate.
3. To route ownership, set Assign To with a user ID or email. Bookmark or subscribe if the team wants to track it.

## Output
Confirm the issue ID, its new status, and the assignee, so the change is auditable.

skills.name: investigate-issue-events
skills.description: Pull the events behind a Sentry issue to inspect impacted users, environments, and context.
skills.content:
# Investigate Issue Events

Drill into the raw events for an issue to understand who and what is affected.

## Steps
1. Run List Events for the project, optionally filtering by an issue ID and an events search query (for example user.email or environment filters).
2. Run Get Event on a representative event ID to retrieve the full payload: tags, breadcrumbs, request context, and stack trace.
3. Group findings by environment, release, browser, or OS.

## Output
Summarize the affected environments and users, the common context across events, and the likely trigger, citing the specific event IDs examined.

skills.name: track-release-and-deploy
skills.description: Create a Sentry release for a version and mark a deploy to an environment for regression tracking.
skills.content:
# Track Release and Deploy

Register a new version in Sentry so errors can be attributed to the release that introduced them.

## Steps
1. Run Create Release with the version string and the comma-separated project slugs. Add the git ref, release URL, and commits JSON if available so Sentry can associate suspect commits.
2. Run Create Deploy with the same version and the target environment (for example production), including start and finish times.
3. Optionally run List Releases afterward to confirm the version is registered.

## Output
Report the created release version, the deploy environment, and confirm both were recorded for regression monitoring.

templates.title: Serper SERP digest
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled daily workflow that runs Serper searches for tracked keywords, writes the SERP positions of my domain into a tables-based SEO log, and pings on changes.

templates.title: Serper competitor SERP watcher
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that runs Serper searches for competitor keywords weekly, captures top SERP entries, and writes a competitive SEO digest to Slack.

templates.title: Serper news monitor
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that uses Serper news search for brand keywords, classifies each result, and posts notable mentions to a Slack PR channel.

templates.title: Serper local-pack tracker
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that uses Serper to track Google local-pack rankings for tracked queries by city, writes the results to a tables-based SEO log, and surfaces wins.

templates.title: Serper research agent
templates.prompt: Build an agent that uses Serper as a primary web-search tool, returns answers with citations, and saves long-form research to a knowledge base.

templates.title: Serper image-search collector
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that uses Serper image search for brand or product mentions, captures unique image URLs into a table, and flags potential trademark misuse.

templates.title: Serper geo-SERP comparator
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that runs Serper across multiple regions for the same keywords, identifies geo-relevant ranking differences, and writes the analysis to a file.

skills.name: research-web-topic
skills.description: Run a Serper web search on a topic and synthesize the top organic results into a sourced summary.
skills.content:
# Research Web Topic

Gather current web results on a topic and turn them into a concise, sourced briefing.

## Steps
1. Run the search operation with a focused query. Set the country and language for the target audience and choose a result count (10 to 100) appropriate to the depth needed.
2. Read the organic results, titles, snippets, and any answer box or knowledge graph data.
3. Synthesize the findings, noting agreement and disagreement across sources.

## Output
Return a short summary of what the web says about the topic, each key claim linked to the result URL it came from.

skills.name: monitor-news-mentions
skills.description: Search recent news for a brand, person, or topic via Serper and summarize the coverage.
skills.content:
# Monitor News Mentions

Track what the news is saying about a brand, competitor, person, or topic.

## Steps
1. Run the news operation with the entity or topic as the query, setting country and language to scope the coverage.
2. Collect the headlines, sources, publish dates, and snippets.
3. Group the coverage by sentiment or theme and highlight the most recent and most prominent items.

## Output
Return a dated list of news items with source and headline, plus a short overall read on tone and notable developments.

skills.name: compare-regional-rankings
skills.description: Run the same Serper query across multiple regions to compare search rankings by geography.
skills.content:
# Compare Regional Rankings

See how search results differ for the same query across countries.

## Steps
1. Pick the target keyword and the set of countries to compare.
2. Run the search operation once per country, varying only the country (and language where relevant), keeping the result count consistent.
3. Line up the top organic results per region and note which domains rank where.

## Output
Return a per-region ranking comparison for the keyword, calling out domains that rank strongly in some regions but not others.

skills.name: find-local-businesses
skills.description: Use the Serper places operation to find local businesses for a query and area, and rank them.
skills.content:
# Find Local Businesses

Pull Google Maps style local results for a query in a target area.

## Steps
1. Run the places operation with a query that includes the business type and location (for example coffee shops in Seattle), setting the country and language to scope results.
2. Read each place result: name, address, rating, review count, category, and phone or website where present.
3. Rank or filter the results by rating, review volume, or proximity to the target area.

## Output
Return a ranked list of local businesses with name, address, rating, and review count, noting the top candidates for the query.

templates.title: JSM-to-ServiceNow bridge
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that mirrors Jira Service Management incident requests into ServiceNow incident records and vice versa, keeping status, assignment, and comments in sync so teams on either side see the same truth.

templates.title: ServiceNow incident commander

templates.title: ServiceNow change request analyzer

templates.title: ServiceNow asset audit
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that queries the ServiceNow CMDB for assets missing owner, lifecycle, or last-discovered fields, flags stale or orphaned records in a tracking table, and opens remediation tasks against the responsible group.

templates.title: ServiceNow ticket auto-classifier
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered by new ServiceNow incidents that classifies category and subcategory, sets impact and urgency, infers the affected service from the description, and routes the ticket to the right assignment group.

templates.title: ServiceNow weekly ops digest
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled weekly workflow that pulls ServiceNow incident, change, and request data, calculates MTTR, change success rate, and top failing services, and posts a digest to Slack with the standout records linked.

templates.title: ServiceNow ticket deflection bot
templates.prompt: Build a Slack bot that lets employees report IT issues in natural language, reads similar resolved ServiceNow records to suggest a fix first, and only creates a new ServiceNow incident record with the right category when self-service does not resolve it.

skills.name: create-incident
skills.description: Create a new ServiceNow incident record with the right category, priority, and description.
skills.content:
# Create Incident

File a new ServiceNow incident from a reported issue.

## Steps
1. Use the Create Record operation against the incident table.
2. Populate the field values: a clear short description, the longer description, category, and priority or impact and urgency.
3. Set caller or assignment group fields when known.

## Output
Return the created record sys_id and incident number so the reporter can track it, and echo the category and priority that were set.

skills.name: search-records
skills.description: Query a ServiceNow table for records matching a condition and return the matching rows.
skills.content:
# Search Records

Find records in any ServiceNow table that match a condition.

## Steps
1. Use the Read Records operation against the target table (for example incident, change_request, or sc_task).
2. Provide an encoded query to filter (for example active incidents in a category) and limit the number of rows returned.
3. Choose the display-value setting so returned fields are human-readable rather than raw sys_ids when needed.

## Output
Return the matched records with their key fields and sys_ids, and report how many matched the query.

skills.name: update-record-status
skills.description: Update fields on an existing ServiceNow record, such as state, assignment, or work notes.
skills.content:
# Update Record Status

Modify an existing ServiceNow record once a decision or action is taken.

## Steps
1. Identify the record by its sys_id (from a search step or a notification).
2. Use the Update Record operation against the correct table, supplying only the fields to change such as state, assigned_to, or work_notes.
3. Confirm the change by reading the record back.

## Output
Confirm the record number, the fields that changed, and their new values so the update is auditable.

templates.title: Excel invoice generator
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that reads a sales orders table, populates a Microsoft Excel invoice template per order, and saves the file to a SharePoint folder for finance review.

templates.title: Excel + SharePoint forecast hub
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that aggregates regional forecasts submitted in Microsoft Excel files on SharePoint, normalizes formats, and writes a consolidated forecast table for leadership.

templates.title: Microsoft Planner retrospective
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that runs at the end of a sprint, pulls completed Microsoft Planner tasks, summarizes wins and patterns, and writes the retro doc to a SharePoint page.

templates.title: OneDrive backup verifier
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that verifies OneDrive backups by sampling files and comparing checksums against the originating SharePoint copy, writing the report to an SRE table.

templates.title: SharePoint policy publisher
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that turns a Google Docs policy update into a published SharePoint page, posts the change diff to the policies team in Microsoft Teams, and writes the version history.

templates.title: SharePoint stale-page sweeper
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that lists SharePoint pages not updated in 180 days, opens an owner-review thread in Teams, and archives pages once the owner approves.

templates.title: SharePoint knowledge agent
templates.prompt: Build an agent that indexes SharePoint sites into a knowledge base, answers internal questions with cited links, and deploys as a Teams chat endpoint.

templates.title: SharePoint external-share audit
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that audits SharePoint external sharing, flags items above the sensitivity threshold, and posts a security report to Teams compliance channel.

templates.title: SharePoint onboarding hub
templates.prompt: Build a workflow triggered by a new hire in Workday that creates a personalized SharePoint onboarding hub with role-relevant docs and shares it with the hire and their manager.

templates.title: SharePoint search-relevance auditor
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that runs benchmark queries against SharePoint search weekly, scores the top result relevance, and writes a quality report to Teams.

templates.title: SharePoint to Confluence migrator
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that imports SharePoint pages into Confluence under matching spaces, preserves attachments, and writes a mapping table so links can be redirected.

skills.name: publish-site-page
skills.description: Create a new SharePoint page on a site with a title and content body.
skills.content:
# Publish Site Page

Create a new page on a SharePoint site, for example an announcement or knowledge article.

## Steps
1. Run List Sites to find the target site and note its identifier.
2. Run Create Page on that site with a clear title and the page content body.
3. Optionally run Read Page afterward to confirm the page was created as intended.

## Output
Return the created page title and its URL or identifier so the page can be shared.

skills.name: append-list-items
skills.description: Add rows to a SharePoint list, creating the list first if it does not yet exist.
skills.content:
# Append List Items

Write structured rows into a SharePoint list.

## Steps
1. Run List Sites to locate the site, then Read List to confirm the target list and its column schema.
2. If the list does not exist, run Create List with the needed columns.
3. Run Add List Items with the field values mapped to the list columns.

## Output
Return the list name and the number of items added, and confirm the field values matched the list schema.

skills.name: read-list-data
skills.description: Read items from a SharePoint list and summarize the rows for downstream use.
skills.content:
# Read List Data

Pull the contents of a SharePoint list into the workflow.

## Steps
1. Run List Sites to find the site, then Read List against the target list.
2. Inspect the returned items and their column values.
3. Filter or summarize the rows as needed for the task.

## Output
Return the list items with their relevant column values and a count of rows read.

skills.name: upload-file-to-site
skills.description: Upload a file to a SharePoint site document library from a previous block.
skills.content:
# Upload File to Site

Store a file in a SharePoint document library.

## Steps
1. Run List Sites to identify the destination site.
2. Provide the file from a previous block and run Upload File to the target site library.
3. Confirm the upload completed.

## Output
Return the uploaded file name and its location on the SharePoint site.

templates.title: Google Sheets inventory sync
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that pulls Shopify inventory into Google Sheets hourly, calculates days-of-cover, and highlights items needing reorder for the ops team.

templates.title: Sendblue order-status notifier

templates.title: Shopify VIP segmenter

templates.title: Fulfillment status tracker
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that lists Shopify orders and their fulfillment status, updates a status table with shipped, in-transit, and delivered states, and proactively emails customers when their order misses an SLA so support gets ahead of the inquiry.

templates.title: Product launch publisher
templates.prompt: Build a workflow that takes a new product brief, creates the product in Shopify with variants and pricing, adds it to the right collection, drafts a launch announcement, and queues a Slack and email broadcast for marketing review before going live.

templates.title: Order anomaly detector
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that runs every fifteen minutes, lists recent Shopify orders, scores each for anomalies — high value, unusual destination, mismatched billing — flags suspects in a review queue table, and Slacks the operations team for hands-on inspection.

templates.title: Twilio order-status notifier
templates.prompt: Create a workflow triggered when an order ships that looks up the customer’s phone number and sends a Twilio SMS with the tracking number and estimated delivery date.

templates.title: Webflow product catalog sync
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that mirrors Shopify products and pricing into a Webflow CMS product collection, keeps both in sync, and posts conflict alerts to Slack.

templates.title: WhatsApp order tracking
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches Shopify shipment events and sends customers a WhatsApp message with the tracking number, ETA, and a follow-up review request after delivery.

skills.name: create-product-listing
skills.description: Create a new Shopify product with title, description, status, and variants.
skills.content:
# Create Product Listing

Add a new product to the Shopify store.

## Steps
1. Run Create Product with the title, body description, vendor, and product type.
2. Set the status (active, draft, or archived) so the product publishes only when ready.
3. Verify with Get Product on the returned product ID.

## Output
Return the new product ID, title, and status, and confirm the listing was created as draft or active as intended.

skills.name: process-recent-orders
skills.description: List recent Shopify orders and summarize them by status, value, or fulfillment need.
skills.content:
# Process Recent Orders

Review the latest orders to triage fulfillment and flag anything unusual.

## Steps
1. Run List Orders filtered by status (open, closed, cancelled, or any) and a recent time window.
2. For orders needing detail, run Get Order to read line items, customer, and shipping address.
3. Group orders by fulfillment status and total value.

## Output
Return a summary of recent orders with their order numbers, totals, and status, highlighting any that need immediate fulfillment or review.

skills.name: fulfill-order
skills.description: Create a fulfillment for a Shopify order and update its status.
skills.content:
# Fulfill Order

Mark an order as fulfilled once it has shipped.

## Steps
1. Run Get Order to confirm the order and its line items, and List Locations to identify the fulfilling location.
2. Run Create Fulfillment for the order, supplying the location and tracking details if available.
3. Optionally run Update Order to record any notes.

## Output
Confirm the order number, the fulfillment created, and any tracking number supplied.

skills.name: adjust-inventory
skills.description: Check and adjust Shopify inventory levels for an item at a location.
skills.content:
# Adjust Inventory

Reconcile stock levels for an inventory item.

## Steps
1. Run List Inventory Items and List Locations to identify the item and the location.
2. Run Get Inventory Level to read the current available quantity.
3. Run Adjust Inventory with the delta needed to reach the correct count.

## Output
Report the inventory item, the location, the previous and new quantities, and the adjustment applied.

skills.name: manage-customer-record
skills.description: Create, look up, or update a Shopify customer record.
skills.content:
# Manage Customer Record

Maintain a customer profile in Shopify.

## Steps
1. To find an existing customer, run List Customers with a filter or Get Customer by ID.
2. To add a new one, run Create Customer with name, email, and any tags.
3. To change details, run Update Customer with only the fields to modify.

## Output
Return the customer ID, name, and email, and note whether the record was created, found, or updated.

templates.title: Ahrefs + Similarweb growth scoreboard
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled monthly workflow that joins Ahrefs SEO data with Similarweb traffic intelligence, writes a growth scoreboard table, and emails leadership.

templates.title: Polymarket + Similarweb event volume tracker
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that overlays Polymarket market activity with Similarweb traffic for the involved entities, identifies volume-driving news, and writes the analysis.

templates.title: Similarweb traffic intelligence
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that pulls Similarweb traffic data for tracked competitor domains monthly, writes traffic, sources, and engagement to a tables-based scoreboard, and flags step changes in Slack.

templates.title: Similarweb account intel sync
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that watches my CRM for new accounts, pulls Similarweb data on each account domain, writes traffic estimates, rankings, and engagement signals back to the account record for sales context.

templates.title: Similarweb category benchmarking
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that pulls Similarweb category rank, visit duration, and bounce rate for my domain and a set of tracked competitors, then writes a ranked benchmarking table for the marketing review.

templates.title: Similarweb funnel-source analyzer
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that pulls Similarweb traffic-source data for my domain and competitors, surfaces shifting acquisition channels, and writes the analysis to a marketing table.

templates.title: Similarweb traffic-source overlap finder
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that pulls Similarweb traffic-source breakdowns for my domain and tracked competitors, identifies channels where competitors over-index, and writes an acquisition opportunity table.

templates.title: Similarweb engagement scorecard
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that pulls Similarweb bounce rate, pages per visit, and average visit duration for my domain and key competitors, writes the engagement metrics to a table, and posts a Slack scorecard highlighting where my site under- or over-performs the set.

templates.title: Similarweb prospect prioritizer
templates.prompt: Create a workflow that reads a list of target company domains from a table, pulls each domain's Similarweb website overview and monthly visits, scores them by traffic size and growth, and writes a prioritized outbound list for the sales team.

skills.name: profile-website-traffic
skills.description: Pull a Similarweb website overview and traffic metrics for a domain and summarize its scale.
skills.content:
# Profile Website Traffic

Build a quick traffic profile for a single domain.

## Steps
1. Run Website Overview for the domain to get a high-level snapshot.
2. Run Traffic Visits, Bounce Rate, Pages Per Visit, and Visit Duration for deeper engagement metrics, setting the country (or worldwide) to scope the data.
3. Interpret the numbers together: high visits with a low bounce rate and long duration indicates strong engagement.

## Output
Return a concise profile of the domain: estimated monthly visits, bounce rate, pages per visit, and average visit duration, with a one-line read on overall traffic health.

skills.name: compare-competitor-domains

skills.content:
# Compare Competitor Domains

Benchmark a set of competing domains on traffic and engagement.

## Steps
1. For each domain, run Website Overview and Traffic Visits using the same country scope so the numbers are comparable.
2. Optionally add Bounce Rate and Pages Per Visit for an engagement dimension.
3. Rank the domains by visits and engagement.

## Output
Return a ranked table of the domains with their visits, bounce rate, and engagement metrics, and a short read on which competitor leads.

skills.name: score-prospect-domains
skills.description: Score a list of prospect domains by Similarweb traffic size to prioritize outreach.
skills.content:
# Score Prospect Domains

Prioritize sales prospects by the size of their web traffic.

## Steps
1. For each prospect domain, run Website Overview and Traffic Visits in the relevant region.
2. Assign a score based on monthly visits and any visible growth trend.
3. Sort the prospects from highest to lowest score.

## Output
Return the prospect domains ranked by score, each with its estimated monthly visits, so the sales team can prioritize the biggest-traffic targets.

# Enrich Lead

1. Run Enrich Lead with whatever you know about the person: name, company, email, or LinkedIn.
2. Request only the fields you need to keep credit usage down.
3. Review the returned profile: title, seniority, company, and any social or contact data.

## Output
Return the enriched lead profile with the discovered role, company, and context, and note any fields the research could not resolve.

skills.name: find-contact-details
skills.description: Find a verified email or phone number for a prospect using Sixtyfour AI.
skills.content:
# Find Contact Details

Locate a reachable email or phone number for a prospect.

## Steps
1. Provide the person identity you have: name plus company or domain.
2. Run Find Email to discover a work email, or Find Phone for a phone number. Choose the professional or personal type as appropriate.
3. Validate that the result matches the intended person before using it.

## Output
Return the discovered email or phone number with its type, and clearly state if no verified contact could be found.

# Enrich Company

skills.name: daily-standup-summary
skills.description: Read a standup channel and post a structured recap of progress, plans, and blockers.
skills.content:
# Daily Standup Summary

Read the messages posted in the standup channel since the last working day and produce a concise team recap.

## Steps
1. Collect every standup update in the channel from the relevant window (skip bot and off-topic messages).
2. Group the content into three sections:
   - **Done** — what was completed.
   - **Today** — what each person plans to work on.
   - **Blockers** — anything waiting on someone else, with the owner @-mentioned.
3. Call out anyone who did not post an update.

## Output
Post a single threaded message with the three sections as bullet lists. Keep each bullet to one line. Lead with blockers if any exist so they are not missed.

skills.name: channel-catch-up
skills.description: Summarize what happened in a busy Slack channel so you can catch up fast.
skills.content:
# Channel Catch-Up

Summarize recent activity in a Slack channel for someone who has been away.

## Steps
1. Pull messages from the requested time range (default: since the user was last active, or the last 24 hours).
2. Cluster the conversation into topics or threads rather than listing messages chronologically.
3. For each topic, capture: the gist, any decision reached, and open questions still unanswered.

## Output
- A 1-sentence TL;DR.
- A bulleted list of topics, each with **Decision:** and **Open:** lines where relevant.
- A final "Needs your input" list of items where the user was @-mentioned or a question is unresolved.
Link to the source thread for each topic.

skills.name: slack-question-responder
skills.description: Watch a channel for questions and draft sourced, in-thread answers from your knowledge base.
skills.content:
# Slack Question Responder

Monitor a support or help channel and answer incoming questions.

## Steps
1. Detect when a message is a genuine question (ends in a question mark, asks "how/where/can someone", or is a help request).
2. Search the connected knowledge base for the answer.
3. If a confident answer exists, draft a concise reply in the thread with the answer and a citation/link to the source.
4. If no confident answer exists, do not guess — post a short note that a human should help, and @-mention the channel owner.

## Guidance
- Always reply in-thread, never in the main channel.
- Keep answers to 2–4 sentences plus the source link.
- Never fabricate links or policy.

skills.name: escalate-urgent-messages
skills.description: Scan a channel for urgent or at-risk messages and surface them to the right owner.
skills.content:
# Escalate Urgent Messages

Triage a channel for messages that need fast attention.

## Steps
1. Review recent messages and classify each as **Urgent**, **Today**, or **FYI** based on signals like "blocked", "down", "ASAP", customer impact, or an unanswered direct ask.
2. For Urgent items, identify the most likely owner from the channel topic or message context.
3. Skip resolved threads (those with a ✅ reaction or a clear answer).

## Output
Post a short escalation summary listing only Urgent and Today items: each as a one-line description, an @-mention of the owner, and a link to the message. If nothing is urgent, say so in one line.

skills.name: daily-football-fixtures

skills.content:
# Daily Football Fixtures

Get the football matches scheduled for a given day.

## Steps
1. Use Get Football Fixtures by Date with the target date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
2. Optionally set Includes to `participants;scores;league` to enrich each fixture.
3. Optionally set Filters such as `fixtureLeagues:501,271` to restrict to specific leagues.

## Output
A list of fixtures with kickoff time, the participating teams, and league.

skills.name: live-football-scores
skills.description: Fetch in-play football matches and their current scores from Sportmonks.
skills.content:
# Live Football Scores

See which matches are being played now and the live score.

## Steps
1. Use Get Inplay Football Scores to fetch matches in progress.
2. Set Includes to `participants;scores` for team names and the scoreline.
3. Optionally filter with `fixtureLeagues:501`.

## Output
A list of live fixtures, each with the two teams, current score, and match state.

skills.name: football-league-table
skills.description: Build a football league standings table for a season from Sportmonks.
skills.content:
# Football League Table

Get the current standings for a competition.

## Steps
1. Find the season ID (use Get Football Leagues, then its current season).
2. Use Get Football Standings by Season with that season ID.
3. Set Includes to `participant` for team names and `form` for recent results.

## Output
An ordered league table with each team's position, points, and recent form.

skills.name: race-weekend-sessions
skills.description: List the motorsport sessions on a given date from Sportmonks.
skills.content:
# Race Weekend Sessions

Get the practice, qualifying, and race sessions for a day.

## Steps
1. Use Get Motorsport Fixtures by Date with the target date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
2. Set Includes to `venue;participants` to attach the track and entrants.

## Output
A list of sessions for the day with type (Practice/Qualifying/Race), track, and start time.

skills.name: motorsport-championship

# Motorsport Championship

Get the title race state for a season.

## Steps

2. Use Get Motorsport Team Standings by Season with the same season ID.
3. Set Includes to `participant` for driver/team names.

## Output

skills.name: pre-match-odds
skills.description: Fetch pre-match odds for a fixture and compute implied probabilities.
skills.content:
# Pre-match Odds

Get the betting odds for an upcoming fixture.

## Steps
1. Use Get Pre-match Odds by Fixture with the fixture ID.
2. Set Includes to `market;bookmaker` and optionally Filters like `bookmakers:2,14` to narrow results.

## Output
The odds per outcome with decimal value and implied probability, grouped by market and bookmaker.

skills.name: odds-line-shopping
skills.description: Find the best available price per outcome across bookmakers.
skills.content:
# Odds Line Shopping

Find the best odds for each outcome.

## Steps
1. Use Get Pre-match Odds by Fixture for the fixture (do not filter to one bookmaker).
2. Group the returned odds by market and outcome label.
3. For each outcome, pick the highest value and note its bookmaker_id.

## Output
For each outcome, the best decimal price and which bookmaker offers it.

skills.name: resolve-country

skills.content:
# Resolve Country

Normalize a country name to Sportmonks reference data.

## Steps

2. Read the matching country id, iso2, iso3, and fifa_name.

## Output
The country id plus its ISO2, ISO3, and FIFA codes for use in other lookups.

skills.name: take-payment

skills.content:
# Take Payment

Charge a customer using Square.

## Steps
1. Run Create Payment with the source ID (card nonce or card on file), the amount in the smallest denomination, and the currency.
2. Optionally attach a customer ID, location ID, or order ID.
3. Confirm the result with Get Payment if you need the latest status.

## Output
Return the payment ID, status (APPROVED, COMPLETED, or FAILED), and the amount charged. If a refund is needed, run Refund Payment with the payment ID.

skills.name: issue-and-publish-invoice
skills.description: Create a Square invoice for an order and publish it to the customer.
skills.content:
# Issue And Publish Invoice

Bill a customer with a Square invoice.

## Steps
1. Make sure an order exists (use Create Order if needed) and you have the customer ID.
2. Run Create Invoice with an invoice object referencing the location, order, primary recipient (customer), and payment requests. Note the returned invoice ID and version.
3. Run Publish Invoice with that invoice ID and version to send it to the customer.
4. Track payment with Get Invoice.

## Output
Return the invoice ID, status, and the public URL where the customer can pay.

skills.name: manage-catalog-item
skills.description: Create or update a Square catalog item and attach an image to it.
skills.content:
# Manage Catalog Item

Build out the Square catalog.

## Steps
1. Run Upsert Catalog Object with an ITEM object (use a temporary id like "#Name" for new items). Capture the returned object ID.
2. To add a picture, run Create Catalog Image with the image file and the object ID to attach it to the item.
3. Verify with Get Catalog Object or Search Catalog Objects.

## Output
Return the catalog object ID, type, and version, plus the image object ID when an image was attached.

skills.name: find-customer-activity

# Extract Structured Data

Pull clean, structured data off a single web page.

## Steps
1. Run the Extract Data operation with the target URL.
2. Describe exactly what to extract and the shape you want (for example product name, price, and availability), so Stagehand returns typed fields rather than raw HTML.
3. Choose the LLM provider for the extraction.

## Output
Return the extracted fields as a structured object, and note any field the page did not contain so downstream steps can handle gaps.

skills.name: run-browser-agent-task
skills.description: Hand Stagehand a natural-language goal and let its agent navigate and act on a site autonomously.
skills.content:
# Run Browser Agent Task

Delegate a multi-step web task to the Stagehand agent.

## Steps
1. Run the Run Agent operation with a clear natural-language goal (for example find the latest pricing on a vendor site and capture it).
2. Provide the starting URL and pick the execution mode (DOM, hybrid, or CUA) and the LLM provider appropriate to the task.
3. Let the agent navigate, click, and read pages to complete the goal.

## Output
Return the agent result, the key data it captured, and any screenshots, plus a short note if the goal could not be fully completed.

skills.name: monitor-page-for-changes
skills.description: Periodically extract a value from a web page with Stagehand and report when it changes.
skills.content:
# Monitor Page for Changes

Watch a specific value on a web page over time.

## Steps
1. Run the Extract Data operation against the target URL, extracting just the value to watch (price, stock status, headline).
2. Compare the extracted value against the last known value stored from a previous run.
3. Decide whether the value changed beyond a meaningful threshold.

## Output
Report the current extracted value, whether it changed since the last check, and the old and new values when a change is detected.

# Collect Payment

Charge a customer by creating and confirming a payment intent.

## Steps
1. Run Create Payment Intent with the amount, currency, and customer.
2. Confirm the intent with Confirm Payment Intent, or Capture Payment Intent if it was created for manual capture.
3. If a charge needs to be aborted, run Cancel Payment Intent instead.

## Output
Return the payment intent ID, its status (succeeded, requires action, or canceled), and the captured amount.

skills.name: manage-subscription
skills.description: Create, update, pause, or cancel a Stripe subscription for a customer.
skills.content:
# Manage Subscription

Handle the lifecycle of a recurring subscription.

## Steps
1. To start a subscription, run Create Subscription with the customer and price items.
2. To change a plan, run Update Subscription with the new items. To pause and later restart, use Cancel Subscription or Resume Subscription as appropriate.
3. Confirm the current state with Retrieve Subscription.

## Output
Return the subscription ID, its status, current period end, and the plan items, and note exactly what changed.

skills.name: issue-invoice
skills.description: Create, finalize, and send a Stripe invoice to a customer, then track payment.
skills.content:
# Issue Invoice

Bill a customer with a Stripe invoice.

## Steps
1. Run Create Invoice for the customer with the line items.
2. Run Finalize Invoice to lock it, then Send Invoice to deliver it to the customer.
3. Track payment with Retrieve Invoice, or run Pay Invoice to charge a saved payment method. Use Void Invoice to cancel an unpaid invoice.

## Output
Return the invoice ID, its status (draft, open, paid, or void), the amount due, and the hosted invoice URL when available.

# Query Supabase Table Rows

Fetch records from a Supabase table using PostgREST filters so downstream steps work with exactly the rows they need.

## Steps
1. Use the Get Many Rows operation with the project ID, service role secret, and target table.
2. Set Select Columns to the fields you need (for example id,name,email) instead of returning every column.
3. Add a PostgREST Filter such as status=eq.active or created_at=gte.2024-01-01 to narrow the result set.
4. Set Order By (for example created_at DESC) plus Limit and Offset for predictable pagination.
5. For a single record use Get a Row with a filter like id=eq.123.

## Output
Return the matched rows as structured JSON. Note how many rows came back and surface the key fields each consumer needs.

skills.name: upsert-record
skills.description: Insert a new Supabase row or update it if it already exists in one idempotent call.
skills.content:
# Upsert a Supabase Record

Write a record without first checking whether it exists, so repeated runs stay idempotent.

## Steps
1. Choose the Upsert a Row operation with the project ID, service role secret, and table.
2. Provide the Data as a JSON object whose keys match the table columns, including the conflict key (such as id or email).
3. Supabase inserts the row when the conflict key is new and updates the existing row otherwise.
4. For a guaranteed new row use Create a Row instead; for a known existing row use Update a Row with a filter like id=eq.123.

## Output
Confirm whether the row was inserted or updated and report the resulting record fields back to the caller.

skills.name: semantic-vector-search
skills.description: Run pgvector similarity search against a Supabase table to retrieve the closest embeddings.
skills.content:
# Semantic Vector Search in Supabase

Find the most relevant rows by embedding similarity, the retrieval step for a RAG agent.

## Steps
1. Generate an embedding for the query text with your model and capture it as a numeric array.
2. Use the Vector Search operation, pointing Function Name at your pgvector match function (for example match_documents).
3. Pass the embedding into Query Embedding as a JSON array like [0.1, 0.2, 0.3].
4. Tune Match Threshold (for example 0.78) and Match Count (for example 10) to balance precision and recall.

## Output
Return the matched rows with their similarity scores, ordered by closeness, ready to feed an answer-generation step.

skills.name: upload-file-to-storage
skills.description: Upload a file to a Supabase Storage bucket and return a public or signed URL.
skills.content:
# Upload a File to Supabase Storage

Store a generated or received file in a bucket and hand back a shareable link.

## Steps
1. Use Storage: Upload File with the bucket name, file name, and the file reference from a previous block.
2. Set an optional Folder Path and Content Type, and enable Upsert if you want to overwrite an existing object.
3. For a permanent link on a public bucket use Storage: Get Public URL with the file path.
4. For private buckets use Storage: Create Signed URL with an Expires In value such as 3600 seconds.

## Output
Return the stored object path plus the public or signed URL so later steps can reference or share the file.

skills.name: invoke-edge-function
skills.description: Call a deployed Supabase Edge Function over HTTP and use its JSON response.
skills.content:
# Invoke a Supabase Edge Function

Run server-side logic deployed as a Supabase Edge Function and feed its result into the workflow.

## Steps
1. Use the Invoke Edge Function operation with the project ID, service role secret, and the function name (for example hello-world).
2. Choose the HTTP Method (defaults to POST) and provide a JSON Request Body the function expects.
3. Add optional custom Headers as a JSON object when the function reads specific headers.
4. This is different from Call RPC Function, which runs a PostgreSQL function inside the database rather than deployed function code.

## Output
Return the function response body as JSON so downstream steps can branch on or transform the result.

templates.title: Tailscale device inventory

templates.title: Tailscale key-expiry sweeper

templates.title: Tailscale access audit

skills.name: audit-tailnet-devices
skills.description: List every device in the tailnet and flag stale, unauthorized, or update-pending nodes.
skills.content:
# Audit Tailnet Devices

Produce a clean inventory of the devices on your tailnet and surface the ones that need attention.

## Steps
1. Use the List Devices operation with your API key and tailnet (use "-" for the default tailnet).
2. For each device review lastSeen, authorized, updateAvailable, and the assigned tags.
3. Flag nodes not seen in 30+ days, devices still pending authorization, and any with an update available.
4. Use Get Device with a deviceId to pull full detail on anything suspicious.

## Output
Return a table of devices with hostname, user, OS, last seen, and authorization status, plus a short list of nodes that need review.

skills.name: provision-auth-key
skills.description: Create a scoped Tailscale auth key with the right tags, reusability, and expiry for onboarding.
skills.content:
# Provision a Tailscale Auth Key

Generate an auth key so a new device or user can join the tailnet with the correct access.

## Steps
1. Use the Create Auth Key operation with your API key and tailnet.
2. Set Tags (for example tag:server,tag:production) so devices joining with the key get the intended ACL access.
3. Choose Reusable, Ephemeral, and Preauthorized values to match the use case (ephemeral for short-lived CI nodes).
4. Set an Expiry in seconds (for example 7776000 for 90 days) and a clear Description.

## Output
Return the generated key value once (it is only shown at creation), the key ID, its tags, and the expiry timestamp.

skills.name: offboard-device
skills.description: Deauthorize or remove a departing user device and revoke its auth keys.
skills.content:
# Offboard a Tailscale Device

Remove a device from the tailnet during offboarding so access is cut cleanly.

## Steps
1. Use List Devices to find the deviceId tied to the departing user.
2. To immediately cut access use Authorize Device set to Deauthorize, or Delete Device to remove it entirely.
3. Use List Auth Keys to find any keys the user created, then Delete Auth Key for each.
4. Capture the device detail with Get Device before deletion if you need an audit record.

## Output
Confirm the device was deauthorized or deleted and list the revoked auth keys for the offboarding audit log.

templates.title: Multi-source research agent

templates.title: Tavily research-augmented agent

templates.title: Tavily URL content extractor

skills.name: answer-with-web-citations
skills.description: Search the web with Tavily and return a grounded answer with linked source citations.
skills.content:
# Answer a Question with Web Citations

Ground an answer in fresh web results so it is current and verifiable.

## Steps
1. Use the Search operation with the question as the Search Query.
2. Set Include Answer to Advanced, Search Depth to advanced, and Max Results to about 5 for good coverage.
3. Pick the Topic (news or finance) when the question is time-sensitive, and set Time Range (day, week, month) to keep results recent.
4. Use Include Domains or Exclude Domains to keep results on trusted sources.

## Output
Return the synthesized answer followed by a numbered list of the source titles and URLs used to support it.

skills.name: extract-article-content
skills.description: Pull clean main content from one or more URLs with Tavily Extract for summarization.
skills.content:
# Extract Clean Article Content

Turn a messy web page into clean text or markdown that an agent can summarize.

## Steps
1. Use the Extract Content operation and pass the page URL into the URL field.
2. Set Extract Depth to advanced for content-heavy pages and choose Markdown or Text as the Format.
3. Enable Include Images only if downstream steps need the media.
4. Feed the extracted content to an agent to summarize the key points.

## Output
Return the page title, source URL, and the cleaned content, plus any failed URLs so they can be retried.

skills.name: crawl-site-section
skills.description: Crawl a website section with Tavily and gather page content matching path rules.
skills.content:
# Crawl a Website Section

Walk a site beginning at a root URL and collect content from matching pages.

## Steps
1. Use the Crawl Website operation with the root Website URL.
2. Give natural-language Instructions describing what to collect (for example "gather all product documentation pages").
3. Bound the crawl with Max Depth, Max Breadth, and Limit so it stays focused.
4. Use Select Paths and Exclude Paths regex patterns (for example /docs/.* to include, /admin/.* to exclude) to target the right section.

## Output
Return the crawled pages with their URLs and extracted content, ready to index into a knowledge base or summarize.

skills.name: map-site-structure
skills.description: Map a website URL structure with Tavily without extracting full page content.
skills.content:
# Map a Website Structure

Discover the URL layout of a site quickly without pulling full page bodies.

## Steps
1. Use the Map Website operation with the root Website URL.
2. Set Max Depth and Max Breadth to control how far the mapper explores.
3. Apply Select Paths or Exclude Paths regex patterns to focus on the sections you care about.
4. Toggle Allow External Links only if you want links that leave the root domain.

## Output
Return the discovered list of URLs so you can pick targets for a later crawl or extract pass.

templates.title: Telegram alert relay

skills.name: send-alert-message
skills.description: Post a formatted alert or notification to a Telegram chat or channel.
skills.content:
# Send a Telegram Alert

Deliver a timely notification to a Telegram chat, group, or channel.

## Steps
1. Use the Send Message operation with your Bot Token and the target Chat ID.
2. Compose the Message with the essentials up front: what happened, severity, and a link for follow-up.
3. To find a Chat ID, add the bot to the chat, send a message, then read the chat field from the getUpdates response.
4. For recurring alerts, build the message from upstream block outputs so each notification carries live context.

## Output
Return the sent message ID and chat ID so the run can be traced or the message later deleted.

skills.name: send-media-message
skills.description: Send a photo, video, document, or audio file to a Telegram chat with a caption.
skills.content:
# Send Media to Telegram

Deliver a file such as a chart, report, or image to a Telegram chat.

## Steps
1. Pick the matching operation: Send Photo, Send Video, Send Audio, Send Animation, or Send Document.
2. Provide the Bot Token and Chat ID.
3. Upload the file directly, or reference a file produced by a previous block (for example a generated PDF or chart image).
4. Add an optional Caption describing the attachment.

## Output
Confirm delivery and return the message ID so the media post can be referenced later.

skills.name: route-incoming-message
skills.description: Trigger a workflow when a Telegram message arrives and act on its content.
skills.content:
# Route an Incoming Telegram Message

Use Telegram as a trigger so the workflow runs whenever a user messages the bot.

## Steps
1. Enable the Telegram webhook trigger so incoming messages start the workflow.
2. Read the trigger outputs: text, from_username, chat_id, and chat_type.
3. Branch on the message content (for example detect a command or a support question) to decide the next action.
4. Reply with the Send Message operation using the chat_id from the trigger.

## Output
Return the parsed incoming message fields and confirm the reply that was sent back to the user.

templates.title: Temporal order approval gate

templates.title: Temporal runaway workflow janitor

skills.name: start-workflow-execution
skills.description: Start a Temporal workflow execution with the right input and report the workflow and run IDs.
skills.content:
# Start a Temporal Workflow

Kick off a workflow execution on the cluster.

## Steps
1. Confirm the workflow type, task queue, and a unique workflow ID.
2. Assemble the JSON input arguments for the workflow.
3. Start the workflow and capture the run ID.
4. Describe the execution to confirm it is running.

## Output
A confirmation with the workflow ID, run ID, and initial status.

skills.name: investigate-failed-workflow
skills.description: Describe a failed Temporal workflow and pull its close event to explain why it failed.
skills.content:
# Investigate a Failed Temporal Workflow

Diagnose a workflow failure.

## Steps
1. Describe the workflow to confirm its status and timing.
2. Fetch the history filtered to the close event to get the failure details.
3. If needed, fetch earlier history pages to trace the failing activity.
4. Summarize the root cause.

## Output
A failure summary with the failing event, error message, and a recommendation.

skills.name: signal-running-workflow
skills.description: Send a signal to a running Temporal workflow and confirm it was delivered.
skills.content:
# Signal a Temporal Workflow

Deliver data or a decision to a running execution.

## Steps
1. Find the target execution by workflow ID (or list executions to locate it).
2. Send the signal with the JSON payload.
3. Query or describe the workflow to confirm the signal took effect.

## Output
A confirmation with the workflow ID, signal name, and resulting state.

skills.name: audit-running-workflows
skills.description: List running Temporal executions and surface long-running or stuck workflows.
skills.content:
# Audit Running Temporal Workflows

Find executions that need attention.

## Steps
1. List executions filtered to ExecutionStatus = "Running".
2. Sort by start time and flag the longest-running executions.
3. Describe flagged executions to inspect pending activities and retry counts.
4. Recommend cancellation or escalation for stuck workflows.

## Output
A per-workflow report with age, pending activities, and a recommended action.

skills.name: ingest-events
skills.description: Stream JSON or NDJSON events into a Tinybird Data Source via the Events API.
skills.content:
# Ingest Events into Tinybird

Stream realtime events into a Data Source so they are queryable within seconds.

## Steps
1. Use the Send Events operation with your Base URL and API Token.
2. Set the Data Source name that matches your target table.
3. Provide the events in the Data field, using NDJSON (one JSON object per line) for batches or JSON for a single object.
4. Enable Wait for Acknowledgment when you need confirmation the rows landed before continuing.

## Output
Return the count of successful_rows and quarantined_rows so you can confirm ingestion and catch rows that failed validation.

skills.name: query-pipe-endpoint
skills.description: Call a published Tinybird Pipe API Endpoint with dynamic parameters and return the result.
skills.content:
# Query a Tinybird Pipe Endpoint

Call a published Pipe by name to get analytics results shaped by dynamic parameters.

## Steps
1. Use the Query Pipe Endpoint operation with the Base URL, API Token, and the Pipe Name (for example top_pages).
2. Pass dynamic Parameters as a JSON object whose keys match the parameters the Pipe expects (for example start_date and limit).
3. Optionally add SQL on top of the Pipe result using the advanced SQL field, selecting from _ to post-process.

## Output
Return the result rows as JSON along with the column metadata and row count, ready to write to a table or summarize.

skills.name: run-sql-query
skills.description: Run an ad-hoc SQL query against Tinybird with the Query API and return results.
skills.content:
# Run a Tinybird SQL Query

Execute SQL directly against your Tinybird data for ad-hoc analysis.

## Steps
1. Use the Query operation with the Base URL and API Token.
2. Write the SQL Query and append FORMAT JSON to get structured rows back (other formats return raw text).
3. Reference Data Sources or Pipes by name in the FROM clause.

## Output
Return the result data as an array of objects plus the column metadata, row count, and execution statistics.

skills.name: manage-datasource-rows
skills.description: Append from a URL, truncate, or delete rows by condition in a Tinybird Data Source.
skills.content:
# Manage Tinybird Data Source Rows

Maintain a Data Source by loading, clearing, or pruning its rows.

## Steps
1. To load data, use Append Data Source (from URL) with the Data Source name, a Source File URL, and the source format (CSV, NDJSON, or Parquet).
2. To clear everything, use Truncate Data Source with the Data Source name.
3. To remove specific rows, use Delete Data Source Rows with a SQL Delete Condition such as event_date < '2024-01-01'.
4. Enable Dry Run on a delete first to preview how many rows would be removed.

## Output
Return the job ID and status for append and delete operations so you can poll for completion, or confirm the truncate succeeded.

templates.title: Trello stale-card sweeper

skills.name: create-card
skills.description: Create a Trello card in a list with a description, due date, and labels.
skills.content:
# Create a Trello Card

Add a new card to a list so work is captured on the right board.

## Steps
1. Use the Create Card operation and select your Trello account.
2. Provide the List ID where the card should land and the Card Name.
3. Add an optional Description, a Due Date (natural language like "next Friday" works), and Label IDs.
4. Set Position to top or bottom to control where the card appears in the list.

## Output
Return the created card including its id, url, and list, so it can be linked or updated later.

skills.name: triage-and-move-cards
skills.description: List cards on a board or list, classify them, and move each to the correct list.
skills.content:
# Triage and Route Trello Cards

Read incoming cards, decide where each belongs, and route them automatically.

## Steps
1. Use Get Lists with the Board ID to learn the available lists and their IDs.
2. Use List Cards with the board or list ID to pull the cards needing triage.
3. Classify each card by its name and description (topic, priority, owner).
4. Use Update Card with the Move to List ID to route each card to its destination list.

## Output
Return a summary of how many cards were moved and the destination list for each.

skills.name: comment-on-card
skills.description: Add a comment to a Trello card to leave a note, nudge, or status update.
skills.content:
# Comment on a Trello Card

Leave a comment on a card to record context or nudge an owner.

## Steps
1. Use the Add Comment operation and select your Trello account.
2. Provide the Card ID of the target card.
3. Write the Comment text, including any links or mentions the team needs.

## Output
Return the created comment action with its id and date so the note can be referenced.

skills.name: review-card-activity
skills.description: Pull the recent action history for a Trello board or card and summarize it.
skills.content:
# Review Trello Card Activity

Inspect what has happened recently on a board or card to build a digest or audit.

## Steps
1. Use the Get Actions operation with either a Board ID or a Card ID (one or the other, not both).
2. Set an Action Filter such as commentCard,updateCard,createCard to focus on the events you care about.
3. Use Board Action Limit and Action Page to page through longer histories.

## Output
Return the actions with their type, date, author, and text, summarized into a short activity recap.

skills.name: trigger-task-and-wait
skills.description: Trigger a Trigger.dev background task with a payload and poll until the run completes, returning its output.
skills.content:
# Trigger Task and Wait

Kick off a Trigger.dev background task and collect its result.

## Steps
1. Use the Trigger Task operation with the task identifier and a JSON payload. Set an idempotency key when the same event might arrive twice.
2. Poll the Get Run operation with the returned run ID until the status is COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, CRASHED, or another terminal state.
3. On COMPLETED, read the run output. On failure states, read the attempts to surface the error message.

## Output
Return the run ID, final status, duration, and the run output — or the error details if the run did not complete.

skills.name: monitor-failed-runs
skills.description: List recent failed Trigger.dev runs, group them by task, and produce a failure digest. Use for run health monitoring.
skills.content:
# Monitor Failed Runs

Review recent Trigger.dev failures and summarize what needs attention.

## Steps
1. Use the List Runs operation with a status filter of FAILED, CRASHED, SYSTEM_FAILURE and a created-within period (e.g., 1h or 1d).
2. Group the runs by task identifier and count failures per task.
3. For the most affected tasks, fetch a representative run with Get Run and pull the attempt error message.

## Output
Report failures per task with counts, representative error messages, and run IDs. If nothing failed, say so briefly.

skills.name: replay-transient-failures
skills.description: Inspect failed Trigger.dev runs and replay the ones whose errors look transient (timeouts, rate limits, network).
skills.content:
# Replay Transient Failures

Retry failed Trigger.dev runs that are safe to run again.

## Steps
1. List runs with status FAILED for the relevant period and task filter.
2. For each run, use Get Run and inspect the attempt errors. Treat timeouts, rate limits, and network errors as transient; treat validation and logic errors as permanent.
3. Use the Replay Run operation on transient failures only, and record the new run IDs.

## Output
List the replayed runs (old run ID to new run ID) and the runs skipped as permanent failures, with the reason for each decision.

skills.name: human-approval-waitpoint
skills.description: Create a Trigger.dev waitpoint token for a task to wait on, then complete it with approval data once a human decides.
skills.content:
# Human Approval Waitpoint

Gate a Trigger.dev task on an external decision using waitpoint tokens.

## Steps
1. Use Create Waitpoint Token with a timeout (e.g., 1d) and an idempotency key tied to the request, and pass the token ID to the task that should wait.
2. When the decision arrives, use Complete Waitpoint Token with the token ID and a JSON payload like {"status": "approved"} so the waiting run resumes with that data.
3. Use Get Waitpoint Token or List Waitpoint Tokens to check for tokens that are still WAITING or have TIMED_OUT.

## Output
Report the token ID, its status, and the completion data passed to the run. Flag tokens that timed out without a decision.

skills.name: manage-cron-schedules
skills.description: Create, update, activate, deactivate, or delete Trigger.dev cron schedules for a task, scoped by external ID.
skills.content:
# Manage Cron Schedules

Keep Trigger.dev schedules in sync with the desired cadence.

## Steps
1. Use List Schedules to find existing schedules for the task, matching on external ID when schedules are per customer or per resource.
2. Create a schedule with the task identifier, cron expression, timezone, and a deduplication key so reruns do not create duplicates.
3. Update the cron or timezone on an existing schedule by ID, and use Activate or Deactivate to pause and resume without deleting.
4. Delete schedules that are no longer needed.

## Output
Report the schedule ID, task, cron expression, timezone, active state, and next run time after the change.

templates.title: SMS appointment reminders
templates.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow that checks Google Calendar each morning for appointments in the next 24 hours, and sends an SMS reminder to each attendee via Twilio with the meeting time, location, and any prep notes.

templates.title: Twilio appointment reminders
templates.prompt: Build a scheduled workflow that reads tomorrow’s appointments from a table and sends each customer a personalized Twilio SMS reminder with the time and a reschedule link.

templates.title: Twilio order-status notifier

templates.title: Twilio payment-failure outreach

templates.title: Twilio daily standup nudge
